544439|2026-03.headline: Crizac FY26 revenue rose 22.7% to INR 10,422 mn and Q4 PAT rose 50% to INR 750 mn, but management withheld FY27 guidance until next quarter.
544439|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue from operations was INR 3,917 mn (up 15% YoY, up 40.6% QoQ) and FY26 EBITDA reached about INR 2,824 mn with margin up 172 bps to 27%. Q4 EBITDA grew 42.8% YoY to INR 939 mn, with margin at 24%, and management attributed part of the Q4 margin jump to favourable GBP/INR movement it called transitional. Management completed or operationalised four acquisitions/investments (StudiesPlanet, 51% of Global Tree Careers, EduMentor commitment, Medway NZ team) and the company remains debt-free with net cash of INR 4,674 mn. FY27 guidance was deferred to the next quarter citing geopolitical uncertainty, with management saying growth should be in line with the past trend and a full-year growth of 15% to 17% noted in Q&A.

financial_highlights.change: Affected by termination fee of about INR 55 crore

segments.name: Source markets (applications and conversion)
segments.commentary: Applications grew 43% YoY to about 394,000 and active agents rose 36% to 5,389; blended conversion about 14%, with India about 10%, China and LatAm about 20%, and Africa about 5%. Non-India source countries now contribute more than 50% of students.

segments.name: Destination markets
segments.commentary: UK is about 97% of destination mix per Q&A; management targets UK below 60% and rest of world about 40% in roughly two to three years, dependent on government policy. New Zealand was operationalised in April 2026 via the Medway team; Australia contracts are starting and recruitment expected within 3 to 6 months.

segments.name: Enrolments
segments.commentary: Student enrolments grew 14% YoY in FY26; management said it has grown 10% to 20% annually and expects similar or higher growth going forward.

guidance_outlook: No firm FY27 revenue guidance; management will issue guidance in the next quarter once geopolitical visibility improves.

Management said FY27 growth should be in line with the historical year-on-year rate; in Q&A the CFO said full-year growth of 15% to 17% is expected, and an analyst cited a 15% to 20% growth figure from earlier in the call.
Gross margin for the business to stay in a 20% to 30% range; analyst-cited FY27 gross margin of 28% to 30% was not explicitly rejected, and EBITDA margin guidance was withheld.
Visibility is roughly 6 to 9 months; management expects FY27 seasonality to match FY26, with H2 higher than H1.
Dividend payout of about 64% in Q4 FY26 is above the earlier committed 40%; management said it would consider buybacks versus dividends.
Australia recruitment expected to start within 3 to 6 months; management says 40% non-UK share is a three-year aspiration subject to immigration rules.
capex_capacity: Four transactions in FY26: StudiesPlanet acquisition (completed October 2025, opens LATAM corridor), 51% stake in Global Tree Careers (January 2026, B2C counselling and immigration), USD 2.5 mn over five years committed to EduMentor AI platform (March 2026), and onboarding of the Medway Educational Consultant team for New Zealand (April 2026).
Inorganic pipeline described as active across existing and new geographies; no specific deal values were disclosed for pipeline.
Company is asset-light; ROCE of 48.6% cited, and management said cash generation exceeds growth investment needs.
Over 300 US universities tied up per management, with Australia and Canada opening dependent on government policy.
demand_pricing: Management attributes the enrolment gap versus application growth to mix shift across markets with differing conversion rates.
Middle East pipeline damaged by the West Asia conflict; management expects it to recover as the war subsides.
US visa appointments limited; management ranks Australia ahead of the US as the next growth driver.
Pricing power argued to rise as UK Agent Quality Framework and Australian national codes raise compliance barriers; universities expected to consolidate suppliers.

FX: GBP/INR averaged 116 in FY26 vs 105 in FY25; management said 67% to 70% of expenses (agent commissions) are paid in GBP directly to agents, so FX impact is mainly on the portion repatriated to India.
Management quantified the FX-led benefit to EBITDA/gross margin at roughly 1% to 1.5%.

qa_highlights.answer: Not quantifiable on an agent-by-agent basis; active agents grew from about 4,000 to 5,500 and no agents were lost.

qa_highlights.answer: Growth has been 10% to 20% a year; management expects similar or higher going forward, with FY26 at 14%.

qa_highlights.answer: Management deferred firm guidance to next quarter; full-year growth expected at 15% to 17%, and a 15% to 20% figure was referenced by an analyst.

qa_highlights.question: FY27 gross and EBITDA margins on a normalised basis?
qa_highlights.answer: Gross margin said to stay in the 20% to 30% range; analyst-quoted 28% to 30% for FY27 not rejected. EBITDA guidance withheld until growth guidance is given.

qa_highlights.answer: Promoter holding about 80% with two more years to reach the 75% SEBI threshold; management open to buybacks as a shareholder-value option.

544439|2026-06.headline: Crizac Q1 FY27 revenue fell 4% YoY to INR2,012 million on adverse university mix; management now guides FY27 flat versus FY26.
544439|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations was INR2,012 million, down 4% YoY and below the INR3,917 million of Q4 FY26, consistent with Q1 being the seasonal trough. Management attributed the decline to a less favourable university mix (fewer high-fee top-ranked university bonuses and slabs), not lower platform activity, as enrolments rose 15% YoY. EBITDA fell 7.6% YoY to INR600 million, with margin at 29.8% versus 31%, while PAT grew 2.9% to INR471 million. Management moved from earlier growth expectations to a flat FY27 outlook, citing flight disruption and rupee volatility expected to hit Q2, with pent-up demand expected in Q3 and Q4. It also announced a leadership change: Chairman Christopher Nagle stepped down as UK CEO and became Non-Executive Chairman of the Indian holding company, with Eric Wijmenga taking UK and Europe operations.

Recent deals also include Studies Planet (Latin America), Global Tree (India), Medway (New Zealand) and EduMentor (talent acquisition).

Visa and currency pressure: UK graduate route cut from 24 to 18 months; US/UK strength in currency raising costs for emerging-market students; demand redirecting to Ireland, Germany and New Zealand per management.

qa_highlights.question: Why did revenue fall QoQ and what is the Q2 outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Constant-currency revenue fell about 4% as volume rose 15% but university mix shifted; Q2 expected weaker due to Feb-June flight cancellations and rupee volatility.

qa_highlights.question: Will FY27 growth be 20-25% or 15-17% as earlier hinted?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Management now expects FY27 flat versus FY26, with pent-up demand in Q3 and Q4 offsetting Q1 and Q2 shortfalls.

qa_highlights.question: Why is standalone PBT above consolidated PBT in Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Crizac India standalone recognised some payments as revenue; investments in Crizac UK and subsidiaries should pay off in Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a buyback plan given the stock trades around 11x EBITDA?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the company has only about 20% public float and SEBI rules do not allow a buyback at this level; the compliance team will look at the suggestion.

qa_highlights.question: Will the UK concentration fall, and what is the target?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, the target is to get UK share below 60% within about three years, aided by Innova (Netherlands) and other markets, though policy shifts will slow this.

qa_highlights.question: Will value-added services become material?
qa_highlights.answer: Not initially; they could add 2-5% to EBITDA and 1-1.5% of revenue over the next couple of years, with ForeignAdmits accelerating this.

qa_highlights.question: Is the dividend a one-time payout?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Management said the DRHP commits to a minimum 40% of PAT as dividend for at least three years; FY26 is done, leaving at least two more years.

544439|2026-09.headline: Crizac Q2 FY27 operating income fell 36.7% YoY to INR 1,027 million; management guides FY27 revenue and profit in line with FY26 on deferred students.
544439|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 was hit by the West Asia conflict, currency moves in a key source market, and post-grad students deferring intakes. Operating income was INR 1,027 million (down 36.7% YoY), operating EBITDA INR 330 million (down 44%), and PAT INR 369 million (down 23.7%). Management attributes the shortfall to timing, saying revenue is deferred rather than lost, with Q3 FY27 revenue guided up 10-12% YoY and FY27 revenue and profit guided in line with FY26. An interim dividend of INR 4 per share was declared, and the company reported net cash of about INR 5,984 million.

segments.name: UK (anchor market)
segments.commentary: Management says UK-sponsored study visas fell 20% between FY24 and FY26 while Crizac students grew 53%. Three universities accounted for 44% of revenue. The UK budget of 28 October proposed a 2-year graduate visa for high-compliance universities versus 18 months for others from January 2027; qualifying universities are yet to be defined.

segments.name: Non-UK destinations
segments.commentary: Non-UK destinations were about 9.5% of H1 applications versus 4.7% in H1 FY26, but contributed only 1.4% of revenue as of today. Management targets 30% of revenue from outside the UK by FY30.

guidance_outlook: Q3 FY27 revenue expected to grow 10-12% YoY over Q3 FY26, based on students who already have admission and visa in place.
FY27 revenue and profit guided in line with FY26, barring any black swan event; management says a large share of Q4 applications is already received and being processed.
Interim dividend INR 4 per share declared; total FY27 dividend including final expected at INR 8-10 per share.
Steady-state EBITDA margin guided at 25-26%, same as last year; salary cost expected at 3-4% of revenue in the medium to long term.
No FY28 guidance yet; management says it will be in a better position to guide next quarter. FY28 is subject to market reaction and US mid-term election outcomes.
Acquisitions: targets EBITDA-accretive deals with a 10-20% return, depending on geography; M&A pipeline described as active but cautious.
capex_capacity: Over 600 institutional partners; relationships with the top 30 partners exceed 5 years.
Counselling partner network of more than 18,500, of which 4,942 were active in H1.
Platform processed over 2 lakh applications from 92 countries; enrolment rate 12.8% on a rolling 12-month basis.
USD 2.5 million committed in March 2026 to in-house development of EduMentor, an AI-led student-university matching and mentorship platform.
Asset-light model: accommodation and student loans are distributed as a DSA for third parties; no real estate acquisition planned.
Medway Education (New Zealand) acquired at the start of FY27; New Zealand main intake is February, so revenue lands in Q4.
demand_pricing: Applications fell about 3% YoY in Q2, but revenue fell about 37%. Management attributes the gap to deferral timing, not lower revenue per student or mix.
Market share rose from 3.5% to 6% globally (FY24 to FY26). Share of Indian students rose from 9% to 13.9%, while visas to Indian students fell 22% over the same period.
Share of ex-India students rose from 1.5% to 3.7%.
Students deferred to the November and January intakes. Management says the Q2 shortfall should be recovered in Q3 and Q4.
Gross margin was about 54% in Q2 versus about 70% last year. Management says this reflects the H1 mix: 30% retained and 70% paid to the accounting partner, with full-year margin expected at 65-70%.
Management believes AI will not remove agents: universities still need counsellors for visa and process support, and inter-university competition favours platforms.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the Q2 revenue gap came from post-August deferrals, and what gives confidence deferrals will convert rather than cancel?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not quantify deferrals by student count, since they span September, November and January intakes. It cited pipeline evidence (applications, deposits, visas) supporting 10-12% Q3 growth, and said many students have deferred to the January intake.

qa_highlights.question: Is the applications-to-revenue gap purely timing?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes. Management said it was mainly students deferring, all timing-related, with no change in revenue per student.

qa_highlights.question: Will FY27 M&A or capital deployment be pursued given the cash balance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is actively looking at M&A but is cautious given geopolitical uncertainty. Criteria include synergies, founders, source and destination jurisdictions, revenue and EBITDA; the target is EBITDA-accretive at 10-20%.

qa_highlights.question: Why did standalone results hold up while consolidated results fell, and was the INR 57 crore termination fee one-off?
qa_highlights.answer: Standalone India books revenue on application processing, ahead of UK subsidiaries, which book on enrolment. The termination fee to Crizac Informatics UK (INR 57 crore vs INR 21.5 crore in FY25) was a one-time item that will not recur in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for employee cost and EBITDA margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Employee cost is largely fixed and rose with acquisitions and tech hiring. Salary cost is expected at 3-4% of revenue in the medium to long term, and steady-state EBITDA margin is 25-26%.

qa_highlights.question: Can the company diversify away from the UK, and when will non-UK revenue reach 10%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management gave no date for 10% non-UK revenue. It expects 30% of revenue from outside the UK by FY30, citing New Zealand (via Medway), Netherlands, Europe and expected openings in Australia, Canada and the US.

risks_watch: Revenue is heavily concentrated: 44% of revenue came from three universities, and the UK is the dominant destination.
Q3 (+10-12% YoY) and FY27 (flat YoY) guidance depends on deferred students converting in Q3-Q4 and on the Q4 application pipeline. The company did not quantify the deferred student count.
US revenue is constrained by visa appointment limits; the Raj Consultants US presence has not scaled.

Buyback as a promoter tax-efficient route is blocked until the promoter holding falls below 75% (MPC compliance, about 3 years to achieve).

544441|2026-03.headline: Meta Infotech FY26 revenue rose 23% to INR270 crore but PAT fell to INR11 crore; management targets 4x PAT by FY29 with no numeric guidance.
544441|2026-03.overview: FY26 was described as an investment year: revenue grew 23% YoY to INR270 crore and H2 revenue grew 72% YoY to INR60 crore, but EBITDA fell to INR18 crore (FY25: INR25 crore) and PAT fell to INR11 crore (FY25: INR14 crore). Management attributed the squeeze to new hires, geographic expansion, 12 new vendor onboardings, a Thales-owned Imperva transition that cut professional services revenue from about INR8.5 crore to INR2 crore, and a forex loss on a large contract. The company set an aspirational target of up to 4x PAT by FY29 from FY26 levels, without numeric revenue or margin guidance. Order book stood at INR506 crore as of May 2026, about 1.9x FY26 revenue.

segments.name: Services
segments.commentary: FY26 services revenue was about INR36 crore versus INR35 crore in FY25, roughly 13% of total revenue; services contributed 75% of FY26 EBIT. Management targets at least 25% growth in services revenue in FY27.

segments.name: Product / trading
segments.commentary: Product business, including the large low-margin deal, carried H2 product EBIT loss versus about 8.2% product EBIT margin in H1 per an analyst's reading; management said it will decline product deals below 5-6% margin and target 9-10% going forward.

guidance_outlook: Aspirational target to grow PAT up to 4x from FY26 levels by FY29, described as a three-year plan starting FY27; no revenue or margin numbers given on compliance grounds.
PAT margin to rise above 10% from about 4% currently; management said ex the large low-margin order, PAT margin would already exceed 10%.
Services mix expected to rise from about 13% toward 25-30% of revenue over three years.
Imperva/Thales professional services expected at about INR10 crore in FY27 (INR6-7 crore Imperva, about INR3 crore Thales).
Headcount expected at 350-375 by March 2027; intends to add about 50 engineers per year.
Contracts to be signed on a Spot+2 forex basis going forward to avoid INR-price variability.
capex_capacity: Headcount rose from 265 (Mar-25) to 309 (Mar-26); share of core technical staff increased from about 50% to 90%.
Added around 40-45 people during the year, mostly engineers and mid-senior staff, plus six senior hires with 17-33 years' experience.
Offices now in Mumbai, Delhi, Bangalore, Chennai and Hyderabad; Pune expected in one to two months.
In-house paid training centres in Mumbai and Hyderabad (three-month programme) feed fresh hires; Jetking tie-up used for three-year-bond resources.
Dubai: three projects running, one a three-year contract; Gulf, Australia, APAC and US expansion planned.
demand_pricing: Order book INR506 crore as of May 2026 (about 1.9x FY26 revenue), management said to execute over about three years.
Large single contract above INR100 crore (vendor Zscaler) is recognised mainly in H1; management said it would not have taken this order at its margin given a choice, and it dilutes PAT margin.
Largest customer, a private bank, was about 50-55% of FY26 revenue per management; other customers mostly below INR10 crore each.
Forex: INR rate moved from about INR80-85 to INR88-89 per USD on the large deal, causing a loss of a couple of crore; management said this was a one-time item.
Vendor base expanded to about 10 vendors with 12 added in FY26 (8 focused); two more PS partner agreements expected to be signed.
India cybersecurity market cited at USD6-7 billion, growing 15-18% YoY (management estimate).

qa_highlights.question: Why does H2 revenue dip versus H1 each year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to one large Zscaler-linked order above INR100 crore recognised mainly in H1, with billing timing also affected by forex-related delays.

qa_highlights.question: What caused the drop in Imperva services revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Imperva was acquired by Thales; the existing team left, cutting Meta's professional services revenue from about INR8.5 crore in FY25 to INR2 crore in FY26, versus an expected INR10 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Why was H2 product EBIT negative and what is the margin path?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it would check the H2 segment numbers; it stated a policy to avoid product deals below 5-6% margin and to target 9-10% product margins.

qa_highlights.question: Operating cash flow weak versus PBT; is it structural?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO Paresh Soni said it is timing: about INR20 crore of inventory at March, expected to sell in April; tax payments also weighed on operating cash flow.

qa_highlights.question: Does the company need more equity or debt?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no extra funding is needed for growth; the IPO was not required for expansion, and it cited delayed billing from forex-linked contracts.

risks_watch: Thales/Imperva PS revenue recovery: FY27 expectation of about INR10 crore depends on the new owner's team ramping up; management cited a one-to-one-and-a-half-year gestation period.
Margin dilution from the large low-margin Zscaler-linked contract running for about three years.
Cash conversion: management attributed weak operating cash flow to inventory of about INR20 crore at March and tax outflows; no reconciliation was given.
Attrition: management cited under 20% in FY26 versus 25-40% industry; a 15-25 person bench is maintained.
Customer concentration: largest bank was about 50-55% of FY26 revenue.
Management declined to give numeric revenue or margin guidance on compliance grounds; PAT target of INR40-45 crore by FY29 was an analyst's extrapolation, not confirmed.
544441|2026-03.management_tone: Confident and forward-looking on the three-year plan, but defensive on FY26 results, attributing the profit decline to one-off factors. Evasive on specific numbers, repeatedly citing compliance limits when asked for FY27 revenue, margins and H2 product losses.
key_quotes: So whatever happened before IPO and what is going to happen after the IPO over last six months, of course, there is a dip in overall revenue and stuff like that, which is conscious decision we have taken.
Our gross profit was INR49 crores in '25-'26 and '24-'25. We maintained the same.
So, all our contracts is conversion agnostic. So, customers we are signing up as Spot Plus 2.
Yes, there is a dip. That's a fact and we are not hiding the fact.

544441|2026-09.headline: H1 FY27 revenue fell 57% YoY to INR89.5 crore as Meta exited low-margin product sales to one bank; EBITDA margin rose to 8.7%.
544441|2026-09.overview: Revenue from operations was INR89.5 crore in H1 FY27 versus INR210 crore in H1 FY26, down 57% YoY, which management attributed to deliberately discontinuing lower-margin product sales to one leading bank. Sequentially, revenue rose 49% from INR59.9 crore in H2 FY26. EBITDA was INR7.8 crore (8.7% margin) versus INR15.8 crore (7.5%) a year earlier and INR2.3 crore (3.8%) in H2 FY26. PAT was INR4.9 crore versus INR10.4 crore in H1 FY26, with the order book at INR92.7 crore as of September 2026.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company on track for FY29 4x PAT versus FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 4x PAT is the ultimate target and it is on track, supported by recurring business and new business of INR20-30 crore a year.

544443|2026-03.headline: Travel Food Services Q4 system-wide sales grew 27.7% YoY to INR9 billion, while FY26 adjusted consolidated PAT rose 21.5% to INR4.5 billion on about 1% traffic growth.
544443|2026-03.overview: Management described FY26 as a disruption-heavy year (India-Pakistan conflict, aircraft crash-related schedule cuts, FDTL crew rest curbs, Middle East conflict from March 2026) in which TFS airport passenger traffic grew only 1.2%. Despite this, system-wide sales grew 25.4% to INR32.1 billion, driven by 9.4% like-for-like growth and 13.1% net contract gains. Q4 saw gross margin of 87.3% (85.6% after a one-time reclassification) and EBITDA up 38.3%, but PAT growth was held to about 15% by a INR212 million litigation provision and a weaker JV contribution. Trade receivables rose to about INR2.64 billion at year-end on EATS ramp-up, which management expects to normalise by H1 FY27.

segments.name: Travel QSR
segments.commentary: About 55% of FY26 consolidated revenue; growth driven by throughput, menu engineering and value combos.

segments.name: Lounges
segments.commentary: About 41% of FY26 consolidated revenue; growth from premiumisation and dwell time. Kyra Lounge opened at Hong Kong International Airport and a Cochin lounge opened in the year.

segments.name: Management and other services
segments.commentary: About 4% of FY26 consolidated revenue.

guidance_outlook: Gross margin expected in the 80% to 83% range for FY27 overall, with some inflationary pressure from LPG prices linked to the Middle East conflict.
Capex averaging INR50 crore to INR60 crore a year, including FY27, mainly for unit mobilisation at Delhi, Cochin and upcoming Noida.
Receivables (about INR264 crore at year-end vs INR100-110 crore average) expected to normalise to 40-45 days by H1 FY27.
Management expects FY27 passenger traffic growth of around 5%, per public reports, with Q1 FY27 still affected by the war-like situation.
Annual dividend of INR10.25 per share for FY26, subject to shareholder approval.
Bhogapuram (Vizag) contract under GHL expected to add about seven outlets; Noida airport operations expected to start in the coming months.
capex_capacity: Pipeline of more than 50 outlets, all committed per management.
Network now covers 20 airports and more than 550 travel QSR outlets and lounges; 76 travel QSR units mobilised in FY26 (including Delhi, Mumbai, Ahmedabad, Cochin, Navi Mumbai).
Noida airport on track to start operations in the coming months; two more airports in the works in the coming months.
International: Malaysia lounges expanded to three airports; second Hong Kong lounge opened in Q4; subsidiaries in Dubai and Indonesia.
Delhi T3 concession expired in February 2026; a six-month short-term extension was granted, and the company plans to bid through its JV GHL when it comes up.
demand_pricing: Passenger traffic at TFS airports grew 1.2% in FY26; Q4 was broadly flat YoY, with January up, February flat and March/April weaker on international traffic.
Management said domestic traffic was robust while international traffic fell nearly double digits in March-April, especially at southern airports and Goa.
Food inflation was about 3% to 5% in April per management; price hikes taken in line with inflation; key supplier contracts are annual.
Management said the mass-market credit card lounge access curbs are offset by premium cards growing more than 50%, with premium cardholders being frequent flyers.
Management expects LFL to be driven by about 7% to 10% passenger traffic plus about 7% to 10% from price and initiatives (combined).

qa_highlights.question: How is Q1 FY27 trading, given last year's Q1 was hit by India-Pakistan conflict?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said January was strong, February was muted, March and April were weak on international traffic, and early May shows improving trends versus March and April.

qa_highlights.question: Inorganic growth in FY27 and risk from Kolkata airport privatisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not guide numbers; cited 11 airports in the privatisation pipeline and said Kolkata's inclusion or state changes are not expected to alter the schedule.

qa_highlights.question: Can airport F&B pricing and energy costs be passed on?
qa_highlights.answer: Electric equipment is a large part of the cost base, giving a natural hedge; food inflation has been manageable, and price hikes follow inflation.

qa_highlights.question: Are airport concession fees rising and what is long-term economics?
qa_highlights.answer: Rentals are a normal portfolio negotiation with some going up and some down; management said nothing dramatically different is happening.

qa_highlights.question: What is the structural versus temporary Q4 EBITDA margin improvement?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the one-off reclassification of INR78 million cost reduced gross margin to 85.6% in Q4; full-year gross margin excluding it is about 84%.

qa_highlights.question: Why did finance cost rise, and what drove the receivables increase?
qa_highlights.answer: Finance cost rose due to a INR212 million litigation provision booked in full; receivables rose on EATS bank billing ramp-up and should normalise by H1 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the steady-state LFL breakup?
qa_highlights.answer: LFL is roughly passenger traffic (7% to 10% historically) plus 7% to 10% from price and initiatives, averaged over a year.

qa_highlights.question: Capital allocation and interest in duty-free or retail?
qa_highlights.answer: Management stressed cash discipline, zero debt and ROCE of about 45%, and prioritised international lounges and expressway wayside amenities; no duty-free plans were mentioned.

risks_watch: Middle East conflict and international traffic recovery; Gulf-bound and NRI travel remains weak.
Input cost pressure: LPG prices and food inflation impact on gross margin against the 80% to 83% range.
Receivables of about INR264 crore at year-end must normalise to 40-45 days by H1 FY27 as EATS scales.
Credit card lounge access restrictions from banks, a structural lounge risk.
Litigation provision of INR212 million, with the outcome still open; Delhi T3 concession extension expires after six months.

544443|2026-06.headline: Travel Food Services Q1 FY27: consolidated PAT up 35.6% YoY to INR1.3 billion on 20.6% revenue growth, despite flat passenger traffic and 0.8% system-wide LFL.
544443|2026-06.overview: Management reported system-wide sales up 18% YoY to INR8.4 billion and consolidated revenue from operations up 20.6% YoY to INR4.5 billion, with net contract gains of 15.9% system-wide. Passenger traffic was broadly flat YoY, with international traffic hit by the Middle East conflict and May's domestic rebound reversed in June. EBITDA rose 11% to INR1.6 billion, but margin moderated to 35.8% on pre-operating and employee costs for new airports (Noida, Cochin, Delhi). PAT was helped by a INR131 million one-time GST provision write-back in other income.

qa_highlights.answer: INR223 million of lounge aggregation cost sits in other expenses; excluding it, other expenses rose 22% YoY. Management expects normalisation within about 12 months.

qa_highlights.question: Why are JV and associate revenues growing slower than consolidated?
qa_highlights.answer: Some JV contracts are moving to JV structures over time, and Western airports with Middle East exposure, which form a bulk of JV portfolio, were hit.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Delhi T3 contract moving to JV in H2?
qa_highlights.answer: Delhi T3 contract runs to 30 September 2026; GHL has bid and results are awaited. The new SPV with GMR has 30% TFS shareholding, so it will not be consolidated going forward.

qa_highlights.question: Are the 50 outlets under development in existing airports?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, a blend of already-announced airports such as Delhi, Navi Mumbai and Bhogapuram; these were won 3-8 months ago and are in build-out.

qa_highlights.question: Highways strategy: is it accelerating?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said highways are a medium-to-long-term opportunity tied to government wayside amenity plans, with a return threshold that must be met; it will be calibrated, not immediate.

risks_watch: International traffic recovery depends on airline route restorations from September-October 2026; Middle East conflict renewed in June.
EBITDA margin (35.8%) under pressure from pre-operating and employee costs at new airports; watch normalisation in next 12 months.
Delhi T3 contract ends 30 September 2026 and the GHL JV bid outcome is unknown; it moves out of consolidation.
Chennai and Kolkata renewals due end-March 2027 and early Q1 FY28 may bring cost resets.
PAT growth flattered by INR131 million one-time GST write-back; underlying growth is lower.
544443|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on medium-term growth and balance sheet, but cautious on near-term traffic; management repeatedly attributes weakness to temporary external factors. Evasive on specific numbers such as net contract gain targets and JV economics, and on the Delhi T3 bid outcome.
key_quotes: Despite the disruptions arising from the ongoing conflict in the Middle East, we delivered double -digit growth in both sales and profitability, continued to expand our network, and further strengthened our position across key airport markets.
So, in a sense, if you see, we tend to be in that range of more than passenger traffic, somewhere in the 5% to 7% above that at least in terms of performance.
Those are the leverages that we tend to enjoy, in terms of bringing the required economies of scale.
In the new SPV, our shareholding with GMR is 30% and therefore it doesn't get consolidated going forward.

544444|2026-03.headline: Glen Industries H2 FY26 PAT of INR8.20 crore on INR108.60 crore income; management targets INR500 crore turnover and INR90 crore EBITDA in FY28.

Management attributed margin compression from about 23-24% in FY25 to about 18-19% in FY26 to passing on PLA price benefits to customers. A capacity expansion (plastic food containers roughly 3x, plus about 750 MT paper-based food packaging including paper cups) has a revised project cost of INR130-135 crore, now expected to start commercial production from September 2026. qa_highlights.question: Utilisation of straws and paper products given seasonality?

544447|2026-06.headline: Smartworks Q1 FY27 revenue rose 44% YoY to INR 546 crores, with normalized EBITDA margin at 19.6% and guidance of 28-30% revenue growth reaffirmed.
544447|2026-06.overview: Revenue reached INR 546 crores, up 44% YoY and 5% QoQ, while normalized EBITDA grew 74% YoY to INR 107 crores at a 19.6% margin. Normalized PAT nearly tripled YoY to INR 39 crores. Growth was supported by mature-centre occupancy (committed 92%) and a higher share of 1,000+ seat clients, GCCs and multi-city clients, though overall occupancy dipped to 81% from 82% QoQ as new centres filled up. Management reaffirmed FY27 guidance (28-30% revenue growth, 19-20% normalized EBITDA margin, 13 million sq ft by March 2027) and started a heavy capex cycle of INR 550-600 crores for the year.

vs negative INR 4.9 crores a year ago
vs INR 22 crores in same quarter last year

segments.name: GCC clients
segments.commentary: GCCs contribute 21% of revenue, up from 15% in FY26. Recent wins include a Swiss bank and a manufacturing GCC; a Japanese NBFC subsidiary took space in Mumbai.

segments.name: Singapore
segments.commentary: Work Studio acquired, taking the portfolio to over 1,500 seats (about 2% of revenue); 400-450 seats now available to sell, funded from Singapore cash flows. Management says no further meaningful expansion planned.

Security deposits of INR 33 crores paid to landlords to lock buildings for FY28 and part of FY29.

Seat retention 74% in Q1, with client count down while occupied seats and revenue rose. Management says the churn is deliberate repricing of older, lower-rate clients; the annual retention range it cited was 80-88%.
Realization on incremental mature-footprint seats leased in Q1 FY27 was about INR 181 per sq ft per month, up from about INR 170 a year earlier. Management cited a rental INR 185 per seat figure.
Mix: IT/ITES down to 35% of clients (from over 40%); target 25-30/35%. Multi-city clients 35% of revenue (31% in FY26).
Pre-commitment: about 30-35% of new buildings is pre-committed by existing or incoming clients. Landlord mix is about 65% non-institutional and 35% institutional.

qa_highlights.question: Rationale for the Singapore Work Studio acquisition, expected revenue and occupancy, and whether fit-out costs of INR 1,350 face inflation.
qa_highlights.answer: Acquired from internal cash flows at roughly construction cost; the target was about 60% occupied. Singapore is about 80,000 sq ft in total and 2% of revenue, with 400-450 seats now available to sell. Expansion will not be meaningful, and capex is set at INR 550-600 crores for FY27.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the expansion is speculative, and how much is pre-leased?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 30-35% of any new building is pre-committed by existing clients, and occupancy ramps to 80-85% within 13-14 months, as seen on prior centres.

qa_highlights.question: Is the drop in retention a sign of demand weakness, and will similar churn continue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 74% was Q2-seasonal churn; mature committed occupancy is 92%, and most churned space is already re-let. Churn is expected to fall in Q3 and Q4, as in prior years.

qa_highlights.question: Is there supply risk from developer delays?
qa_highlights.answer: Supply is covered by a buffer of 0.7-0.8 million sq ft over the 2.5-3 million sq ft target, and management is working with institutional developers such as DLF, Hiranandani, Tata, Panchshil and Salarpuria.

qa_highlights.question: How is the 28-30% guidance built, given the existing base is at 92% committed occupancy?

qa_highlights.question: Why did OCF/EBITDA dip, and what about VAS margins and pricing power?
qa_highlights.answer: The dip reflects INR 33 crores of security deposits paid to landlords. VAS is take-rate based with no direct cost, so it is margin accretive, but it is only in pilot stages and not in FY27 projections. Management said the nearest competitor prices 10-15% higher than Smartworks.

qa_highlights.question: Is the ROCE flat at 21.6% a peak, and when does FCF turn positive?

544454|2026-03.headline: IndiQube FY26 revenue hit a record INR 1,469 crore (+37% YoY) with EBITDA margin at 21% and PAT at INR 125 crore.
544454|2026-03.overview: FY26 delivered record revenue of INR 1,469 crore (+37% YoY), EBITDA above INR 300 crore (+60%) and PAT of INR 125 crore (+145%). Average steady-state occupancy was about 84%, while March 2026 end-of-month occupancy was 81%, which management attributed to newly delivered large properties ramping up. Management guided FY27 to 1.5-2 million sq ft of annual area addition, 25-30% revenue growth, EBITDA margin of 18-21% and PAT margin of 8-10%. Capex per sq ft is rising to about INR 16.5 from INR 15.5, and the company is adding 30-35 MW of solar next year.

segments.commentary: Contributed 15% of revenue in FY26 versus 12% a year earlier; management expects 17-18% over the next year. VAS EBITDA margins are about 10-15%, below the 18-20% space business. Around INR 40 crore of the quarter's VAS was one-time, per an analyst's figure.

segments.commentary: Recorded 1.4 million transactions over the year; new space management module and vehicle pooling feature in transport module gaining traction.

qa_highlights.question: Why did occupancy appear to dip to about 80-81% while area addition was small, and why did capex (about INR 413 crore) exceed the INR 360 crore guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the relevant metric is the FY26 average occupancy of about 84% (a 1% dip), and that quarterly swings are normal. The capex overrun reflected solar investment of about INR 73 crore that generates INR 20-23 crore of annual savings, plus vendor payment timing.

qa_highlights.question: Will lease payments grow in line with revenue next year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said lease costs will grow in line with revenue, at 25-30%, with EBITDA margin held at 18-21%.

qa_highlights.question: Are IT/ITES tenants reducing footprint, and why do landlords accept 15-year lock-ins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the vertical mix will broadly stay the same with gradual shifts. Landlords accept long lock-ins because the company funds fit-outs, which would be lost on exit, and similar norms exist in hotels and retail.

qa_highlights.question: What is the demand outlook for flex and GCCs over the next 12 months?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited strong absorption, no war impact yet, a weaker rupee boosting India work, and GCC-led absorption; AI impact not yet visible. It sees flex taking 20-25% of large occupiers' portfolios.

qa_highlights.question: What is driving the rise in one-time VAS revenue, and how will VAS mix evolve?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said one-time items are upfront sales of IT products, design-and-build and furniture, and are hard to predict; VAS share is expected to rise from 15% to 17-18%.

qa_highlights.question: Why is capex per sq ft rising, and what was the IPO fund reallocation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said material costs rose 5-7% due to the war, taking capex to INR 16.5 per sq ft from INR 15.5, absorbed by the company. The IPO reallocation moved INR 187 crore of capex to design-and-build, security deposits, solar and adjacent investments.

qa_highlights.question: Why not grow faster given available cash and about 50% headroom in area under management?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it prioritises sustainable growth and micro-market defensibility, avoids overbuilding, and values landlord relationships; it said it is trying to push growth faster within those limits.

qa_highlights.question: Can the company disclose quarterly rent-paying area additions in advance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management agreed to consider disclosing expected quarterly rent-paying area; it said it adds about 1-1.5 lakh sq ft per month of RPA, with about 1-1.25 lakh sq ft per month of rent-yielding area.

Management described the rental inflation of 4-5% in key micro-markets as sustainable.

544454|2026-06.headline: Indiqube Q1 FY27 revenue hit a record INR428 crore (+37% YoY) and PAT rose 91% to INR35 crore, with PAT margin at 8%.
544454|2026-06.overview: Management reported record quarterly revenue of INR428 crore (+37% YoY), EBITDA of INR87 crore (+34%), EBIT of INR55 crore (+59%) and PAT of INR35 crore (+91%). Margins expanded, with EBIT margin at 13% (11% a year ago) and PAT margin at 8% (6%). Rent-paying area was flat QoQ, which management attributed to the timing of building handovers, with about 2 million sq ft of annual additions still guided. Q&A centred on VAS revenue (INR39 crore one-time in the quarter), solar capex, a large new Noida centre, and occupancy and margin ranges. Management declined to give quarterly OCF or capex figures ahead of the H1 audit.

segments.name: Client mix (revenue)
segments.commentary: GCCs ~52-53% of revenue, startups and unicorns ~23%, Indian enterprises ~28% (of which GCCs ~10-12%). Multi-center clients ~41% of revenue; top five clients 12% of revenue; 855 clients as of June 2026.

segments.name: VAS (DesignQube, IndiCare, Eco)
segments.commentary: VAS is ~17% of revenue and management expects it to rise by about 2-4 percentage points. VAS EBIT margin is guided at ~15% for the next one to two years, as growth takes priority over margin.

segments.name: Solar / sustainability
segments.commentary: About 30 MW of solar capacity is operational. Plan to add 25-30 MW this year at INR100-120 crore capex; solar IRR stated at 18-22%.

guidance_outlook: Annual additions of close to 2 million sq ft (about 44,000 seats) reiterated; about 3.9 million sq ft (about 97,000 seats) of headroom already signed.
Corporate occupancy guided at 80-85% (stated later as 82-86%); mature centres (over 12 months) at 85-90% (stated as 86-90%/88-90%).
Margin ranges guided at EBITDA 19-21%, EBIT 11-13%, PAT 8-10% on a annual basis.
Operational break-even for new centres is 5-6 months at about 52-57% occupancy; steady state around 12 months (9-12 months to reach ~90%).

Large Noida centre expected to go live around mid-2027 (Q2 or Q3 FY28).
Management expects to sign larger spaces in Hyderabad and Mumbai during this financial year.

Capex and OCF for Q1 not disclosed; management said figures would be provided with H1 results after audit and review. Capex is driven by interiors, design-and-build, solar and vendor payment cycles.
Debt increase is attributed to solar investment, not the leasing business (per Vikas Agarwal).
New Noida centre is a large single building; live by mid-2027 (Q2/Q3 FY28).
demand_pricing: Institutional supply share rose to ~20% of portfolio from ~12% a couple of years ago; institutional buildings carry higher rents and CAM costs but management says margins are consistent across supply types.
Tier-2 centres: real estate cost INR50-70 per sq ft; seat pricing INR6,500-7,500 per seat; unit economics said to be similar to Tier-1.
Bangalore is ~60-64% of area; Chennai ~10%. Management expects Bangalore share to fall as NCR, Hyderabad, Mumbai and West India grow.
Attrition is negative (net expansion); client renewal rate ~90%; client notice periods 60-90 days; leases are straight leases with landlords (no back-to-back).
Tech parks are ~20% of portfolio. North Bangalore exposure is under 0.5 million sq ft of ~6.5 million sq ft in Bangalore.

qa_highlights.question: Why was there no QoQ rise in rent-paying area despite 2 million sq ft annual guidance, and is supply slowing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said additions are lumpy and tracked annually; H2 FY26 added ~1.14 million sq ft. No slowdown is seen, and ~3.9 million sq ft of signed headroom is available.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the INR39 crore one-time VAS revenue and how sustainable is it?
qa_highlights.answer: Revenue came across DesignQube, IndiCare and Eco. Management said it is non-recurring in quarters but will keep recurring over time, with VAS share rising 2-4 percentage points.

qa_highlights.question: How much solar capex is planned and what IRR is expected?
qa_highlights.answer: Plan of 25-30 MW more at INR100-120 crore; solar IRR 18-22%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for the large Noida centre and is it demand-backed?
qa_highlights.answer: Live by mid-2027 (Q2/Q3 FY28). Management said it was largely proactive supply, not pre-leased, based on NCR micro-market research.

qa_highlights.question: Will new centres dilute margins given slow break-even?
qa_highlights.answer: Operational break-even takes 5-6 months at 52-57% occupancy and steady state ~12 months, so no margin pressure expected. The 36 months referred to full capex recovery.

qa_highlights.question: What margin will VAS deliver and will it drive group margin expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: VAS margin ~15% for the next one to two years; management prioritises scale. Group-level margins are expected to stay within the stated ranges.

544454|2026-09.headline: IndiQube Q2 FY27 revenue rose 34% YoY to INR475 crore and PAT grew 63% to INR57 crore, with VAS at 17% of operating revenue.
544454|2026-09.overview: Management reported Q2 FY27 revenue of about INR475 crore (up 34% YoY), IGAAP EBITDA of INR105 crore (up 40%) and PAT of INR57 crore (up 63%). H1 revenue was INR904 crore (up 35%) and H1 PAT INR92 crore (up 66%). Steady-state occupancy improved to 91% from 89%, and VAS revenue reached INR154 crore in H1 (up 74%). Management guided to FY27 EBITDA margin of 19-21% (INR380-400 crore) and about 2 million sq ft of rent-paying area additions this year, while introducing new initiatives: a co-investment land pilot (SaiEdge, about INR35 crore), solar expansion, and a retail bank-branch fit-out business.

segments.name: Grow (core managed workspace)
segments.commentary: Core platform of 138 centers in 17 cities, about 10.86 million sq ft and about 241,000 seats across 884 clients; rent-paying area 8.2 million sq ft at Q2 FY27. Clients in GCCs contribute 54% of revenue.

segments.name: Value-added services (IndiQare, DesignQube, MiQube)
segments.commentary: H1 VAS revenue INR154 crore, up 74% YoY, about 17% of operating revenue. Management says VAS margin improved to about 20% from 15% and expects a range of about 18-20% going forward.

segments.name: Solar / IndiQube Eco
segments.commentary: About 30 MW operational capacity with another 30 MW expected within a year; about INR15 crore revenue in H1 against about INR46 crore invested. Payback about 3 years; planned about INR100 crore capex per year in Karnataka, Maharashtra and Tamil Nadu.

segments.name: Retail branch management (IndiQare)
segments.commentary: Early pilot with a large gold bank for about 30 branches; banks cited as 500-1,000 branch rollouts a year. Management described it as early, with capex models of INR1,400-1,800 per sq ft.

segments.commentary: Proposed investment of about INR35 crore in a Bangalore asset co-owned with investors, to be leased then sold or forward sold. Management said it is a three-year pilot and not core business.

qa_highlights.question: Rationale for the proposed ~INR35 crore SaiEdge Realty investment and planned solar capex.
qa_highlights.answer: Pilot co-ownership model to secure supply in micro markets where occupancy is above 90%; IndiQube would lease and then sell or forward-sell, with capital appreciation. Solar capex about INR100 crore per year over the next two years across Karnataka, Maharashtra and Tamil Nadu.

qa_highlights.question: Drivers of the Q2 margin uptick and whether the 20% VAS margin is a floor.
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the uptick to occupancy gain (89% to 91%, about 40% of growth), finance cost reduction of 1% (about 25%), VAS margin improvement and operating leverage from a 1% reduction in salary and other costs. VAS margin was not set as a floor; it is expected at about 18-20% as VAS is used as a foot-in-the-door.

qa_highlights.question: Renewal rates and renewal economics.
qa_highlights.answer: About 90% of expiring contracts renew; about 80% at same terms with 6% escalation. Renewal spend of INR40-50 per sq ft is expensed and tied to new lock-ins, and EBITDA converts to PBT after capex recovery.

qa_highlights.question: Branch management business and management bandwidth.
qa_highlights.answer: Early pilot with a large gold bank (about 30 branches); about 80% of retail fit-out needs match office interiors. Management said 50% of bandwidth goes to the existing Grow expansion and 50% to new opportunities.

544457|2026-06.headline: Brigade Hotel Ventures Q1 FY27 PAT rose 140% to INR17 crores on 9% RevPAR growth and lower finance cost, despite a ~INR14 crore West Asia-linked MICE cancellation hit.

risks_watch: Occupancy gap in non-Bangalore hotels: Courtyard Kochi (ex-Four Points) and ibis Styles Mysuru need to lift occupancy; Sheraton Grand rate growth was marginal.
Execution risk on the INR400-450 crore H2 capex and on the unidentified acquisition, which may slip one to two quarters.
Capex slippage: FY27 spend running well below allocation (INR84 crore in H1 vs about INR450 crore plan).
Leverage peaking at 3.5x to 4x net debt to EBITDA in FY28-FY29 as the pipeline is funded.
F&B and MICE dependence on event calendar, given the Q1 cancellations linked to the West Asia crisis.
544457|2026-09.management_tone: Confident on Q2 rate-led growth and margin expansion, and on the H2 outlook. Cautious and somewhat evasive on specifics: no numerical RevPAR range or upgrade to guidance, and the acquisition timing was left open.
key_quotes: This quarter we did about 10% and for half year, it was 9%, but we expect the second half of the year to be better.
Our growth for this quarter is rate-led.
So, we believe that from the second week of November onwards is when we will really see a very vibrant business, I guess, in all the hotels.
I don't want to change the guidance at this point in time, but I am happy about the EBITDA increase for Q2, which is very encouraging.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Q2 EBITDA margin rose to 36.7% from 32% and H1 margin reached 35.8% on rate-led growth (ADR +11%), with GST 2.0 drag easing to 1.6% in H1, though Q2 impact was 1.4%.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Courtyard Chennai (45 keys) is guided to open end Q3 or early Q4 FY27, but the Fairfield hotels and SPV hotels are only expected towards end FY28 or later, so the near-term addition is small.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management guides H2 RevPAR up mid-teens versus Q2 at about 10% and H1 at 9%, supported by festive, wedding and conference bookings, with occupancy flat at 75.2%.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation is 75.2%, below the 80% threshold, but the INR3,600 crore expansion plan with 1,700 keys under development and an unidentified acquisition as top priority makes further capex or deal announcements likely.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management held mid-teens FY27 revenue and EBITDA guidance and declined to raise it, with H1 total income only +7% and Q1 hit by about INR14 crore of West Asia cancellations still to recover.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Capex is running well below plan (INR84 crore in H1 vs about INR450 crore FY27 plan), the acquisition may slip one to two quarters, and Kochi and Mysuru occupancy is weak at 66% and 68%.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Courtyard by Marriott Chennai (45 keys) is expected to open end Q3 or early Q4, and the luxury mix is planned to rise from 14% to 31% by FY29, with Grand Grand Hyatt, InterContinental, JW Marriott and Ritz-Carlton in the pipeline.

rows.label: Unidentified IPO-funded acquisition
rows.why: Targeted as top priority in the next two to three quarters, with slippage of one to two quarters possible, and about INR400-450 crore of H2 FY27 capex includes earmarked capital for it.

rows.label: Courtyard Kochi occupancy recovery
rows.why: Occupancy fell to 66% in Q2 and 40% in H1 after the rebrand, with management guiding stabilisation over 2-3 quarters and a 17% ARR gain already achieved.

rows.label: Leverage peaks at 3.5-4x net debt/EBITDA
rows.why: Net debt to EBITDA is guided at 3.5x to 4x in FY28-FY29 as the INR700 crore FY28 capex is funded, with DSCR around 2x to 2.5x and net cash of INR29 crore today.

tone.note: Management was confident on Q2 rate-led growth, margin expansion and H2 RevPAR up mid-teens, but cautious on specifics, holding guidance without an upgrade and leaving acquisition timing open; analysts pushed on occupancy gaps in non-Bangalore hotels, leverage peaks and capex slippage.

544458|2026-03.headline: Shree Refrigerations FY26 revenue rose about 50% to INR153 crore and PAT to INR21 crore, with H2 EBITDA margin at 26.3% against 11% in H1.
544458|2026-03.overview: Management reported FY26 revenue of INR153 crore (roughly 50%+ growth), PAT up about 64% and reported EPS up 28% to INR6.47 despite the IPO dilution. H2 revenue of about INR100 crore was roughly double H1's INR50 crore, as H1 was spent on design and type-test approvals, machine additions and a new Wajeri facility. Working capital days fell from 570 to 370, and the closing order book was INR270 crore. Management guided to 20-24% EBITDA margin going forward and 40% revenue CAGR for 3-5 years, with data centre revenue expected only from FY28.

financial_highlights.change: Up about 50%+ YoY (management cited ~150% growth in one place; call transcript inconsistent)
Up about 100% YoY and HoH vs INR50 crore in H1
Up from INR13 crore; PAT up about 64% YoY per management
Up 28% YoY from INR5 despite higher share count
from INR118 crore, on IPO and profit
from 570 days; receivable days 350 to 250; inventory days 250 to 230

segments.name: Defence / naval HVAC, AC plant and refrigeration
segments.commentary: Core business with management-stated 64%-plus market share; 8 ongoing projects, 4 of which are expected to complete in FY27. Order book INR270 crore at March-end, mostly HVAC, AC plant and refrigeration.

segments.name: Spares, service and AMC
segments.commentary: Fell to about 7% of revenue in FY26 from about 30% last year; management targets 15% (and 15-20% in another answer) to lift EBITDA margin.

segments.name: Data centre cooling (via Smardt tie-up)
segments.commentary: Channel partnership about six months old; reference installation targeted in FY27, with major revenue expected from FY28. No data centre revenue assumed in FY27 guidance.

guidance_outlook: EBITDA margin expected at 20-24% going forward; management said commodity inflation was considered in this guidance.
Growth guided at about 40% CAGR for 3-5 years; CEO reiterated INR1,000 crore revenue target within about 5 years and INR120-130 crore PAT target for FY30-31 from the earlier presentation.
FY27 guidance excludes data centre revenue.
FY27 order inflow expected to be lumpier across halves but H2 still expected to be bigger than H1; management says the skew will be reduced.
Working capital days expected to keep improving from 370 days; GST input credit refund expected to reduce other current assets in H1 FY27.
Management said the business needs no major capex for at least a couple of years; growth to be funded by internal accruals and bank working capital funding.
capex_capacity: Hanbarwadi Phase 1 capex INR25 crore, mostly spent; plant to start commercial production in June 2026.
Leased unit (about 20,000 sq ft) to close in June 2026; owned facility brings manufacturing space to about 70,000-80,000 sq ft, expandable by a further 50,000 sq ft.
Management says existing infrastructure can generate up to about INR400 crore of revenue at peak.
New Kochi office planned in FY27; new ATU controlled-ambient test room and AC plant and wet plant test facilities added.
Six AC plant capacities standardised by Navy: four type-tested; all six ATU and all AFU capacities type-tested; about 70% of ventilation fan variants type-tested.
demand_pricing: Navy plans to grow from about 150 ships to about 230 over 5-7 years; AONs of INR2.3-2.4 lakh crore granted, translating into orders over two years.

Management estimates its addressable share at about 1% of project cost, i.e. about INR2,500 crore defence TAM over two years, plus about INR500 crore non-defence; total TAM stated at INR3,000-3,500 crore over about 2-2.5 years.
Retrofit hit rate close to 100%; newbuild tenders lost in some cases.
Expected defence tenders of about INR1,000 crore to be floated in FY27; win rate not guided.
Data centre cooling is about 12-13% of data centre project value; data centre cooling market stated at USD 2.99 billion growing to about USD 9 billion over 3 years (25-30% CAGR).
Commodity inflation (copper and other metals) acknowledged; fixed-price projects of 2-3 years carry risk, with impact called small versus peers.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 H1/H2 revenue phasing and why was FY26 skewed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY27 will be less skewed than FY26 but H2 will still be bigger; shipyard delivery schedules drive timing, and more concurrent projects should smooth it.

qa_highlights.question: What EBITDA margin range should be expected?
qa_highlights.answer: Manoj Kothale guided 20-24% EBITDA margin going forward, and management said commodity inflation was factored into this.

qa_highlights.question: What is the data centre revenue timing and is it in the 40% growth guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Reference installation in FY27 and major data centre revenue from FY28; FY27 guidance excludes data centre revenue.

qa_highlights.question: How does the INR1,000 crore revenue target reconcile with 40% CAGR?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 40% growth would reach about INR833 crore, but it stands by INR1,000 crore within about 5 years.

qa_highlights.question: Will external fundraising be needed?
qa_highlights.answer: No; working capital growth to be funded through internal accruals and bank funding, with a non-leveraged balance sheet.

qa_highlights.question: Export plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Export plans are nascent and limited to marine (defence/naval) business, not data centre; no details given.

qa_highlights.question: Danfoss servicing tie-up size?
qa_highlights.answer: Appointed Turbocor Authorized Service Partner; revenue not significant at present as the installed base is about 1,200-1,300 compressors, described as a strategic capability step.

risks_watch: Revenue skew to H2 and lumpy delivery timing by shipyards; quarterly reporting declined by management.
Metal and commodity inflation on fixed-price projects of 2-3 years; margin guidance depends on it.
Spares and service share (7% in FY26) must recover to 15%+ to support margin.
Working capital still 370 days; GST input credit refund (other current assets up 6x to INR19.94 crore) pending.
Data centre revenue depends on Smardt product qualification; competition from around 30-40 global players, with most already present in India.
Management says main-board listing not allowed for about two more years.
Some newbuild tenders lost; FY27 defence tender flow of about INR1,000 crore is an uncertainty on order inflow.
544458|2026-03.management_tone: Confident and expansive on the long-term story (40% CAGR, INR1,000 crore target, data centre), while being evasive on quarterly reporting and on specifics such as data centre revenue sizing and export plans. Management repeatedly stated that the FY26 H1/H2 skew came from project and delivery timing.
key_quotes: So, we are very confident that we will achieve the guidance that has been given by our CEO.
INR1,000 crore is the ladder which we are here in next 5 years and it will happen, sir.
Data centre revenue will start trickling in from next year onward, FY28 and onward, not in FY27.
So, for next going forward, we expect that our EBITDA margin will remain somewhere between 20% to 24%.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management guided 20-24% EBITDA margin going forward vs FY26 21% and H2 26.3%, with commodity inflation said to be factored in, and spares/service to recover from 7% of revenue toward 15-20%.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.when: Q1 FY27 (Hanbarwadi Phase 1 commercial production June 2026)
rows.why: Hanbarwadi Phase 1 (INR25 crore capex, mostly spent) starts June 2026, and owned facility brings manufacturing space to about 70,000-80,000 sq ft, expandable by a further 50,000 sq ft; management says existing infrastructure can generate up to about INR400 crore revenue at peak versus FY26 revenue of INR153 crore.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management guides ~40% revenue CAGR for 3-5 years backed by a INR270 crore closing order book (about 1.8x FY26 revenue), with 8 ongoing projects, 4 of which complete in FY27.

rows.why: Revenue is skewed to H2 (H1 INR50 crore vs H2 INR100 crore), defence tender flow of about INR1,000 crore in FY27 is uncertain, fixed-price projects of 2-3 years carry metal inflation risk, and GST refund of INR19.94 crore is pending.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Data centre cooling via Smardt tie-up has a reference installation targeted in FY27 and major revenue from FY28, but no data centre revenue is in FY27 guidance and product qualification is pending.

rows.label: Defence tender flow and Navy fleet expansion
rows.why: Navy plans to grow from about 150 to about 230 ships over 5-7 years, AONs of INR2.3-2.4 lakh crore granted, and about INR1,000 crore of defence tenders expected in FY27 against a INR270 crore order book.

rows.label: Working capital days falling further
rows.why: Net working capital days fell from 570 to 370 and management expects further improvement, with GST input credit refund reducing other current assets (up 6x to INR19.94 crore) in H1 FY27.

rows.label: Data centre cooling via Smardt
rows.when: reference installation FY27; major revenue FY28
rows.why: Data centre cooling is about 12-13% of project value and the market is stated at USD 2.99 billion growing to about USD 9 billion over 3 years, but revenue depends on Smardt product qualification and competition from 30-40 global players.

544458|2026-09.headline: Shree Refrigerations H1 FY27 revenue rose about 84-85% YoY to roughly INR 100 crore, with EBITDA margin up to 13.5% from 11%; FY27 margin guided at about 22%.
544458|2026-09.overview: H1 FY27 revenue was roughly INR 100 crore, up about 84-85% YoY, and EBITDA margin improved to 13.5% from 11% despite commodity inflation. Management reiterated 40% revenue CAGR and about 22% annual EBITDA margin guidance, while H1 margins remain skewed low versus H2. Order book stood at about INR 198.6-200 crore at September, down from INR 270 crore at the start of the year, and operating cash flow was negative about INR 42 crore in H1. Management said the data centre opportunity is excluded from guidance and is expected to take 6-12 months to gain traction.

financial_highlights.change: Up about 84-85% YoY vs H1 FY26
Down from INR 270 crore at start of year
Up from INR 105 crore; about 250 days
Up from about 370 days after IPO-era improvement

segments.name: Refrigeration vertical (HVAC, AC plant, Ref plant)
segments.commentary: Management reports a single refrigeration vertical with no separate product segments; HVAC is a larger share than AC plant, and Ref plant is a very small share. Retrofit is the major business line, with defence spares a large component, alongside installation, commissioning and service.

segments.name: Non-defence / industrial
segments.commentary: Industrial chillers and test equipment are described as negligible today. A new wholly owned subsidiary for sub-zero chillers (Aquilon) targets chemical, food and pharma, with commercial operations expected from next financial year.

segments.name: Data centre (oil-free / magnetic-bearing chillers)
segments.commentary: No data centre orders yet; the Danfoss Turbocor-based offering is sourced from an Australian partner. Management expects traction in 6-12 months and excludes data centre revenue from FY27 and FY28 projections.

guidance_outlook: Revenue to grow at about 40% CAGR; management reaffirmed this for FY27 and beyond, noting the guidance excludes data centre revenue.
EBITDA margin about 22% at annual level for FY27; H1 at 13.5% implies a steep H2 ramp, which management attributes to higher H2 volumes and product mix.
Working capital days expected to fall to about 350 days (CEO) and receivable days to about 200 days (CFO) over time.
Operating cash flow expected to turn positive by year-end FY27.
Order book expected to be healthy by year-end; management said orders will come in continuously rather than concentrated in Aug-Sep as last year.
Subsidy for the Karad unit 2 facility (Maharashtra D-class area) is not in projections and could add to margin.
capex_capacity: Unit 2 (Karad/Hanbarwadi) recently opened with about 50,000 sq ft in use; combined with unit 1 (about 20,000 sq ft) total manufacturing area about 70,000 sq ft.
Adjacent land of about 50,000 sq ft is already levelled, so a new shed can be built quickly if a new opportunity arises.
Management says current capacity is sufficient for guidance; no fresh equity needed unless a new opportunity emerges.
Unit 1 (about 20,000 sq ft) being converted into a full testing facility, including an ambient-controlled AC test room.
Small CapEx expected for the Aquilon sub-zero chiller initiative; a small manufacturing unit is being set up.
demand_pricing: Navy fleet support ship turnkey project is among about 10 live projects; management cites a large AC/HVAC/Ref plant order for the Indian Navy.

Management cites a market of about INR 2,750 crore over two years from naval ship approvals (about 1% share) and about INR 2,500 crore in non-naval shipbuilding (about 0.5% share), for an estimated INR 4,000-5,000 crore opportunity.
Next-generation corvette (NGC) orders reportedly cleared by CCS; management expects part of the orders to convert into firm orders in FY27 and the rest in FY28.
Eight orders are in the pipeline.
Imports reduced from about 30%+ to single digit in AC plants, per management.

qa_highlights.question: Why are H1 margins low again, and what H2 margin is needed to hit guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited commodity (copper, metals) inflation on fixed-price contracts, offset by strategic sourcing and higher inventory. H2 is seasonally stronger due to higher volumes absorbing overheads and product mix. Management said the 22% guidance is annual, not half-yearly, and skewness should fade over 2-3 years.

qa_highlights.question: Why are receivable days high and what is the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said receivable days fell from about 350 in FY25 to 250 at March 2026, were held at about 250 in H1 despite 84% growth, and should go to about 200. Management said there is no one-off and that shipyard milestone-based payments limit faster reduction.

qa_highlights.question: Why is operating cash flow negative and when does it turn positive?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO attributed negative operating cash flow of about INR 42 crore to strategic sourcing, H2 deliveries and higher receivables. Management expects cash flow to turn positive by the end of FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the data centre plan and are orders expected?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no data centre orders yet; the oil-free/magnetic-bearing technology is sourced from an Australian partner, with no manufacturing in India until volumes justify it. Traction is expected in 6-12 months and is excluded from FY27-28 projections.

qa_highlights.question: Can capacity support 40% growth and are new capex or funds needed?
qa_highlights.answer: Capacity is sufficient for current guidance. Land is levelled for a further shed if needed. Funding would be raised only if a new opportunity needs it; the additional working capital is to come mainly from internal accruals and some bank borrowing.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the depreciation method changed to straight line?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said straight-line depreciation better reflects asset use and was adopted in a year of heavy capex. No quantified impact was given on the call.

risks_watch: Commodity inflation (copper, metals) on fixed-price contracts could compress margins if strategic sourcing is insufficient.
Negative operating cash flow and rising receivables (INR 128 crore) and inventory (INR 80 crore); working capital days were about 400 against a target of about 350.
Order book fell from INR 270 crore to about INR 200 crore; the H2 order ramp is not yet visible.
Dependence on naval shipbuilding timelines and government budget or election-related delays were raised as questions; management disputed the risk.
Data centre traction is unproven and excluded from guidance; management acknowledged no orders yet.
ROCE currently about 14-15% per analyst; management says the same capital base should lift returns as growth is funded by working capital.
544458|2026-09.management_tone: Confident on growth and the naval pipeline, with repeated reassurance on the 40% CAGR and 22% margin guidance. Cautious and somewhat evasive on H1 margin gap, cash flow and the data centre timeline, relying on H2 skew and sector explanations. We feel that we are still about 6 to 8 months, maybe even about a year away for that kind of traction and therefore, we do not actually include data centre business revenues either into this financial year nor into our projections for the next year.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Aquilon sub-zero chiller subsidiary has commercial operations expected from next financial year (FY28), and data centre offering traction is expected in 6-12 months, but neither is in guidance and no orders exist yet.

rows.label: Naval fleet and NGC corvette orders converting to firm orders
rows.why: Management expects part of the cleared next-generation corvette orders to convert to firm orders in FY27 and the rest in FY28, with about 10 live projects and 8 pipeline orders, though the order book has fallen to about INR 200 crore.

rows.label: Operating cash flow turns positive and receivable days fall
rows.why: H1 operating cash flow was negative INR 42 crore and receivable days were about 250; management targets positive cash flow by FY27 end and receivable days of 200 going forward, with shipyard milestone payments limiting pace.

rows.label: Karad unit 2 subsidy not in projections
rows.why: The Maharashtra D-class area subsidy for the Karad facility is excluded from projections and could add to margin, but no amount was quantified on the call.

544459|2026-03.headline: Shanti Gold Q4 FY26 revenue rose 121.65% YoY to INR 658.93 crore, a record quarter, with EBITDA margin at 10.17%.
544459|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue from operations was INR 658.93 crore, up 121.65% YoY, the highest quarterly revenue in company history, driven by new customers, higher volumes and elevated gold prices. FY26 revenue reached INR 2,018.71 crore (+82.46%), with PAT of INR 140.15 crore (6.94% margin). Management changed inventory valuation from FIFO to weighted average cost with retrospective effect from April 1, 2024. Much of the profit uplift was attributed by management to inventory gains from gold bought outright with IPO proceeds, and management guided to a core PAT margin of around 4%.

financial_highlights.change: from INR 9.19 crore in Q4 FY25

segments.name: Studded / bridal jewellery (existing line)
segments.commentary: Management said about 70% of revenue comes from the existing studded line; bridal jewellery carries higher margins and contributed to the Q4 EBITDA improvement.

segments.name: Plain gold jewellery (new line)
segments.commentary: About 30% of revenue is from the newly entered machine-made plain gold segment, which management described as lower margin, higher volume.

guidance_outlook: FY27 guidance: volume growth of 30% to 40% and value growth of 60% to 70%; management cited FY27 turnover of around INR 3,000 to 3,500 crore in one answer and about INR 4,000 crore in another.

Core PAT margin guided at around 4% (management cited a 3.5% to 4% core range); the FY26 margin above this was attributed to inventory gains on gold bought outright with IPO proceeds, which management says is now mitigated and not included in guidance.
Export share guided to rise from about 5-10% to 10-20% this year, with Dubai subsidiary incorporation extended to June 2026.
Management expects to reach full 7,900 kg capacity in three to four years.
Working capital: management said inventory and trade receivables are each under 50 days; plain jewellery is expected to improve working capital cycle over time.
Debt-equity: management said it is comfortable at up to 1:1 (currently 0.36) to fund growth.
capex_capacity: Existing Andheri facility: installed capacity about 2,700 kg per annum, operating at around 65% utilisation.
Marol facility in Mumbai: adds about 4,000 kg per annum; management said it should be ready in about a month, starting at roughly 100 kg per month before ramping up.
Jaipur facility: adds 1,200 kg per annum; expected to start around September-October 2026.
Post-expansion total installed capacity is about 7,900 kg per annum, roughly three times the current capacity.
Quarterly volume reported at about 145-150 kg per month in a Q&A answer, which management said was disclosed quarterly in the presentation.
demand_pricing: Management said the structural shift from unorganised to organised jewellery retail is driving outsourcing to scalable manufacturers.

Management said demand is resilient, particularly in wedding and occasion-led categories; new products include Turkish jewellery (Turkish artisans onboarded for Marol), Mangalsutra and Cuban bracelets.
Management said the company has more than 400 customers and about 7% of volume or value from its top customer; it does not supply Titan/Tanishq currently.

Gold price context: management cited a move from about INR 78,000 to about INR 108,000 per 10 g and an assumed price of about INR 1,50,000 for guidance; it said guidance is based on current prices and not speculation.
Management said the 15% import duty increase would not hurt demand, citing a period when duty was 15% for many years and was cut to 6% last year.

qa_highlights.question: Is FY26 growth mainly price-driven, and what is the demand outlook ex-gold?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said volume grew about 15% in FY26 after the IPO and value growth was higher; FY27 is guided at 30-40% volume and 60-70% value growth.

qa_highlights.question: Sustainable margin and how much of FY26 profit was from gold?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said a core PAT margin of around 4% is sustainable; the extra profit came from gold bought outright with IPO money, when gold prices rose.

qa_highlights.question: Capacity utilisation and volume per month?
qa_highlights.answer: Current utilisation is about 65%; volume is about 145-150 kg per month per the quarterly figures in the presentation.

qa_highlights.question: Working capital and maximum debt level?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said debt-equity of up to 1:1 is the target ceiling, with the current ratio at 0.36; inventory and receivables are each under 50 days.

qa_highlights.question: Why did volume guidance fall from 60-70% to 30-40%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY26 volume grew 15% and FY27 guidance of 40% plus is an increase, not a reduction; no contradiction in volume guidance.

qa_highlights.question: What is the hedging policy and inventory held?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said its hedging policy is to buy as it sells; it said about 600 kg of stock plus debtors is left, and it does not chase price movements.

risks_watch: Gold price volatility: management acknowledged gains and losses from inventory price movements; FY26 profit included inventory gains that management says are now excluded from guidance.
Margin gap: FY26 PAT margin was 6.94% versus the 4% core margin guided for FY27, and an analyst noted that doubling revenue to INR 4,000 crore at 4% implies only about INR 160 crore PAT.
Execution of the Marol (about 4,000 kg) and Jaipur (1,200 kg) ramp-ups, and the timing of the Jaipur start in September-October 2026.
Working capital and receivables: debtor days rose from 42 to 48-49; management expects new plain jewellery to improve the cycle.
Leverage: debt-equity expected to rise towards 1:1 to fund growth from 0.36 currently.
Geopolitical risk: the Dubai subsidiary has been delayed to June 2026 and export share targets depend on it.
Management said the 15% import duty would not hurt demand, but the duty increase is a demand-side watch item.
544459|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on volumes and demand, but defensive and at times evasive on margin sustainability and gold-price exposure, repeatedly redirecting to a 4% core margin. Answers on the inventory gains and PAT trajectory were inconsistent, and the call was marked by answers that were brief and sometimes unclear.

544465|2026-03.headline: Laxmi India Finance FY26 AUM rose over 27% to INR1,626 crore, PAT up 38% to INR49.7 crore, Gross NPA 2.13%.

Net interest income rose nearly 39% to INR161 crore and PAT rose over 38% to INR49.7 crore. Blended cost of borrowing fell to 10.8% from 11.48%, and Acuite upgraded the rating to A/Stable. Management guided to 30-35% AUM CAGR and about 40-45% PAT growth in FY27, with Q4 PAT helped by an upfront gain of INR8.66 crore on a INR41 crore direct assignment (DA) pool.

segments.commentary: 176 branches across six states (Rajasthan, Gujarat, MP, Chhattisgarh, UP, Maharashtra), with 18 added in FY26. Breakeven takes about 7-8 months and about INR1.5-2 crore of disbursement per branch.

segments.name: Treasury / borrowings
segments.commentary: Over 40 lenders across PSU banks, private banks, SFBs, NBFCs and FIs; bank borrowings are the focus. Incremental cost is about 10.25-10.30%, and post-IPO fresh borrowing is at 10-10.25%.
