544465|2026-06.headline: Laxmi India Finance Q1 FY27 PAT rose ~70% YoY to INR16.4 crore, NIM expanded to 11.36%, while credit cost jumped to 0.95% on vehicle loans.
544465|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 showed strong growth: AUM up 28% YoY to INR1,721.7 crore, own book up 31.7% to INR1,626.9 crore, and disbursements of INR232 crore versus INR166 crore a year ago. Profitability improved sharply, with PBT up ~72% to INR21.9 crore and PAT up ~70% to INR16.4 crore, driven by a 67 bps fall in cost of borrowing to 10.66%. Asset quality improved sequentially (GNPA 2.08%, NNPA 0.93%), but credit cost rose to INR3.69 crore (0.95%) from 0.58%, attributed mainly to vehicle finance and an extra 10% provisioning on up-money cases. Management kept FY27 PAT growth guidance of 40-45% and AUM growth of 30-35% unchanged.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR166 crore in Q1 FY26 (~+40%)

financial_highlights.value: INR3.69 crore (0.95% of avg gross loan)

financial_highlights.metric: Debt to equity / net debt to equity

segments.name: MSME (secured SME)
segments.commentary: Core vertical at ~INR1,395 crore AUM; management says core MSME and construction credit costs remain moderate. A new prime MSME product for INR25-50 lakh tickets was recently launched.

segments.name: Vehicle finance (wheels)
segments.commentary: AUM ~INR131 crore; source of the credit cost rise, attributed to older vintages in specific geographies. Acceptance criteria tightened and field follow-ups increased.

segments.name: Construction and loan against property
segments.commentary: AUM ~INR90 crore.

segments.name: Wholesale lending
segments.commentary: AUM ~INR58 crore.

segments.commentary: AUM ~INR49 crore.

capex_capacity: Branch network at 184 across six states (Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, Gujarat, Chhattisgarh, Uttar Pradesh, Maharashtra); 25 branches added over the last year, including 10 in UP and 6 in Maharashtra.
New branches reach breakeven in ~7-9 months (range 5-12 months) at an AUM of ~INR1.5-2 crore per branch; one of the 25 new branches is already at breakeven.
Branches are tiered: Tier 1 with 5-6 relationship officers, Tier 2 with 5-6, Tier 3 with 2-5.
Rajasthan (mother state, ~90 branches) remains the largest contributor; other states are expected to gain share over 3-4 years.
Digitised LOS/LMS, CKYC, RCU, eNACH and auto-dialer; only physical loan signing remains, expected to move to eSign shortly.
demand_pricing: Disbursements of INR232 crore grew ~40% YoY, ahead of 28% AUM growth; management attributes the gap to repayments and closures.

Management flagged rising competitive intensity in MSME lending and said underwriting discipline will be maintained.

qa_highlights.question: How are the new branches performing versus the mature network, and what is the gestation period to steady-state productivity?
qa_highlights.answer: Of 25 branches opened in the last year, one has reached breakeven. Breakeven takes about 7-9 months (5-12 months range) at branch AUM of roughly INR1.5-2 crore; Tier 1, 2 and 3 branches are staffed with 5-6, 5-6 and 2-5 relationship officers respectively.

qa_highlights.question: Over 3-5 years, what must change to move from a regional NBFC to a pan-India MSME franchise, and what is the biggest constraint?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it will enter one or two new states per year, having started in Rajasthan and expanded through Gujarat, MP, Chhattisgarh, UP and Maharashtra. Management said it targets ROA of 3.5-3.75% and expects to reach it by year-end, with current ROA at 3.45%.

qa_highlights.question: What product and geographic mix changes are planned as AUM scales?
qa_highlights.answer: MSME stays the core product, with a new prime MSME product for INR25-50 lakh tickets. Plan is 30-35 branches in existing states in FY27, with 10 added in Q1. Rajasthan (about 90 branches) stays the largest state for the next 3-4 years, with other states gaining share.

qa_highlights.question: Why did credit cost rise to about 1%, and is stress coming from newer geographies or vintages?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the rise to the wheels (vehicle) portfolio, specifically older vintages in certain geographies, and said it is localised. Gopal Krishan Sain said the main P&L driver was an extra 10% provisioning on up-money transactions, with 70% of that provisioning booked so far.

qa_highlights.question: How much balance sheet capacity remains before equity is needed, given CRAR moderation from about 26% to 25%?
qa_highlights.answer: Net debt to equity is 2.57x with liquidity of about INR255.9 crore. Management plans to raise about INR300-350 crore in roughly 1-1.5 years, starting next financial year, when leverage reaches about 3.5-4x (pre-IPO about 4-4.5x).

qa_highlights.question: What are the FY27 and FY28 growth and margin guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: AUM growth of 30-35% CAGR will be maintained. Margins depend on cost of borrowing and yield; management expects to pass some borrowing-cost relief to borrowers once cost of borrowing is in a declining phase.

qa_highlights.question: Are the El Nino and global uncertainties affecting the portfolio, and is AUM being expanded aggressively?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said global conflict has limited direct impact since customers are in Tier 2/3 cities, though crude prices raise borrower costs. qa_highlights.answer: Net slippages were INR3.26 crore.

qa_highlights.answer: Piyush Somani said another 20-25 bps reduction is expected over coming quarters, assuming stable global rates and no RBI hike; incremental cost of borrowing is about 10.48% over the last 12 months. Cost-to-income is below 50% now, with an internal target of around 42-44%; opex is elevated by new-state branch openings.

544466|2026-03.headline: Aditya Infotech Q4 FY26 revenue rose 45.5% YoY to INR1,422 crore with EBITDA margin of 18%; FY27 revenue guidance raised to INR6,000-6,500 crore.
544466|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue grew 45.5% YoY to INR1,422 crore, with EBITDA up 162% to INR258.3 crore and margin up 800 bps to 18%, helped by price rise, low-cost inventory and SKU mix. Full-year FY26 revenue reached INR4,220.8 crore (+35.6%), EBITDA INR579 crore (13.7% margin) and adjusted PAT INR368 crore (+166.1%). Management raised FY27 guidance to revenue INR6,000-6,500 crore, EBITDA margin 14-15% and PAT margin 8.5-9.5%. Management flagged that low-cost inventory is now exhausted and component costs (chips, memory, USD, freight) will keep rising through 2027, so price increases are being passed on monthly in small steps.

financial_highlights.change: Debt repaid from IPO proceeds; Q4 finance cost down 38%

segments.name: CP PLUS brand
segments.commentary: Contributed 86% of AIL revenue in Q4 and FY26; IP products are 73% of the CP PLUS portfolio.

segments.name: Camera/CCTV (India market)
segments.commentary: Company market share about 45.4% as of Q3 FY26, versus about 30% overall and about 25% for CP PLUS at the start of the journey. Management says it is not targeting a specific share number.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guidance raised to INR6,000-6,500 crore, about 50% growth over FY26.
FY27 EBITDA margin guidance 14-15%; PAT margin around 8.5-9.5%. Management called 14-15% the new normal for FY27 and FY28, with Q4 a one-off above that level.
Unit volume growth target 25-30%, against an industry CCTV unit growth estimate of 15-16%.
Average per-unit camera realisation expected to rise 20-25% in FY27 (analyst-cited ASP growth about 25%).
FY27 capex expected at INR200-300 crore, funded mainly from internal accruals and some debt.
FY28 vision: double production capacity versus current levels, complete backward integration in key components, and a fully functional global R&D presence including Taiwan.
capex_capacity: Manufacturing capacity has reached 2.5 million units; management targets 90-100% utilisation.
Housing plant: Phase-1 operational by Q2 FY27 and Phase-2 by Q4 FY27, targeting 30 million housings and enclosures per year.
New lens assembly line commissioning with initial capacity of 5 lakh lenses per month, scalable to 1 million per month; CCTV lens production to start soon at Kadapa.
Kadapa: acquiring additional land and adding a 50,000 sq ft shed. Noida: proposed 3 lakh sq ft facility in Sector 68, operational by Q4 FY27.
Orient Cables JV for LAN and CCTV cable manufacturing: plant in Rajasthan (about 1 lakh sq ft), commercial operations expected between Q2 and Q3 FY27.
HD analog job work planned to move to EMS partners at about 0.5 million units per month. Evaluating further land in North India.
demand_pricing: Price hike of 6-8% taken in January 2026; management now moves prices monthly in small steps (single-digit % per month, varying by category) to avoid shocking customers. Further increases expected in FY27.

Market unit growth expected at 15-16% for FY27. Management says the industry's pent-up demand from the STQC transition was muted in FY26, and ASP increases are heavier on entry-level IP and NVR than on enterprise/project segments.
Consumer purchases are under 10% of the business; the business is largely B2B. Government is 15-20% of revenue and management plans for a similar share.

Memory: half of the 6-7 non-China DDR makers have stopped DDR3 output, pushing supply tightness onto smaller players. Management says scale lets AIL secure supply ahead of competitors.
Volume vs value in FY26: volume growth about 18-20%, with the rest from ASP and mix.

qa_highlights.question: How much of Q4 gross margin (about 31.8%) came from low-cost inventory, mix or price rise, and is it sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Anup Nair cited a mix of low-cost inventory, the Q4 price rise and higher-end SKUs (STQC-certified project SKUs from H2). He said the low-cost inventory is now mostly used up, but FY27 guidance is above FY26 and slightly below Q4 margin.

qa_highlights.question: Cash conversion cycle and working capital needs with advance chip and memory purchases?
qa_highlights.answer: Anup Nair said the cash conversion cycle has risen because creditors fell as the company secured supply, and some inventory is being blocked with advance payments. Working capital is factored into FY27 plans; capex is to be funded mainly from internal accruals and some debt.

qa_highlights.question: Capex plans for FY27-28?
qa_highlights.answer: Aditya Khemka said the earlier plan of about INR200 crore has been raised to INR200-300 crore for FY27, with FY28 plans still under work. Funding is through internal accruals and some debt; the debt-equity ratio is very low.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 14-15% EBITDA margin the new normal?
qa_highlights.answer: Aditya Khemka said 14-15% should be the new normal for FY27 and FY28, driven by localisation, cost optimisation, the shift to higher-end and enterprise products and premiumisation. Q4 was a one-off.

qa_highlights.question: Export plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Aditya Khemka said export action may start in FY27, but domestic demand comes first. Some thoughts are underway and the outcome is not yet clear.

qa_highlights.question: Revenue split FY26: volume vs price?
qa_highlights.answer: Anup Nair said volume growth was about 18-20% and the rest came from ASP and mix. The price rise was mainly in Q4. For FY27, ASP growth is about 25% and volume growth 25-30%.

risks_watch: Chip and memory supply: lead times are long, contracts are being invalidated under force majeure, and management says costs are rising every fortnight to week. Watch whether monthly price increases keep pace.

rows.why: Three new launches are planned in H1 FY27 (Aquaria and Trident this quarter, Sky Plaza in H1 with about 80% approvals), with three more H2 launches expected to get approvals in Q1 FY27, but Monarch, Avalon and Solana are delayed and the Ghatkopar matter is pending, so timing carries risk.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: FY27 pre-sales guided at INR1,800-2,000 crores versus INR1,157 crores in FY26 (about 55-73% growth), and revenue growth of 55-60% is guided, backed by six launches worth INR5,000-5,500 crores GDV, though collections of INR82 crores in Q4 against INR308 crores revenue show execution still lags.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management guided FY27 pre-sales of INR1,800-2,000 crores and revenue and PAT growth of 55-60%, with no sign of running ahead of this; Q4 PAT grew only 17% against 62% revenue growth, so there is no evidence yet of an upgrade.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Monarch, Avalon and Solana are delayed, Sky Plaza is only about 80% approved, and collections (INR82 crores in Q4, INR376 crores in FY26 against INR769 crores revenue) lag, so FY27 pre-sales of INR1,800-2,000 crores depend on launches that are not yet fully approved.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Six named launches (Aquaria, Trident, Aurelia, Sky Plaza, Portofino, Odyssey) with GDV INR5,000-5,500 crores, three of them in H1 FY27 with combined revenue potential of INR2,500-3,000 crores, and Aquaria and Trident already at approval stage with launches planned this quarter.

rows.label: Collections catch-up as new projects reach plinth
rows.why: Collections were INR82 crores in Q4 against INR308 crores revenue and INR376 crores for FY26 against INR769 crores, with management expecting improvement as the four new projects move from basement to plinth and superstructure.

rows.label: Ultra-luxury pricing premium of 10-20% (up to 25%)
rows.why: Management says pricing is 10-20% (up to 25%) above competitors in each micro market, with Lotus Celestia booking INR155 crores within 7 days of launch and Q4 pre-sales of INR462 crores.

rows.label: Ghatkopar matter at Supreme Court (about INR600 crores GDV)
rows.why: The matter is pending at the Supreme Court with an outcome expected this year, and it covers about INR600 crores of GDV that could be affected either way.

tone.note: Management was confident on ultra-luxury demand, pricing power and the INR1,800-2,000 crore FY27 pre-sales target, but was evasive on weak collections, approval delays for Monarch, Avalon and Solana, and the Ghatkopar matter, and gave little numerical detail on cost and margin impact.

544469|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 pre-sales rose 567% YoY to INR409 crores and PAT grew 77% to INR46 crores at a 34.5% margin.
544469|2026-06.overview: Sri Lotus reported strong Q1 FY27 growth: pre-sales INR409 crores, collections INR150 crores (+115% YoY), revenue INR132 crores (+116%), and EBITDA INR48 crores (36.4% margin). Management reiterated FY27 guidance of INR1,800-2,000 crores pre-sales and 55-60% revenue and PAT growth. A new Juhu commercial redevelopment (GDV about INR1,600 crores) was won, and the company reported a net cash balance sheet of INR623 crores. Q&A surfaced some inconsistencies on launch timing and the split of Q1 pre-sales between new and existing launches.

segments.name: Residential redevelopment (Mumbai ultra-luxury)
segments.commentary: Core focus; 17 of 22 pipeline projects are redevelopment-led. Management says micro-market pricing is 10-15% above other developers, with 5-10% price rises seen over the past year.

segments.name: Commercial
segments.commentary: Two commercial projects in the pipeline; Juhu commercial-cum-retail redevelopment (GDV about INR1,600 crores) won, expected to start next year after approvals and take 3-4 years to complete.

guidance_outlook: FY27 pre-sales guidance maintained at INR1,800-2,000 crores; management said it will 'easily achieve' INR1,800 crores.
FY27 revenue and PAT growth guidance of 55-60% maintained.
EBITDA margin guidance 35-40% and PAT margin 25-30% stated in the prepared remarks; in Q&A the CEO quoted EBITDA margin of 33-36%, a discrepancy.
FY27 cash collections target of about INR1,000 crores, supported by billing on Arcadian and Varun (each about 90% complete) and Amalfi (60-70%) by year-end.

Four further launches in FY27 with combined GDV of INR3,500-4,000 crores: Lotus Sky Plaza (Oshiwara, about INR1,500 crores, H1-end or early Q3), Lotus Odyssey (Bandstand, about INR1,000 crores, Q4), Lotus Portofino (Versova, about INR500 crores, within 3-4 months), Lotus Aurelia (Napean Sea Road, INR600-700 crores).
Gift City project: mixed-use approvals (commercial, retail, residential) expected by end-2026, with construction to start after approvals.
Promoter stake about 82%; management targets dilution to 75% or below within the remaining two years of a three-year window, with no investor discussions yet.
capex_capacity: Two projects launched in Q1 FY27: Lotus Trident (Andheri West) and Lotus Aquaria (Prabhadevi), together GDV of INR1,350 crores; Aquaria company GDV about INR800 crores (saleable, excluding tenant areas), starting price about INR85,000 per sq ft.
Varun: plinth just completed, about 20 slabs; RCC work targeted by January and 90% of work by March.
Arcadian and Varun targeted at 90% of project cost and Amalfi at 60-70% by end-FY27.

Juhu commercial redevelopment: plot over 5,000 sq m; start next year after plan approvals, 3-4 years to complete. Part of the area to be rehoused for existing tenants, remainder for commercial pipeline; no rental retention decided.
Of the INR550 crores earmarked for subsidiary projects (Amalfi, Arcadian, Varun), INR271 crores deployed as of 30 June 2026. Net IPO proceeds about INR732 crores after INR792 crores fresh issue.
demand_pricing: Q1 pre-sales of INR409 crores: management said only about INR25 crores came from the two new launches; the remainder came from projects launched in FY26 and earlier. Trident already reported about INR150 crores of sales within one month, in July-August.
Management said about INR400-plus crores of sales came from Trident, Aquaria and Celestia over the last two quarters.
Sales pace: 20-30% of inventory sold at launch, then about 30% of stock offloaded per year over a roughly three-year build cycle.
Brand campaign across 11 Mumbai coastal projects is ongoing; sales and marketing spend about 1% of pre-sales, which management expects to be offset by lower brokerage.
Management cited Mumbai luxury housing demand growth of more than 11% while the broader market moderated; constrained supply in Worli, Bandra and South Mumbai.
Versova: three existing sea-facing projects with more society talks under way.

qa_highlights.question: Can the INR409 crore pre-sales support the INR2,000 crore FY27 guidance, and what supports 55-60% growth?
qa_highlights.answer: CEO Sanjay Jain said the company is confident of easily achieving the INR1,800 crore pre-sales guidance, citing four new launches and strong response to Trident, Aquaria and Celestia.

qa_highlights.question: Timing and GDV of the upcoming launches?
qa_highlights.answer: Lotus Sky Plaza (Oshiwara, about INR1,500 crores) at H1-end or start of Q3; Lotus Odyssey (Bandstand, about INR1,000 crores) in Q4; Lotus Portofino (Versova, about INR500 crores) within 3-4 months; Lotus Aurelia (Napean Sea Road, INR600-700 crores).

qa_highlights.question: Juhu project details, margin and rental plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is more than 5,000 sq m plot in middle Juhu with existing shops and offices to be rehoused; no rental retention for this project. EBITDA around 40% and PAT 25-30% expected, which management said it will achieve or beat.

qa_highlights.question: Gap between Q1 pre-sales split and launch-driven sales?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO Rakesh Gupta said about INR25 crores came from the two new launches, with the balance from FY26 and earlier launches. The CEO had earlier cited Trident's INR150 crores within one month, which relates to July-August rather than Q1.

qa_highlights.question: Cash collection goal and EBITDA margin trajectory?
qa_highlights.answer: Collection target about INR1,000 crores this year as billing rises on Arcadian, Varun and Amalfi. CEO said EBITDA margin is in the 33-36% range, which differs from the 35-40% guidance in the prepared remarks.

qa_highlights.question: Price increases and premium versus peers?
qa_highlights.answer: Price rises of 5-10% over the past year. Pricing about 10-15% above other developers in the same micro-markets, per the CEO.

qa_highlights.question: Leverage plans and net worth?
qa_highlights.answer: Investment is about 10% of GDV in redevelopment. Management cited total GDV of about INR18,000 crores and net worth of about INR1,900 crores, with annual net worth additions expected.

qa_highlights.question: Promoter stake dilution timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Promoter stake about 82%; management said there are three years to reach 75% or below, with two years remaining, but no investor discussions yet.

risks_watch: Q1 pre-sales of INR409 crores is mostly from FY26-and-earlier launches (about INR25 crores from the two new launches per CFO), so FY27 guidance of INR1,800-2,000 crores relies on four launches totalling INR3,500-4,000 crores GDV landing on schedule.

Launch timing is inconsistent: Lotus Sky Plaza is guided to H1-end or start of Q3, Lotus Odyssey to Q4, and Portofino within 3-4 months; the answer on the number of FY27 launches also shifted between four and six projects in Q&A.
EBITDA margin guidance conflicts: prepared remarks say 35-40%, while the CEO cited 33-36% in Q&A; Juhu project margin was given as about 40% EBITDA. Track which range is reiterated next quarter.

Cash collection target of about INR1,000 crores depends on billing milestones on Arcadian and Varun (about 90% complete) and Amalfi (60-70%) by March 2027; Varun is only just past plinth with about 20 slabs done.

Juhu commercial redevelopment (GDV about INR1,600 crores) starts only after plan approvals next year, with 3-4 years to complete; Gift City mixed-use approvals are targeted by end-2026, and Lotus Monarch paperwork is still ongoing.

Pipeline GDV figures differ across answers (INR17,500-18,000 crores on the call versus about INR16,500-16,700 crores as of March plus INR1,600 crores Juhu); the promoter stake is about 82% with a 75% target within two years and no investor talks yet.
key_quotes: So, we are very confident that we will easily achieve the INR1,800 crores guidance.
So, this INR800 crore s is company part only. What we disclose as a GDV is our saleable portion only.
So, we have got total three years. One year has passed, so we have still two years to go.
544469|2026-06.management_tone: Confident and promotional on demand, pricing and the launch pipeline, with firm reiteration of FY27 guidance. Less precise under questioning: the CFO and CEO gave conflicting answers on the Q1 pre-sales split, launch count and EBITDA margin range, and several answers were corrected mid-stream.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Q1 EBITDA margin 36.4% and guidance of 35-40% in prepared remarks, but CEO cited 33-36% in Q&A, so the range is unsettled and the Juhu project is guided at about 40% EBITDA.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Four further launches worth INR3,500-4,000 crore GDV are planned, with Sky Plaza at H1-end or early Q3 (about INR1,500 crore), Odyssey in Q4 (about INR1,000 crore) and Portofino within 3-4 months (about INR500 crore); only about INR25 crore of Q1 pre-sales came from the two new launches.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: FY27 pre-sales guided at INR1,800-2,000 crore against INR409 crore in Q1, and revenue and PAT growth guided at 55-60%, with Q1 revenue up 116% YoY to INR132 crore.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Juhu redevelopment (GDV about INR1,600 crore) is won and starts after approvals next year, and Gift City approvals are targeted by end-2026, but no new capex quantum is stated and investment is about 10% of GDV in redevelopment.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management said it will 'easily achieve' INR1,800 crore pre-sales, but Q1 pre-sales were mostly from FY26-and-earlier launches, so an upgrade depends on launches landing and Trident's INR150 crore sales continuing.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Four launches totalling INR3,500-4,000 crore GDV must land on schedule, the launch count shifted between four and six in Q&A, and Varun is only just past plinth with about 20 slabs done against a January RCC target.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Four launches are guided (Sky Plaza, Odyssey, Portofino, Aurelia) with combined GDV of INR3,500-4,000 crore, though launch timing is inconsistent across answers.

rows.label: Juhu commercial redevelopment won (GDV about INR1,600 crore)
rows.when: start next year after approvals; 3-4 years to complete
rows.why: Project is won, but at 3-4 years to complete it adds little to revenue in the window and it starts only after plan approvals.

rows.label: Net cash INR623 crore; promoter stake dilution to 75% or below
rows.when: within two remaining years of three-year window
rows.why: Promoter stake is about 82% and the target is 75% or below, but management says there are no investor discussions yet.

rows.label: Brand campaign with lower brokerage offset
rows.why: Sales and marketing spend is about 1% of pre-sales, which management expects to be offset by lower brokerage, though no quantified saving is given.

tone.note: Management was confident on demand, pricing (10-15% premium, 5-10% price rises) and the launch pipeline, and reiterated FY27 guidance. Analysts and the answers exposed inconsistencies on the Q1 pre-sales split (only about INR25 crore from new launches), launch count and timing, and the EBITDA margin

544469|2026-09.headline: Q2 FY27 pre-sales rose 83% YoY to INR470 crore and EBITDA more than doubled to INR107 crore at a 39.9% margin.
544469|2026-09.overview: Management reported strong Q2 and H1 FY27 growth in pre-sales, revenue, EBITDA and PAT, with margins above 38%. Three redevelopment projects were added in the quarter, adding an estimated INR2,700-2,800 crore GDV, taking the pipeline to 24 projects and about INR20,000 crore GDV. Collections were weaker at INR60 crore in Q2 and INR209 crore in H1, which management attributed to construction-linked billing and expects to improve in H2. Analysts focused on collections, the INR300 crore business development outflow, Prabhadevi sales traction and project timeline slippage.

segments.name: Lotus Trident (Andheri West, luxury commercial)
segments.commentary: Contributed INR178 crore pre-sales in its first full quarter after end-June launch, about 35% of sales sold within three months per management. Management guided EBITDA margin of 33-35%.

segments.name: Residential luxury projects
segments.commentary: Celestia reported 36% sales within six months of launch. Lotus Aquaria (Prabhadevi) reported healthy inquiries, but Lotus Prabhadevi (GDV ~INR800 crore) contributed no pre-sales in Q2.

guidance_outlook: FY27 pre-sales guidance reiterated at INR1,800-2,000 crore.
FY27 revenue and PAT growth guided at 55-60% over FY26.
FY27 EBITDA margin guided at 35-40% and PAT margin at 25-30%.
Four H2 FY27 launches planned: Lotus Aurelia, Lotus Sky Plaza, Lotus Portofino and Lotus Odyssey, combined GDV INR3,500-4,000 crore; about 90% approvals in place.
Project-level surplus estimated at about INR9,500 crore over the development cycle; projects expected to complete over the next 4-4.5 years.
Management expects H2 collections to be much better than H1 as projects reach plinth level; FY28 collection guidance to be given at the start of FY28.
Amara and Athena expected to receive OC in FY27 (Amara within the quarter or by March; Athena before March).
capex_capacity: Pipeline of 24 ongoing and upcoming projects, aggregate GDV ~INR20,000 crore, of which 19 are redevelopment-led.
Business development: Lotus Impressa (Shivaji Park, Dadar West), Lotus Stellar (Versova) and Lotus Supremus (Juhu) added in Q2.
INR550 crore of IPO proceeds earmarked for subsidiary (Amalfi, Arcadian, Varun); INR305 crore deployed as of 30 Sep 2026 of INR732 crore net proceeds.
Upfront premium paid to government for new projects in Q2, which management said is to save costs and secure supplier discounts; new projects typically need 8-10% of project cost to start.
GIFT City plot of 5.5 acres on Sabarmati riverfront; expected 1.3-1.5 million sq ft mixed-use development subject to town planning scheme approval.
Lotus Monarch timeline pushed out by one year due to society, trust, Charity Commissioner and government approvals; Ghatkopar (Salona) timeline also extended.
demand_pricing: Management says the luxury segment is less sensitive to RBI's 25 bps repo hike to 5.5% (first hike since early 2023); buyers rely less on home loans.
Mumbai H1 CY2026 sales of homes priced above INR10 crore reached a record INR18,500 crore; prime residential prices up 6.2% YoY per management.
Management says prices have risen across almost all projects in H1 and will rise further as construction progresses if the market supports it.
Management says it is the only suburban player to have completed a commercial redevelopment (Arc One), and has 2-3 more commercial redevelopment projects; about five commercial projects in portfolio.
Prabhadevi (Lotus Aquaria) pricing set at a premium, with 270-degree sea view and ~200 m Art Deco tower; management says no pushback, pre-sales expected to show in next two quarters.
Collections as a share of pre-sales: management said completion-stage projects carry 90-95% balance due, and expects 95-100% collection on three projects completing next year.

qa_highlights.question: How sustainable are margins above 35% during expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited net debt-free status (no interest burden), minimal marketing spend, a 2.5-3.5 year project cycle that speeds fund deployment, and premium pricing.

qa_highlights.question: What EBITDA margin is expected for Trident and what is the commercial redevelopment outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO guided Trident EBITDA margin at 33-35%, in line with guidance. Management expects commercial redevelopment to carry sustainable margins and cited 2-3 more projects.

qa_highlights.question: How will collections catch up with pre-sales?
qa_highlights.answer: CEO said collections are construction-linked: about 5-10% at launch and about 25% at plinth. Of about INR800 crore H1 pre-sales, INR200 crore was collected, and H2 should improve as two of three recent projects move past basement.

qa_highlights.question: Medium-term growth beyond FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management gives annual guidance only. It pointed to ~INR20,000 crore GDV and ~INR9,500 crore project surplus, with completion over the next 4-4.5 years.

qa_highlights.question: Why did timelines shift for upcoming projects?
qa_highlights.answer: Lotus Monarch moved out by one year due to multiple approving bodies. Ghatkopar (Salona) timeline also extended. Management says overall guidance is unchanged and new projects will replace slipped ones.

qa_highlights.question: Why no Prabhadevi pre-sales, and will the business development outflow constrain the company?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Prabhadevi is a new micromarket with marketing under way and results expected in two quarters. The INR300 crore outflow was upfront government fees and discounted supplier payments; management said cash is sufficient. Operating cash flow will stay negative in launch periods, though Arcadian is working-capital positive.

risks_watch: Collections lag: Q2 collections of INR60 crore and H1 of INR209 crore against H1 pre-sales of about INR800-879 crore; track whether H2 collections rise as two of three recent projects move past basement to plinth.

Timeline slippage: Lotus Monarch pushed out by one year (society, trust, Charity Commissioner, government approvals) and Ghatkopar (Salona) extended; watch whether replacement projects keep FY27 guidance intact.

Cash deployment: INR305 crore of INR732 crore IPO net proceeds deployed by 30 Sep 2026; management says operating cash flow may stay negative in launch periods, with no FY28 collection guidance until start of FY28.
Prabhadevi (Lotus Aquaria, GDV ~INR800 crore) had no Q2 pre-sales; management expects results in next two quarters at a premium price point.
Delivery of four H2 FY27 launches (combined GDV INR3,500-4,000 crore, about 90% approvals) and the FY27 pre-sales guidance of INR1,800-2,000 crore versus H1 INR879 crore.
key_quotes: Delighted to share that we recorded pre-sales for the quarter at INR470 crores, up 83% year-on-year.
Collections in our business are linked to construction milestones and can vary from quarter -to-quarter.
So, right now, it's not a good time to because we need to evaluate and update you.
So, project-wise, yes, but overall, maybe we cannot give that.
544469|2026-09.management_tone: Confident on sales, margins and launch plans, with the CEO and CFO more cautious and non-committal on collection timing, FY28 numbers and operating cash flow, deferring to the start of FY28 or project-level answers. Management repeatedly stressed the net debt-free balance sheet and construction-linked billing as the reason collections trail pre-sales.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Q2 EBITDA margin was 39.9% and H1 38.8%, against FY27 guidance of 35-40%; management cites net debt-free status, minimal marketing spend and premium pricing, while Trident is guided at 33-35%, which dilutes the blend.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: No unit capacity is measured for a developer; the four H2 FY27 launches (combined GDV INR3,500-4,000 crore, about 90% approvals) and the 24-project pipeline (~INR20,000 crore GDV) are the closest equivalent, but Lotus Monarch slipped one year and GIFT City is subject to town planning approval.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Pre-sales grew 83% YoY in Q2 to INR470 crore and 176% in H1 to INR879 crore, and FY27 revenue and PAT growth of 55-60% is held, with Trident contributing INR178 crore in its first full quarter; Lotus Prabhadevi (GDV ~INR800 crore) has yet to contribute pre-sales.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Three redevelopment projects were added in Q2 and INR305 crore of INR732 crore IPO proceeds is deployed, so further business development is likely but no new capex plan with a date was stated; utilisation is not disclosed.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management reiterated all FY27 guidance rather than raising it, and the H2 ramp required to hit pre-sales of INR1,800-2,000 crore leaves little room for an upgrade.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: H1 pre-sales of INR879 crore against FY27 guidance of INR1,800-2,000 crore requires a steep H2 ramp, collections were only INR209 crore in H1, and Lotus Monarch and Ghatkopar timelines have slipped.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Four launches are planned for H2 FY27 (Lotus Aurelia, Lotus Sky Plaza, Lotus Portofino, Lotus Odyssey) with combined GDV of INR3,500-4,000 crore and about 90% approvals in place.

rows.label: Collections lag pre-sales; H2 collections expected to improve
rows.why: Collections were INR60 crore in Q2 and INR209 crore in H1 against H1 pre-sales of about INR800-879 crore, and management expects H2 to be much better as projects reach plinth, with about 25% collected at plinth.

rows.label: Net debt-free with INR494 crore net cash
rows.why: Net cash position of INR494 crore at 30 Sep 2026 with the IPO proceeds still INR427 crore undeployed (INR732 crore less INR305 crore).

rows.label: Amara and Athena receive OC in FY27
rows.why: Management expects Amara (within the quarter or by March) and Athena (before March) to receive occupancy certificate, which would convert completed projects into revenue recognition and collections of 95-100% on three completing projects.

tone.note: Management was confident on pre-sales, margins and the four H2 launches, and cautious or deferred on collection timing, FY28 numbers and operating cash flow; analysts probed collections, the INR300 crore business development outflow, Prabhadevi sales traction and timeline slippage.

544470|2026-03.headline: M&B Engineering FY26 revenue rose 27% to INR1,259.7 crores, but Q4 EBITDA margin fell to 11.9% on forex loss and steel/freight costs; no margin guidance given.
544470|2026-03.overview: FY26 revenue grew 27% to INR1,260 crores and PAT rose 20% to INR92.6 crores, but Q4 revenue (INR364 crores, +16%) saw EBITDA flat at INR43 crores and margin down to 11.9% from 14%. Management attributed the margin squeeze to a INR3.9 crore Q4 forex loss (mostly unrealised translation), a 20%+ jump in domestic steel prices, and sharply higher export freight after the Iran conflict; it says adjusted EBITDA excluding forex is about 13%. Volume growth in Phenix was only about 8% in Q4 versus an expected ~15%, due to raw material and gas disruptions in March. Management guided top-line growth of 23-25% for FY27 but declined to give margin guidance.

segments.name: Phenix (PEB)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR985 crores, +29%; export revenue INR165.6 crores. Order book INR871 crores, of which export INR279 crores (32%). Sanand plant utilisation ~75-76% in FY26.

segments.name: Proflex (self-supported roofing)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR275 crores, +23%. Order book INR212 crores. One new unit from UAE commissioned January 2026; two US units expected Q2 FY27.

guidance_outlook: FY27 top-line growth guided at around 25%; management later cited a 23-25% range, and 20-25% volume growth in PEB and Proflex.
No EBITDA margin guidance for FY27: management cited steel price volatility, uncertain freight, FX and the conflict; will reassess after at least one more quarter.
FY27 export target about INR275-300 crores (around 10,000 tons vs 7,400 tons in FY26); export EBITDA expected 16-17% vs 10-11% domestic at current cost structure.
H1 FY27 expected softer due to Q1 labour availability and Q2 monsoon; H2 historically stronger.
FY27 capex about INR100 crores, including Sanand expansion, part Cheyyar expansion (H2) and maintenance capex.
US sectoral tariff reduced by 25% (effective 6 April per management); benefit partly shared with customers under contract clauses.
capex_capacity: Sanand: adding about 20,000 MT, commissioning expected Q2 FY27, taking capacity to 92,000 MTPA; utilisation expected 65-68% after expansion, peak 75%.
Cheyyar (Tamil Nadu): FY26 utilisation 50-55%; target 68-70% in FY27, with 75% as peak; expansion planned to be operational Q1 or Q2 FY28.
Proflex: installed capacity to rise by about 200,000 sq m p.a. once two US units are commissioned in Q2 FY27.
Volume targets FY27: PEB 85,000-90,000 MT (from ~72,000); Proflex 1.70-1.725 million sq m.
IPO proceeds INR259.32 crores; INR137.81 crores (53%) utilised to 31 March 2026, INR7.5 crores in Q4.
demand_pricing: Order inflow Q4 about INR387-388 crores, down from INR480 crores in Q3 (per analyst); FY26 record inflow INR1,539 crores.
Bid pipeline cited at about INR1,000-1,100 crores across sectors; domestic inquiries in last three months exceeded the prior remaining part of the year.
Export order closures slowing: US cycle time rose from 6-8 weeks to 12-16 weeks amid US inflation and cost pressures.

Steel prices rose about 20%+ in the last quarter (cited INR49,500/t to INR58,500/t); fixed-price contracts with 6-12 month execution; 80-85% of raw material is covered at order booking, 15-20% left open for non-standard items.
New orders being quoted at higher prices; price not locked until advance received. Export freight: a USD 2,000 war surcharge added; cushion built into quotes.
Export realisation about INR2.3-2.7 lakh/t vs domestic about half, driven by US bought-out items costing INR1-2 lakh/t and freight/duties.

qa_highlights.question: How do you see FY27 EBITDA margins given the geopolitical situation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to guide, citing steel price swings (+20% in a quarter), uncertain freight and FX; it will wait at least one more quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What is the export outlook and pipeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Export target at least INR300 crores in FY27 (vs INR165 crores) per Malav Patel; later cited INR275-300 crores and about 10,000 tonnes; US order closures have slowed.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q4 volumes grow only ~8% vs ~15% expected?
qa_highlights.answer: Raw material and steel mill disruptions in March (two major suppliers shut, gas shortages); management estimated 10-15% volume lost to the war.

qa_highlights.question: Are there any signs of demand slowdown in PEB?

544482|2026-03.headline: FY26 revenue rose 6% to INR88.5 crore and EBITDA 17% to INR33.2 crore (37.5% margin), with management guiding 25-30% growth for FY27.

Management attributed the weak top-line to regulatory delays (PNDT, AERB) on new centre openings and said these are now resolved, backing 25-30% growth in FY27. 544484|2026-03.headline: BlueStone Q4 FY26 standalone revenue grew 49.1% YoY; SSG of 34% and FY26 revenue of INR 2,441 crore, with 340 stores after 65 added in FY26.
544484|2026-03.overview: Management reported Q4 FY26 standalone revenue up 49.1% YoY and FY26 revenue of INR 2,441 crore, with same-store sales growth of 34% spread evenly across all three months. The store base reached 340 stores in 134 cities after adding 17 stores in Q4 and 65 in FY26, below the 83 added in FY25 and below the RHP plan of 290 stores over FY26-FY27. Management said pre-Ind AS EBITDA margins improved YoY despite a mix shift toward plain gold, and attributed the recovery to rapid entry-level repricing and vertical integration. Gold price inflation inflated closing inventory, which pushed inventory turns down to about 1.13x from 1.3x in FY25.

544484|2026-06.headline: BlueStone Q1 FY27 revenue rose 49% YoY to INR 733 crore, with pre-Ind AS EBITDA up 135% to INR 55 crore and margin at 7.5%.
544484|2026-06.overview: Revenue grew 49% YoY to INR 733 crore and pre-Ind AS EBITDA rose 135% to INR 55 crore, lifting operating margin to 7.5% (up 273 bps). Management attributed this to operating leverage despite a custom duty hike on gold from 6% to 15% that softened demand in May before June and July recovered. Same-store sales growth was 39%, repeat revenue share rose to about 60%, while new customer additions reportedly fell from about 50,000 to about 40,000 per quarter, which management tied to merchandise dislocation during the sharp gold rise. Management reiterated a long-term target of roughly INR 12,000 crore revenue in four years, around 30% SSSG and about 20% store distribution growth, though analysts questioned the arithmetic.

qa_highlights.answer: Management acknowledged the drop, attributed it to merchandise dislocation being fixed, and said month-on-month new customer trends are improving.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 30% refers to mature-cohort SSSG at maturity (years 3-6), not reported SSSG, and that reported SSSG would be higher due to new stores.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said mix changes in studded share were not material; contribution margin, the more relevant metric, has been largely stable, and EBITDA expansion comes from operating leverage.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said most operating leverage comes from corporate and marketing scale rather than store-level profit, so faster distribution growth is preferred.

qa_highlights.answer: Marketing was about INR 50 crore, 6.9% of revenue, same as last year; it fell from about 9.2% four years ago to 6.6% in FY26.

rows.why: Modified starch trials (cationic, carboxymethyl, pre-gel, spray) to be fully online by September 2026 with 70-80% of volume to existing paper and food customers; Dextrose Anhydrous, Monohydrate and Hydrol expected by about Q4 FY27.

rows.label: Working capital and debt peak then decline
rows.why: CFO said debt peaks in H1 FY27 as working capital is highest, with working capital debt expected to fall in H2 (management cited a prior ~40% reduction by Q4); net debt is Rs 735.32 cr and CCC is 130 days.

rows.label: Bihar interest subvention cap Rs 40 cr pending
rows.why: Subvention cap reportedly amended to Rs 40 cr but final notification awaited; accounts still apply Rs 20 cr cap; FY27 net interest guided at Rs 39-40 cr, flat vs FY26.

rows.label: Export and new-region expansion
rows.why: Export share of revenue rose to 10.4% from 4.9% in Q1 FY26, and management says new markets in South and West India are being developed, though no export target was given.

tone.note: Management was confident on the doubled capacity, export growth and the FY27 crushing volume of 4 lakh tons, but cautious on numbers: it declined to give EBITDA per ton, margin, export targets or FY28 capacity plans, and analysts pushed on margin visibility and the ramp-up.

544485|2026-09.headline: Regaal Resources posted record Q2 FY27 PAT of ₹232 million (+38.7% YoY), with EBITDA margin at 17.1%.
544485|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 manufacturing revenue rose about 64% YoY to ₹3,141 million, and value add rose 64.3% to ₹1,290 million at a 40.8% value-add margin. Operating EBITDA grew 54.7% to ₹542 million, and PAT reached a record ₹232 million at a 7.3% margin. Maize crushing volume was 90,489 MT, up 32% YoY, despite a roughly one-month disruption after damage to a 10 MW turbine at the newly commissioned A25 facility, which has since been recommissioned. Net debt rose to ₹8,808 million on working capital build-up from advance maize procurement, which management expects to unwind over the next two quarters.

financial_highlights.change: +64% YoY vs ₹1,916 million in Q2 FY26

financial_highlights.value: ₹5,357 million term loan; ₹3,506 million working capital

segments.name: Co-manufacturing / manufacturing
segments.commentary: Manufacturing revenue ₹3,141 million, up 64% YoY; crushing 90,489 MT in Q2, up 32% YoY. Products include starch, gluten/feed, germ, fibre and liquid glucose.

segments.name: Trading (maize)
segments.commentary: Management said trading sales in Q2 FY26 were negligible; in Q2 FY27 trading sales were about ₹127 million against ₹1,927 million manufacturing (described as opportunistic, low margin around 5-6%).

segments.name: Value-added products (dextrose, modified starch, CMS, oxidised starch)
segments.commentary: Liquid glucose and dextrose powder lines commissioned; modified starch line started. Value-added share guided at 10-11% in FY27 and 20-23% in FY28 (excluding liquid glucose).

guidance_outlook: Interest cost for FY27 guided at about ₹40-42 crore (H1 at ₹20-22 crore); management said it will not exceed budget.
H2 FY27 crushing guided at about 2,040,000 MT, implying FY27 volume of about 4,040,000 MT.
FY28 crushing guided at 525,000-550,000 MT.
Working capital debt expected to fall materially by March 2027 as inventory is consumed; CWIP-linked term loans to be repaid as projects complete.
Starch-linked sustainable margin framed at about ₹4,500/MT; Q2 EBITDA per tonne about ₹6,000 and H1 about ₹5,300 per tonne.
Maize inventory covers H2 requirements (about 90% in plant), with stock expected to last to about mid-March 2027.
Value-added capex about 27.5% (approx. ₹275 crore) yet to be capitalised; additional 1.6 MW power plant using methane from effluent treatment planned; DMSO-type product planned around FY28.
capex_capacity: Crushing capacity expanded to 1,650 MT/day; operating at 1,500-1,575 MT/day in the recent period, with 1,600 MT/day achieved per management.
A25 facility's 10 MW turbine damaged in Q2, causing about one month's closure; recommissioned and now fully operational.
Liquid glucose and dextrose powder lines commissioned; modified starch (CMS, oxidised starch) started, with sampling and customer approvals underway.
Around 65% of planned capex is said to be already deployed, with the balance (roughly ₹275 crore) to be capitalised in FY27-FY28.
Land: about 70 acres signed with farmers; 57 acres of land said to be vacant at the Bihar site for future expansion.
demand_pricing: Maize prices up about 50% from ₹10 to ₹15/kg (per management) over the period; starch realisations about ₹49-51/kg, germ ₹83 from ₹60, fibre ₹23 from ₹16, and gluten ₹64-65 from ₹60.
Management said order intake reached about 150% of target and prices were being raised again after the call.
Exports about 10% of starch and fibre volumes; management cited tapioca starch at about $700/t.
Distributor sales reduced significantly; management prioritises dealer/retail channels.
GST recovery from distributors: about 60% recovered, with the balance expected by December 2026.
Average realisation for the quarter about ₹35/kg per management.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the Q2 EBITDA margin improvement?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited higher capacity lowering fixed cost per tonne, higher conversion spread, higher selling prices, and new export markets.

qa_highlights.question: Will the working capital debt come down over the next two quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said working capital debt will fall by March as the high-cost maize inventory is consumed; interest cost is expected to stay within the ₹40-42 crore budget.

qa_highlights.question: What are FY27 H2 volume targets?
qa_highlights.answer: H2 crushing guided at about 2,040,000 MT, giving FY27 total of about 4,040,000 MT; management said the turbine outage cost about 20,000 MT.

qa_highlights.question: How sustainable is the margin when maize costs rise?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the current maize inventory was bought at about ₹30-31/kg versus about ₹34 cost, with starch at ₹49-51/kg; sustainability was framed around ₹4,500/MT, but no firm guidance was given beyond FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Are there further capex plans beyond the current expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: Focus is on stabilising current capacity; a 1.6 MW methane-based power plant and an additional product are planned, with timing around FY28.

qa_highlights.question: What is the trading share and long-term intent?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said trading is opportunistic (about ₹8.5 crore in October) and not a long-term vision.

risks_watch: Maize procurement cost reset: Q3-Q4 inventory bought at about ₹30-31/kg is being consumed, with fresh procurement expected to be at higher prices from mid-March 2027.
Value-added ramp: management said real value-add data will only show in Q3 and full picture in Q4; customer approvals still in progress.
Ethanol-linked maize diversion and crop shortfalls in some states may tighten availability, per management.
Execution risk: earlier turbine failure shows plant reliability risk at the new A25 facility.
Debt reduction and interest cost trajectory against guidance of ₹40-42 crore for FY27 (H1 at ₹20-22 crore).
544485|2026-09.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on volumes, margins and debt reduction, but evasive on specific value-add figures, margin sustainability and future capex, deferring details to later quarters. Several answers were vague or contradictory on figures (for example, the balance of value-added capex and the margin-per-tonne basis), so the numbers should be verified against the filings.
key_quotes: We also achieved our highest ever quarterly profit after tax of 232 million, accompanied by a record path margin of 7.3%.
The turbine has been successfully recommissioned and the facility is now fully operational.
As the inventory is progressively consumed over the next two quarters, working capital requirements and associated borrowings are expected to moderate.
It will whatever we had given you basically think guidance can be this 40, 40, 42, 38 whatever we have told you it will be staying there.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Q2 EBITDA ~Rs 6,000/t vs H1 ~Rs 5,300/t and sustainable starch margin framed at ~Rs 4,500/t; maize inventory bought at Rs 30-31/kg vs ~Rs 34 cost, but fresh procurement expected at higher prices from mid-March 2027, so margin expansion is likely to be uneven and not firmly guided.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Balance ~Rs 275 crore (~27.5%) of value-added capex is under construction and to be capitalised in FY27-FY28, with crushing capacity already at 1,650 MT/day and running 1,500-1,575 MT/day (~1,600 achieved), so ~5-10% headroom is used up soon after.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management guides H2 FY27 crushing ~2,040,000 MT (FY27 ~4,040,000 MT) and FY28 525,000-550,000 MT, but Q2's 90,489 MT already includes a turbine outage costing ~20,000 MT and no firm order book figures were given.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation is at roughly 1,500-1,600 MT/day against 1,650 MT/day capacity (~90%+) with a 1.6 MW methane power plant and a DMSO-type product planned around FY28, but management deferred further capex detail to later quarters and said focus is on stabilising current capacity.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY27 crushing guide was raised to ~4.04m t and management said order intake reached ~150% of target and prices are being raised again, but H1 value-add data only shows in Q3 and Q4.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Maize cost reset from mid-March 2027, ethanol-linked diversion and state-level crop shortfalls may tighten availability, and A25 turbine failure (about one month closure, ~20,000 MT lost) shows plant reliability risk.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Modified starch (CMS, oxidised starch) line is in trial runs with customer approvals underway, and liquid glucose and dextrose powder lines are already commissioned, but value-add revenue only shows from Q3 and the full picture in Q4.

rows.label: Working capital debt unwind by March 2027
rows.why: Net debt rose to Rs 8,808 million on advance maize buying (Rs 3,506 million working capital debt) and management expects it to fall as inventory is consumed, with cash conversion cycle already down to 123 days from 130.

rows.label: Price increases after the call
rows.why: Management said prices were being raised again after the call and order intake reached ~150% of target, with starch realisations ~Rs 49-51/kg and maize up ~50% from Rs 10 to Rs 15/kg.

rows.label: Export expansion
rows.why: Exports are only ~10% of starch and fibre volumes, and management cited new export markets and tapioca starch at ~$700/t as a supportive price reference, but no export target was given.

tone.note: Management was confident on volumes, margins and debt reduction and on order intake, but evasive on value-add figures, margin sustainability beyond FY28 and further capex; analysts pushed on margin per tonne basis and the balance of value-added capex.

544487|2026-03.headline: Patel Retail Q4 FY26 PAT rose 39.07% YoY to INR9.98 crore on 53.35% higher income, but EBITDA margin fell to 6.70% as new-store costs hit.
544487|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 total income rose 53.35% YoY to INR339.55 crore, with EBITDA up 31.21% to INR22.74 crore and PAT up 39.07% to INR9.98 crore. FY26 total income crossed INR1,000 crore at INR1,059.29 crore (+28.25%), with PAT up 54.48% to INR39.05 crore and PAT margin at 3.69%. Management attributed the weak Q4 EBITDA margin to upfront costs of new stores and said revenue ramp-up would come in FY27. Analyst questions focused on falling same-store sales (~5%), gross margin compression, a sizeable other-income (FX gain) contribution, and inventory and receivables build-up; several answers were incomplete or inconsistent.

segments.name: Retail
segments.commentary: 51 stores after Rasayani opening in April 2026 (over 2.29 lakh sq ft); 50th store at Thakurli in Q4. Retail sales INR429 crore in FY26; management cited retail EBITDA margin of 7-8% and gross margin of 14-15%, and retail contributes about 35-38% of PAT excluding other income.

segments.name: Manufacturing and processing (B2B)
segments.commentary: Ambernath and Kutch capacity over 1.47 lakh MTPA; utilisation 50-55% vs 45-48% earlier. Management cited about INR618 crore manufacturing and processing sales in FY26, of which about INR319 crore exports; gross margin guided at 16-17% (FY27: 18-20%). Management put manufacturing EBITDA margin at roughly 6.5-7%.

segments.name: Private label / own brands
segments.commentary: Own brands (Indian Chaska, Patel Fresh, Blue Nation, Patel Essentials) are about 17.5% of retail sales; own brands reportedly carry 30-35% operating margins per management, with non-branded gross margin of 15-16%. Indian Chaska distribution covers six states, with MP and Delhi in progress.

guidance_outlook: FY27 EBITDA margin guided at approximately 8-9%.
Gross margin guided at 15-20% overall; FY27 mix expected at 18-20% for B2B and 15-16% for retail.
Management expects double-digit revenue growth in FY27, with 'higher side' at 20% and above, but declined to disclose numbers formally.
Plans to open 8-10 stores a year, with focus on western suburbs and PCMC; possible Gujarat entry. Management said 52 stores as of the call date and seven or eight more expected in FY27.
Management expects positive operating cash flow by H1 FY27 as inventory normalises.
Management expects PAT margin to increase, and expects manufacturing utilisation to rise.
capex_capacity: Manufacturing capacity at Ambernath and Kutch exceeds 1.47 lakh MTPA; utilisation 50-55%, up 4-5 percentage points.
Retail network 51 stores, over 2.29 lakh sq ft; management carries about INR2,000-2,500 inventory per sq ft at store level.
Distribution centre in the cluster holds an additional INR15-20 crore of inventory per management.
Plans to start whole spices in the month of the call, then seasonings, pastes, snacks, and noodles or pasta depending on distribution.
Automation investment planned to improve productivity and cost efficiency.
demand_pricing: Same-store sales growth around 5%; management said mature stores grow 5-6%, versus analyst's recollection of 8-10%.
Grocery and staples are about 68-70% of retail revenue.
Export order book held at INR50-100 crore per management; current export order book figure not provided on the call.
Exports to Sri Lanka, Middle East, Europe, US, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, with African markets being pursued; management says 35+ countries.
Other income of about INR5 crore in Q4 is mainly FX gain on export receivables; management said INR8-9 crore per year is typical and expected to keep rising.
Management said commodity prices have peaked and are declining, and expects inventory gains from raw material procured at competitive prices.

qa_highlights.question: Why did same-store sales appear to slow from 8-10% to about 5%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 5% is good for mature stores, cited no specific reason, and said most revenue comes from grocery and staples (68-70%).

qa_highlights.question: Why did inventory and working capital rise so much?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said incremental working capital was funded from IPO proceeds (INR115 crore deployed into working capital). Management also cited export order book, transit times, and mixed shipments; the exact export order book was not disclosed on the call.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the Q4 margin decline and gross margin fall from about 20% to 14.5%?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO attributed Q4 margin pressure to upfront costs of new stores, and said it is temporary. He did not separately quantify the gross margin decline; management said the West Asia situation had not been the primary factor.

qa_highlights.question: What is the nature of the other income and is it recurring?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said other income is mainly FX gain on export receivables, about INR8-9 crore a year, and expected to keep rising. Management did not explain why the Q4 figure was about INR5 crore or why the gain would be recurring.

qa_highlights.question: Why is retail inventory at about INR90 crore, above the INR55-58 crore implied by store-level inventory per sq ft?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the difference reflects a cluster distribution centre (INR15-20 crore) and category-level inventory days, including about three months of spices stock and three to four months for plastic and steel, with festive stock also included.

qa_highlights.question: Why did receivables rise from INR125 crore to INR161-162 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said about 90% of receivables are less than six months old. He did not explain the increase.

risks_watch: Same-store sales growth of about 5% versus the 8-10% the analyst cited previously; management did not give a clear reason for the slowdown.
Gross margin fell sharply in Q4 (analyst cited about 14.5% versus about 20% a year earlier); management has not quantified the cause.
Other income (FX gain) of about INR5 crore in Q4 is a large share of PAT growth; the analyst argued that excluding it would show a decline.
Inventory (INR259-260 crore) and receivables (INR161-162 crore) rose sharply; management guided to positive operating cash flow only by H1 FY27.
Middle East and West Asia disruption may hit export volumes; management said it is pushing domestic sales to compensate.
DGFT wheat flour export scheme is policy-dependent; management said it does not rely on it fully.
Several Q&A answers were inconsistent or incomplete, including the export order book, the margin split between B2B and B2C, and the retail gross margin figures.
544487|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on growth and capacity plans, with management repeatedly calling Q4 margin dip temporary. Evasive on specifics: declined to give the export order book, FY27 revenue numbers, and the cause of the gross margin fall, and several answers were contradictory on margin and sales-mix figures.
key_quotes: So, in Q4, we have incurred the initial cost and the revenue is likely to be generated into fiscal '26-'27.
We have already achieved the debt-equity ratio to 0.34 from 1.34 in the fiscal '26.
Hitesh Sawlani: Higher side double-digit growth, you can say 20% and above.
We don't want to dump our goods and go wide and deep.

rows.why: Q4 EBITDA margin fell to 6.70% and gross margin dropped from about 20% to 14.5% (analyst figure) with no quantified cause, and positive operating cash flow is only promised by H1 FY27 against INR259-260 crore inventory and INR161-162 crore receivables.

rows.why: Management expects inventory to normalise and guided positive operating cash flow by H1 FY27, versus inventory of INR259-260 crore and receivables up from INR125 crore to INR161-162 crore.

rows.why: Gujarat entry is only a possibility and African markets are being pursued, with exports already in 35+ countries and FY26 exports of about INR319 crore out of INR618 crore manufacturing sales; no order numbers were disclosed.

544487|2026-06.headline: Patel Retail Q1 FY27 total income rose 69.35% YoY to INR310.24 crores, but EBITDA margin fell to about 6.3% on raw material intensity.
544487|2026-06.overview: Total income reached INR310.24 crores, up 69.35% YoY from INR183.19 crores, while EBITDA grew 23.92% to INR19.68 crores and PAT rose 37.43% to INR9.52 crores (EPS INR2.85). Management attributed the margin compression (about 133 bps decline cited, and a 233 bps figure also mentioned) to a higher raw-material-intensity mix in manufacturing, export and commodity-linked business amid volatile raw material prices and odd order timing. The company added stores at Rasayani and Babgaon in Q1 and opened its 53rd store at Uran (Raigad) after quarter-end, and expanded Indian Chaska into Madhya Pradesh. Management guided to positive operating cash flow by H1 FY27 and 8 to 10 new stores in FY27.

financial_highlights.change: +69.35% YoY vs INR183.19 crores in Q1 FY26
decline of 133 bps as stated (233 bps also cited in same answer)

financial_highlights.value: around INR101 crores (as referenced by analyst)

financial_highlights.metric: Private label contribution to retail sales

segments.name: Retail (Patel R-Mart)
segments.commentary: 53 stores after Uran opening; average monthly sales per store put at INR80 lakh to INR1 crore, mature-store sales about INR20,000 per sq ft; ticket size INR500 to INR1,000; wastage below 0.1%. Payback about 24 months.

segments.name: Manufacturing / food processing
segments.commentary: Utilisation currently 50% to 55%, targeted at around 80% to 82% by FY27-FY28; automation expected to cut labour cost and improve quality consistency. Private label share of domestic sales cited at 45%, export sales at 37%.

segments.name: Exports and B2B
segments.commentary: Management stated about 40% of revenue from exports and rest from manufacturing and retail; export contribution to bottom line cited as 35% to 40%. These figures were not reconciled in the call.

segments.name: Indian Chaska (brand)
segments.commentary: Expanded to Madhya Pradesh in August 2026, taking presence to eight states and one union territory; MP averaging INR10 lakh to INR12 lakh per month; whole spices category to be added this quarter.

segments.name: Online / quick commerce
segments.commentary: App has more than 50,000 downloads but online sales were around INR50 lakh in Q1; private label not yet listed on Blinkit or Zepto, with per-SKU terms being finalised; pilot quick commerce running from first stores.

segments.name: Apparel and fashion (general merchandise)
segments.commentary: 8% to 9% of revenue; inventory holding period 15 to 20 days.

guidance_outlook: EBITDA margin expected to move back toward 8% to 9% over coming quarters, with margin in Q1 not treated as steady state.
Positive operating cash flow expected by H1 FY27; conversion of current assets built up in FY26 into cash targeted.
8 to 10 new stores targeted by FY27, each expected to generate about INR1 crore per month in revenue.
Capacity utilisation targeted at around 80% to 82% by end-FY27 to FY28.
Expansion into Western suburbs and Pune/PCMC over the next five years, cluster-based; more gaps still being identified.
capex_capacity: Current processing utilisation 50% to 55%; medium-term target 80% to 82%.
New store payback about 24 months to recover capex and inventory rotation; store size and investment about 5,000 to 6,000 per sq ft as stated.
Automation being introduced at processing facilities, aimed at labour cost reduction and unified quality.
Store additions in Q1 at Rasayani and Babgaon; Uran (53rd store) opened after quarter-end.
Pune/PCMC store economics said to be broadly similar to existing network; 2 to 3 pockets identified.
demand_pricing: Management attributed Q1 margin decline to higher raw material intensity in export and commodity-linked business and volatile raw material prices.
Mature-store sales about INR20,000 per sq ft (retail); average monthly sales per store INR80 lakh to INR1 crore.
Online remains touch-and-feel in Tier-2/3/4 locations; society-focused activation and 30-60 minute delivery trials underway.
Private label planned as combo packs (e.g., rice, dal, salt) to make per-SKU listing and ad costs sustainable on quick commerce.
Plans to launch 2 to 3 more Indian Chaska categories (e.g., protein-related) from next quarter, targeting categories with INR2,000 to 3,000 crore market size.

qa_highlights.question: What must improve to move EBITDA margin from about 6.3% back to 8% to 9%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 decline was due to higher raw material intensity in manufacturing, export and commodity-linked mix and volatile raw material prices; it expects improvement in coming quarters and not treating Q1 as steady state.

qa_highlights.question: Positive operating cash flow by H1 FY27 still on track, and working capital outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said Q1 balance sheet and cash flow not yet published; expects much better operating cash flow by H1, converting FY26 current-asset build into cash.

qa_highlights.question: How many new stores in FY27 and revenue contribution?
qa_highlights.answer: 8 to 10 stores by FY27, expected to contribute around INR1 crore per month in revenue.

qa_highlights.question: Current utilisation and target?
qa_highlights.answer: Current utilisation 50% to 55%; targeted around 80% to 82% in the medium term, by end-FY27 to FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Share of own brands across channels?
qa_highlights.answer: Own brands about 17.5% of overall revenue; private label 17.55% of retail sales, 37% of export sales and 45% of domestic sales as stated by the CFO.

qa_highlights.question: Performance of recently opened stores vs older stores?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said new stores are operationally breakeven since day one, with some growing strongly; payback target about 24 months.

risks_watch: Margin recovery to 8% to 9% depends on raw material cost stability; Q1 EBITDA margin about 6.3%.
Operating cash flow guidance for H1 FY27 unverified; balance sheet and cash flow not yet published; inventory and receivables elevated after FY26 build.
Online and quick commerce traction remains small (about INR50 lakh in Q1) and competition from platform in-house brands noted by analysts.
Internal inconsistencies in disclosed figures (133 bps vs 233 bps margin decline; export share 40% vs 35% to 40% export contribution to bottom line) need clarification.
Store maturity: some stores still not up to mark per management; 8 to 10 new stores in FY27 execution.

key_quotes: Total income stood at INR310.24 crores, registering a robust 69.35% year -on-year growth compared with INR183.19 crores in Q1 FY '26.
The payback period for my new store is almost 24 months to recover the entire capex and the rotation of the inventory

544487|2026-09.headline: Patel Retail Q2 FY27 income rose 33.5% to INR300.9 crore, but EBITDA margin fell to 6.8% from 8.6% and PAT declined to INR9.9 crore.
544487|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 total income grew 33.5% YoY to INR300.9 crore while EBITDA rose 5.2% to INR20.5 crore and PAT fell to INR9.9 crore from INR10.1 crore. H1 FY27 income rose 49.6% to INR611.1 crore, with EBITDA up 13.6% to INR40.2 crore and PAT up 13.9% to INR19.4 crore, but margins compressed on higher COGS. Operating cash flow turned positive at INR31 crore in H1 FY27 against negative INR83.4 crore in FY26, and current borrowings fell to INR89.3 crore. Management guided to 8-10 new stores a year and said Q3 and Q4 margins should improve.

segments.name: Retail (Patel R Mart, 54 stores in Maharashtra)
segments.commentary: Retail was 37% of H1 FY27 revenue; management cites operating margin of 6.5-7%. Average store revenue INR12-15 crore at about 7% store operating margin; same-store sales growth 7-8%.

segments.name: Manufacturing and processing (private label, Indian Chaska)
segments.commentary: Manufacturing and processing was 63% of H1 FY27 revenue; management cites operating margin of 7.5-8%. Indian Chaska recorded about INR7 crore in H1 FY27 and is in distribution in eight states and one UT after Madhya Pradesh entry in August.

guidance_outlook: Add around 8-10 stores each year; four stores added recently (Rasayani, Bhiwandi, Uran, Kalyan East); Ghoti (Nashik) and Mangaon (Raigad) finalised; Navi Mumbai locations under identification.
Management expects Q3 and Q4 retail margins to improve; Diwali season to make Q3 more retail-dominant.
Private label share of retail revenue at 17.6% in Q2 FY27, targeted to reach around 22% over time.
Capacity utilisation at 55-60% (about 55% per another answer), targeted to rise to 80-85%; EBITDA margin expected to improve by 100 bps and above over time.
Double-digit growth expected from operating leverage over the next two to three years and from exports.
capex_capacity: Initial capex about INR1,500-1,600 per sq ft plus inventory of INR2,000-2,100 per sq ft; total initial cash outflow about INR1.75-2 crore (more than INR2 crore) per store; payback about 24 months. Average store size 6,000-7,000 sq ft (5,000-6,000 sq ft in another answer).
Ambernath distribution centre expanded by 20,000 sq ft, from 64,000 to about 84,000 sq ft, after running at full utilisation; can support 10-15 more stores in the existing cluster.
New curry powder production line commenced in July 2026 at the manufacturing facility.
Processing capacity above 1,50,000 metric tons per annum; current utilisation about 55%.
Whole spices range launched under Indian Chaska in October 2026, adding to blended spices.
demand_pricing: Management says raw material is procured seasonally and hedged via forward contracts and derivatives; inventory covers about 12 months of demand; hedging proportion not disclosed.
Management says procurement and mix gains plus lower other expenses offset higher COGS, so it does not plan price increases; prices are set by market and competition.
Indian Chaska distribution network of over 350 distributors reaching more than 50,000 retailers; strategy is to deepen penetration in existing states before going wider.
Retail positioning is neighbourhood stores with locality-specific SKU baskets; expansion focused on Western Line (Virar, Vasai, Bhayander), Nashik and PCMC clusters, and tier 2/3 cities.
Management did not disclose export margins; it expects double-digit export growth.

qa_highlights.question: Why did income grow about 50% while EBITDA grew about 40%, and why did Q2 PAT fall 2%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management credited a rising private label share and procurement efficiency. It acknowledged COGS rose as a share of revenue but said other operating expenses fell, which offset it; it expects to restore historical ratios.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the operating cash flow swing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the swing mainly to recovering about INR29 crore or more from debtors in six months, plus better working capital rotation; inventory turns more than 4-5 times a year.

qa_highlights.question: What are the store addition timeline and economics?
qa_highlights.answer: Management plans 8-10 stores a year and has never closed a store; initial capex and inventory is about INR2 crore per store with 24-month payback; Navi Mumbai location not yet disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: Why did borrowings fall and how will funding work?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the decline reflects 12-15 recently opened stores not yet mature, and expects them to mature within about six months.

qa_highlights.question: Can Indian Chaska scale and what does it contribute?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Indian Chaska is at an early stage, did not disclose revenue targets, and expects more SKUs beyond the spices range.

qa_highlights.question: Why did EBITDA margin fall from 8.67% to 6.58% and what is sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management blamed higher COGS as a share of revenue causing gross margin compression, and cited procurement efficiency, mix, utilisation and operating leverage as levers; it gave no sustainable margin level.

risks_watch: Gross margin compression: EBITDA margin down about 200 bps YoY in both Q2 and H1, with PAT margin down to 3.3% in Q2.
Q2 PAT declined despite 33.5% revenue growth; management has not quantified when margin recovery will show.
Capacity utilisation of only about 55-60% in processing; the 80-85% target depends on Indian Chaska volumes.
Store maturity: 12-15 recently opened stores not yet mature, so the 7-8% same-store growth and borrowing reduction depend on them ramping up.
Management gave inconsistent figures on capacity utilisation (55-60% vs about 55%) and average store size (6,000-7,000 vs 5,000-6,000 sq ft); verify against filings.
Inventory rose to INR282.19 crore, and commodity price pass-through remains unquantified.
544487|2026-09.management_tone: Confident on growth and store expansion, but evasive on margin specifics: it did not quantify price pass-through, hedging levels or export margins, and it did not give a sustainable margin number. Management was candid that Q2 PAT declined and gross margins were compressed.
key_quotes: So the key driver for our growing EBITD A is, you know, the proportionately increasing of our private level contribution as compared to previous year.
So the basic key driver which is, you know, marking our cash flow positive is recovery of our debtors.
So madam, the EBITDA margin decline is primarily attributable to the higher cost of goods sold as a percentage of revenue, resulting in gross margin compression.

rows.why: EBITDA margin fell to 6.8% in Q2 from 8.6% (H1 6.6% vs 8.6%), but management expects Q3/Q4 retail margins to improve and 100bps+ over time, citing procurement mix and lower other expenses; no quantified recovery path was given.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Processing utilisation is only 55-60% (well below the 80% threshold), so no capex is needed for processing now; retail expansion capex (about INR2 crore per store) is already in the store pipeline, with Navi Mumbai sites still being identified.
