rows.why: Management says procurement and mix gains offset higher COGS and it does not plan price increases; raw material pass-through was not quantified.

tone.note: Management was confident on store expansion, Ambernath capacity and private-label mix, but evasive on margin specifics, hedging levels, price pass-through and export margins; analysts pressed on why income grew about 50% while EBITDA grew about 40% and why Q2 PAT fell.

544488|2026-03.headline: Vikram Solar FY26 revenue hit a record INR4,800 crore (+40% YoY) with EBITDA margin up to 19%, but guided FY27 non-DCR per-watt EBITDA lower at INR1.75–2.
544488|2026-03.overview: FY26 set records on revenue (INR4,800 crore), volumes (3.3 GW, +76%), EBITDA (INR917 crore, 19% margin) and PAT (INR470 crore, 10% margin), with Q4 revenue of INR1,450 crore and first 1 GW quarterly run rate. Management said Q4 per-watt cost rose INR0.80 against a INR0.60 realisation gain, compressing per-watt EBITDA to about INR2.35. The order book stood at 8.2 GW at 31 March 2026, with distribution orders removed from the book and C&I DCR orders under renegotiation. The company announced a 6 GW wafer-ingot phase at Gangaikondan (about INR3,700 crore, commissioning FY29) and a 15 GWh BESS target by FY30, while the 9 GW TOPCon cell plant has been pushed to a phased commissioning through Q4 FY27 and ramp in Q2 FY28.

financial_highlights.value: 0.03; working capital net debt INR64 crore; no long-term debt

segments.name: Modules
segments.commentary: Q4 production about 1 GW, the highest ever; nameplate 9.5 GW today rising to 15.5 GW after Gangaikondan 6 GW module plant (first output guided June 2026). Cumulative global deployment crossed 10 GW (over 25 million modules).

segments.name: Cells
segments.commentary: No captive cell capacity yet; 9 GW TOPCon Plus cell plant at Gangaikondan targets first cell December 2026 and completion of phases through March 2027, with a further 3 GW in FY28. A 2 GW DCR cell procurement agreement with Jupiter International supports FY27 DCR offtake, weighted to H2.

segments.name: BESS
segments.commentary: 5 GWh cell-to-pack facility targeted by March 2027 (assembly capex about INR150 crore); 7.5 GWh cell phase 1 in FY29 and phase 2 in FY30 against a 15 GWh FY30 target.

segments.name: Wafer-ingot
segments.commentary: 6 GW phase 1 at Gangaikondan approved by the Board (about INR3,700 crore, commissioning FY29 per call, March 2028 in Q&A); the balance 6 GW is at about INR600 crore per GW, with Board approval planned next fiscal.

guidance_outlook: FY27 production guided at about 8 GW (6 GW non-DCR, 2 GW DCR) and FY27 EBITDA of INR1,500–1,600 crore, about 74% above FY26.
Non-DCR volumes guided to INR1.75–2.00 per watt-peak EBITDA on average through FY27; DCR-linked procurement volumes guided to INR2–2.5 per watt.
Per-watt EBITDA guided to about INR5 in FY28 post cell integration, with a further INR1 reduction as more capex comes in; the current level is about INR6 per watt-peak.
Standard nameplate utilisation of 65–70% for modules and 70–75% for cells after FY27 ramp.
Closing FY27 debt guided at about INR3,200 crore (earlier plan INR3,500 crore); FY28-end debt about INR6,500–6,600 crore; interest and DSCR guardrails above 2.5 and net debt/equity below 1.5.
capex_capacity: 9 GW TOPCon cell plant: civil works by September 2026, cleanroom/MEP October 2026, equipment installation October–November, power by Siemens in November, first cell end-December/early January, commissioning through March 2027, ramp in Q2 FY28; total cell capex for 12 GW about INR5,400 crore, mostly spent in FY27 with the last 10% instalment in FY28 (cost up 10% after switching equipment sourcing from Thailand to China).
Gangaikondan 6 GW module plant in final stretch, first output on track for June 2026; Vallam 5 GW built in under nine months.

Wafer-ingot phase 1 of 6 GW at Gangaikondan (about INR3,700 crore, commissioning FY29; Q&A said March 2028), with advances of under INR100 crore in FY27; BESS cell construction from October 2026 over 24 months, FY27 land and initial spend under INR200 crore.
Management expects standard utilisation of 65–70% on modules and 70–75% on cells, on nameplate basis.
Capex to be funded through a mix of debt and equity, and internal accruals; the company expects to fund FY27 BESS and wafer-ingot outflows largely from internal accruals.
demand_pricing: India added 45 GW of solar in FY26 (against a 24 GW target, about 87% above FY25); cumulative base 150 GW. Utility-scale additions were a record 34 GW and rooftop 8.5 GW.

Management sees over 80 GW of grandfathered Non-DCR demand over two years, about 28 GW of live utility-scale DCR tenders and about 25 GW of inherent DCR demand from C&I, KUSUM and rooftop. Management expects DCR demand of 20–25 GW in FY27.

Cell costs rose during FY26 on higher silver prices and removal of China's export VAT rebate. Aluminium rose from $3,100 to $3,600 per ton; EVA cost rose with crude; partly offset by lower cell prices.
Approximately 80% of the order book has cell price pass-through clauses; FY26 per-watt overhead fell 16%.
Q4 realisations rose about INR0.60 per watt-peak while cost rose INR0.80, compressing per-watt EBITDA to about INR2.35 (DCR mandate from June 2026).

Distribution order book (about 1 GW) was removed from the 1.9 GW Q4 order inflow and moved to spot buying; distribution network about 110+ distributors and 550+ dealers/SIs. A US export project of about 0.6 GW was dropped after the IPP found it unviable.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the 1 GW distribution order book removed, and does the 1.9 GW order inflow include distribution?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said inflow excludes distribution; the recurring distributor order book moved to spot buying as volumes shift to DCR and outsourced cell supply. Distribution was about 20% of Non-DCR volumes last year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the EBITDA per watt-peak in Q4 and in the non-DCR business?
qa_highlights.answer: Q4 per-watt EBITDA was about INR2.35, with non-DCR volumes guided at INR1.75–2 on average for FY27 and about INR5 for FY28 post cell integration (current about INR6).

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 volume and order plan?
qa_highlights.answer: About 8 GW of production in FY27 (2 GW DCR, 6 GW non-DCR) against 8.2 GW order book at March 2026, of which 6 GW goes out in FY27 leaving 1.2 GW, with the rest to be won from the 87 GW grandfathered Non-DCR pipeline.

qa_highlights.question: What is the debt trajectory and interest outflow?
qa_highlights.answer: Closing FY27 debt guided at about INR3,200 crore and FY28 at INR6,500–6,600 crore; interest on construction projects is capitalised until commissioning, so P&L impact is deferred.

qa_highlights.question: How is the company handling the US export orders and where would it source cells?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said exports to the US have slowed to near zero since November; about 1 GW of export orders are with long-standing IPPs and are being executed via cells sourced from North Africa, with EU, Australia and Middle East also explored.

qa_highlights.question: How are silver and silicon cost increases passed on to customers?
qa_highlights.answer: MSAs allow pass-through of cell cost and dollar appreciation to the extent of about 80% of the order book; future pass-through depends on the market once cell and wafer-ingot capacity comes in.

risks_watch: Per-watt EBITDA compression: Q4 cost rose INR0.80 vs realisation gain INR0.60, and FY27 non-DCR guidance is INR1.75–2, well below FY26 levels.

Execution risk on 9 GW cell plant (first cell targeted end-December 2026, ramp Q2 FY28) and 6 GW Gangaikondan module plant (June 2026); a sizable part of FY27 volume relies on a third-party 2 GW DCR cell supply.
Order book quality: about 1 GW distribution orders removed, C&I DCR orders under renegotiation, and US export order risk.
Rising interest and working capital needs with Vallam inventory; debt guardrails (DSCR above 2.5, net debt/equity below 1.5) and the INR6,500–6,600 crore FY28 debt level.
Raw material and silver cost pass-through (about 80% of order book) and cell price competition from domestic capacity additions.
544488|2026-03.management_tone: Confident and expansive on sector growth and integration, with the most specific numbers on FY26 records and FY27 guidance. Less specific or deferring on pricing (2 GW Jupiter procurement commercials not disclosed), US export orders and pass-through terms beyond the current 80% coverage.
key_quotes: The order inflow does not include distribution. We have taken that out of order booking format.
Yes, so when we spoke about a debt level of INR3,500 crores, the plan was to have an entire 12 gigawatt of cell in place, which we have now phased it into 9 plus 3.
Approximately 80% of our order book carries cell price pass-through clauses, insulating the P&L from any input volatility.
So that INR0.20 Additional incremental cost has dented the per-EBITDA-watt-peak to that extent and hence you could see a slight percentage impact on the EBITDA margin level.

Our working assumption is that the sector will stabilize around an 80 to 100 gigawatt of nameplate fully integrated sustainable capacity held by a small group of serious full-stack players, and the total addressable market is heading towards a similar number.

rows.why: 6 GW Gangaikondan module plant first output guided June 2026 (nameplate rising from 9.5 GW to 15.5 GW), and the 9 GW TOPCon cell plant is under construction with INR5,400 crore total cell capex mostly spent in FY27; FY27 production guided at 7.5-8 GW.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: FY27 production guided at 7.5-8 GW versus 3.3 GW sold in FY26 (+76%), against an 8.2 GW order book at 31 March 2026 that covers about 6 GW of FY27 output, though distribution orders (about 1 GW) were removed from the book.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: 6 GW wafer-ingot phase 1 (about INR3,700 crore, commissioning FY29) is Board-approved, 15 GWh BESS target by FY30 is set, and the balance 6 GW wafer-ingot at about INR600 crore per GW goes to Board approval next fiscal; the capex pipeline is already committed.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY27 EBITDA guided at INR1,500-1,600 crore (about 74% above FY26) with per-watt EBITDA compressing, and the 9 GW cell plant has already slipped to phased commissioning through Mar 2027, leaving little room to raise guidance.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Cell plant execution (first cell end-Dec 2026, ramp Q2 FY28), reliance on a third-party 2 GW DCR cell supply weighted to H2, C&I DCR orders under renegotiation, and US export orders near zero since November; per-watt EBITDA is already guided to INR1.75-2.00.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: 5 GWh cell-to-pack BESS facility targeted by March 2027 (assembly capex about INR150 crore) and TOPCon Plus cells from the 9 GW plant starting first cell December 2026 are the planned new product launches.

rows.label: FY27 closing debt at INR3,200 crore (below earlier INR3,500 crore plan)
rows.why: Management guides closing FY27 debt to about INR3,200 crore versus an earlier INR3,500 crore plan, though FY28-end debt rises to INR6,500-6,600 crore as capex continues.

rows.label: Order book depletion and DCR demand replenishment
rows.why: The 8.2 GW order book at 31 March 2026 leaves 1.2 GW after about 6 GW ships in FY27, and management sees 20-25 GW of FY27 DCR demand and over 80 GW of grandfathered non-DCR demand to win from, but about 1 GW distribution orders were removed and C&I DCR orders are under renegotiation.

rows.label: Cell cost pass-through on about 80% of order book
rows.why: MSAs cover about 80% of the order book for cell cost and dollar pass-through, but future pass-through depends on market conditions once cell and wafer-ingot capacity comes in, and silver and aluminium costs have risen (aluminium from $3,100 to $3,600 per ton).

tone.note: Management was confident on FY26 records, the 6 GW module ramp and FY27 production of 7.5-8 GW, but cautious on per-watt EBITDA compression, the slipped cell plant timeline, US export orders and pass-through terms; analysts pushed on pricing and order book quality.

544488|2026-06.headline: Vikram Solar Q1 FY27: record 1,006 MW volume (+32% YoY) and revenue ~INR1,563 cr, but EBITDA fell to INR126 cr (8.06% margin) as costs outran pass-through.
544488|2026-06.overview: Revenue rose about 8% QoQ and 38% YoY to roughly INR1,563 crore on 1.06 GW dispatched, with per-watt realisation up 8% QoQ to INR15.02/Wp on DCR mix. EBITDA was INR126 crore (8.06% margin) and PAT INR19.78 crore, as unit COGS rose INR1.86/Wp from metals, EVA, and cell costs that were only partly passed through. Management attributed the squeeze to ALMM-2 uncertainty, Gulf-conflict input inflation, and industry oversupply. It declined to give fresh FY27 guidance, deferring the update to H1 results, and the Gangaikondan module plant (first module 29 June) and cell plant (Q4 FY27) remain on schedule.

financial_highlights.change: Down sharply; prior-quarter level referenced as ~16%

financial_highlights.value: 76 MW (cited as ~75 MW later on call)

segments.commentary: Base-load book of ~7.1 GW with tighter margins; management says pass-through under MSAs applies to cells only, not balance-of-materials. Price realisation for mid-market expected ~INR0.50/Wp higher.

segments.commentary: 76 MW sold in Q1 at materially higher realisation (DCR ~INR22+/Wp per management). Cell supply is from external domestic partners until own cell line starts; DCR volume expected to grow 2–2.5x each quarter.

segments.commentary: Monthly run rate roughly doubled from ~40 MW last year; network of 119+ distributors and 757+ dealers across 24 states. Management says distribution pricing is spot-linked and realises INR1–1.5/Wp above key accounts.

Gangaikondan cell line (9 GW) on track for commissioning in Q4 FY27, with ramp possibly spilling into Q1 FY28; FY28 cell utilisation targeted at 40–50% (six-month ramp).
Wafer-ingot capacity resized to 9 GW (from 6 GW, part of the 12 GW plan), project cost ~INR5,600 crore; ground-breaking announced for next month.
Capex of ~INR5,000 crore planned for FY27 and similar in FY28; funding targeted at 75:25 debt-equity, ~70:30 once scheme is in place.
capex_capacity: Gangaikondan: 6 GW module (commissioned 29 June 2026, fully funded); module capacity cited as 15.5 GW total across sites, with 9–9.5 GW expected to be deliverable in FY27.
Gangaikondan 9 GW cell plant: civil/PEB advanced, first cell targeted Q4 FY27; ~70% backward integration once live.

Chinese landed cell price cited at ~4 cents/W before 27.5% BCD.

qa_highlights.question: What was the per-watt spread this quarter, and why was the 88% of order book with cost escalation clauses not passed through? Has the spread improved since ALMM-2 deferment?
qa_highlights.answer: Pass-through under MSAs covers only cells, not balance-of-materials (BOM). Cell oversupply also limited price recovery. EBITDA of INR126 crore on ~1 GW works out to about INR1.25/Wp. Management wants one more quarter before judging DCR vs non-DCR margins.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the ~8 GW order book is executable this year?
qa_highlights.answer: Module capacity is 15.5 GW, with 9–9.5 GW deliverable in FY27. Management will not take negative-margin orders and asked for another quarter of clarity on volumes and pricing.

qa_highlights.question: How does DCR spread compare with non-DCR, given cell makers retain most margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said DCR delivers more margin than non-DCR but gave no number. Only 75–76 MW of DCR was sold in Q1, so it is too early to split margins.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 9 GW cell line on track for Q4 commissioning, and will all 9 GW come on stream then?
qa_highlights.answer: Commissioning is on track for Q4 FY27. Ramp-up may spill into Q1 FY28, and the full 9 GW may not be running in Q4.

qa_highlights.question: Will Q2 EBITDA margin return to the ~16% level?
qa_highlights.answer: Not a direct conclusion. Q2 will still see some unabsorbed price impact, partly offset by DCR and channel mix. Management declined to commit to a 16% margin.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Q1 volume driven by an influx of non-DCR orders, and will it normalise?
qa_highlights.answer: Volume depends on backlog and module ramp, and management sees no slowdown. Industry DCR demand estimate was cut to about 17 GW from 20–25 GW as C&I shifts to non-DCR. Country consumption was about 12 GW in the quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Will FY27 production guidance of 7–8 GW and the INR1,500–1,600 crore EBITDA outlook be reaffirmed?

qa_highlights.question: Has the West Bengal election changed renewals, payments or tenders?

qa_highlights.question: Is there FY27 revenue guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO guided 12-15% consolidated growth from the order book plus in-year wins. The MD cited a target of over INR500 crore in FY27 against INR436 crore in FY26.

qa_highlights.question: How much annual revenue was lost from contracts ended or not renewed?
qa_highlights.answer: FY25 revenue was about INR373 crore against INR352 crore in FY24 standalone, as Calcutta Airport (about INR15 crore a year) and IIT Bhubaneswar (INR6-7 crore) were lost. No renewals fell due in FY26; Calcutta Airport re-bid is planned.

qa_highlights.question: What is the labour-code impact on margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said contract labour costs are passed through to clients, and no client has sought renegotiation yet. Formalisation may cut informal operators' margins while expanding opportunities.

qa_highlights.question: Why is growth not 30-40% given the small base?
qa_highlights.answer: The MD said faster growth is possible but low-margin, extended-credit tenders would hurt margins, cash flow and DSO. The company wants margins from most contracts before accelerating.

qa_highlights.question: Why are IPO proceeds not fully deployed?
qa_highlights.answer: INR36.91 crore is unutilised. New contracts started only from November to January after the September IPO, and about INR10 crore was deployed and recovered, so full deployment is expected within two years.

qa_highlights.question: When will CCTV revenue rise?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects better CCTV returns toward year end, with tenders in 2-3 months and 3-4 months of project work, plus AMC contracts for higher margin within about six months.

risks_watch: Receivables of about INR145 crore (about 33% of FY26 revenue) and collection delays from government clients such as DTET and Haldia Dock.
Pending West Bengal draft labour-code rules, which could affect wage and compliance costs for the 70-75% of business in that state.
EBITDA margin mix risk: security and housekeeping run at about 4.5-4.8% EBITDA, while higher-margin CCTV and IFM are stagnant.
Keertika Academy and DDU-GKY tenders for Maharashtra and West Bengal remain under evaluation.
Calcutta Airport re-bid and government renewals (New Secretariat, Nabanna) due next year.
Deployment of INR36.91 crore unutilised IPO proceeds.
544495|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on the West Bengal government pipeline and on CCTV recovery, but cautious on growth pace, citing margin and cash-flow discipline. Answers on receivables and the IPO were detailed, and some were hard to follow; the CFO and MD were occasionally evasive on FY27 guidance.
key_quotes: So we are slightly shy of really increasing revenue without a very strong consideration towards the bottom line either in the terms of the margin or even the cash flow.

544495|2026-06.headline: NIS Management Q1 FY27 consolidated income rose 15.68% YoY to INR115.44 crore, with EBITDA up 36.24% to INR9.22 crore at a 7.99% margin.
544495|2026-06.overview: Consolidated total income reached INR115.44 crore, up 15.68% YoY, and EBITDA rose 36.24% to INR9.22 crore with margin up 121 bps to 7.99%. Net profit was INR6.40 crore (up 35% YoY, margin 5.54%), while EPS of INR3.23 grew only 3.53%. Management reiterated the INR500 crore FY27 revenue goal, flagged that the CCTV segment posted a Q1 loss due to project timing, and declined to commit to a margin expansion path beyond 1-2% over two years. Net debt, the share price fall since IPO, and buyback ideas drew pointed investor questions that management largely deflected toward growth investment.

segments.name: Security and manpower (standalone)
segments.commentary: Security revenue INR54.98 crore and housekeeping INR41.88 crore in June 2026 quarter; management cites ~9.95% EBITDA for manpower-type businesses (security, housekeeping, payroll).

segments.name: IFM and payroll
segments.commentary: IFM revenue INR10.28 crore and payroll services INR3.40 crore in the quarter; management says manpower businesses have similar profitability.

segments.name: CCTV and electronic security
segments.commentary: Revenue INR2.11 crore with a loss at PAT level in Q1, attributed to project execution costs ahead of bill raising; management expects stabilisation by September quarter and calls it the most profitable segment. FY26 CCTV loss was about INR1.5 crore.

segments.name: Vocational training (LLP and Keertika Academy)
segments.commentary: Q1 revenue nil (INR0 lakh); net loss about INR57 lakh across the LLP and Keertika Academy.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue target: cross INR500 crore consolidated, with management saying FY26 Nov-Dec onwards revenues will be booked for the full year, and expecting ~12-15% growth guidance to hold; management ambition of 20% growth stated but not committed.
FY27 EBITDA margin: management says Q1 is seasonally strongest, margins moderate in Q2-Q3 and recover in Q4; no firm FY27 margin expansion number given.
Medium term: Debajit Choudhury expects at least 1-2% EBITDA margin increase over the next two years, driven by electronics and mechanisation mix.
FY28 revenue: Kanad Mukherjee said FY28 will 'definitely cross INR600 crore', with range INR630-640 crore and a target of above INR650 crore by FY28.
CCTV/projects: targeted ~INR30 crore revenue this year (vs INR13-14 crore last year) and PAT of INR3.5-4 crore vs ~INR2.5 crore last year.
Debt: management says no increase in debt; debt levels to stay flat over FY27-FY28.
Free cash flow: average INR8-9 crore over the last 3-4 years; aim to lift to INR13-14 crore by moving systems revenue from INR13-14 crore to ~INR30 crore.
capex_capacity: DDU-GKY Odisha skill project awarded for INR7.93 crore; management expects ~INR4 crore billing this year; about six-month infrastructure gestation period and two-year contract tenor.

HDFC Bank command-and-control centre (CCTV-driven, subscription model, covering 100-150 branches): management expects INR1.5-2 crore investment (about INR1 crore for control room) and INR2-3 crore revenue; final stage negotiations.
Mumbai traffic and police projects: INR15-18 crore expected from one or two tenders; an INR2.18 crore Mumbai traffic tender already received.
NKDA AMC contract worth about INR6 crore expected, pending final tendering; SAIL Burnpur engagement targeted at INR4-5 crore this year.
Acquisitions: management says acquisitions are possible in the future for technology capabilities, but not immediate; no near-term plans for manpower-based acquisitions.
demand_pricing: Q1 order wins: 5 work orders from Reliance Projects and Property Management Services worth INR30.77 crore; 7 Reliance Group FM contracts worth INR14.94 crore (combined INR45.71 crore); 2 Nesco orders worth INR1.94 crore; West Bengal Public Department housekeeping order INR36.71 lakh.
Government GeM tenders now at around 3.85% (L1 pricing); management says it will be more selective in manpower GeM bids and focus on CCTV and DDU-GKY projects.
Customer mix: Reliance top client at INR46-47 crore annually; HDFC Bank ~INR18 crore; Anjali Jewellers ~INR12 crore; airports ~INR30 crore annually; Torrent Power ~INR6-7 crore.
Renewal rates ~96-97%; average client retention 4.5-5 years per management.
Geographic mix: West Bengal ~72-73% of revenue; growth push in Gujarat, Maharashtra, Bihar and Odisha.
Receivable cycle: bills raised after wages; client payment typically in about three months.

qa_highlights.question: Given 12-15% FY27 growth guidance, Q1 growth of ~16% and ~8% margin, is there scope to raise FY27 revenue and margin guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY26 revenues booked from Nov-Dec onwards will be booked for the full year in FY27, and it is confident of crossing INR500 crore this year. Q1 EBITDA is seasonally better, moderating in Q2-Q3 and recovering in Q4, so no margin expansion percentage was committed.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Q1 FY27 revenue split by segment and how has the mix changed?
qa_highlights.answer: June 2026 quarter: security INR54.98 crore, housekeeping INR41.88 crore, IFM INR10.28 crore, payroll INR3.40 crore (total INR110.53 crore); CCTV INR2.11 crore; small security and housekeeping INR1.29 crore; vocational training nil. Manpower EBITDA about 9.95%; CCTV PAT loss about INR1.27 lakh; vocational training net loss about INR57 lakh.

qa_highlights.question: What is the debt outlook and free cash flow target for FY27-FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: No increase in debt; debt levels to stay flat. Average FCF was INR8-9 crore over the last 3-4 years; aim to lift to INR13-14 crore by growing systems revenue from INR13-14 crore to about INR30 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Is 20% growth an aspiration, and how will margins move from ~7% to 8-9%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the hope is to grow 20% without compromising the balance sheet, but no commitment. On margins, Kanad Mukherjee said expansion depends on project businesses catching up with manpower business; Debajit Choudhury expects at least 1-2% EBITDA margin increase over the next two years from electronics and mechanisation mix.

qa_highlights.question: What is net debt, and why not a buyback given the share price fall since the IPO?
qa_highlights.answer: Standalone debt about INR69 crore vs cash about INR60 crore as of June; consolidated debt about INR82 crore. On the buyback proposal (13 lakh shares, about INR6 crore), Debajit Choudhury said the IPO capital is meant for growth, citing skill development capex, and did not commit to a buyback.

qa_highlights.question: Why was CCTV loss-making in Q1 and what is FY28 outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Project businesses incur Q1 losses due to execution spend before completion certificates and billing; FY26 CCTV loss was about INR1.5 crore. Management expects stabilisation by September quarter and targets about INR30 crore CCTV/projects revenue and PAT of INR3.5-4 crore this year. FY28: revenue to cross INR600 crore, range INR630-640 crore, target above INR650 crore.

risks_watch: Thin margin expansion visibility: management declined to give a firm FY27 margin number and expects Q2-Q3 moderation; medium-term 1-2% EBITDA uplift is the only figure given.
CCTV/projects execution: Q1 loss and reliance on lumpy tenders (Mumbai traffic INR15-18 crore, HDFC Bank command centre, NKDA AMC ~INR6 crore, SAIL INR4-5 crore) that are not yet awarded.
Pricing pressure in government manpower work: GeM L1 bids at about 3.85%, with management saying it will be more selective.
Working capital and receivables: about 3-month (90-day) client payment cycle; debt flat at about INR69 crore standalone and cash of INR60 crore as of June, with rising loans and advances.

Client concentration and renewal: Reliance at INR46-47 crore annually is the top client, and the DTET contract is under renewal with a loss already provided for; monitor renewal outcome and West Bengal concentration (72-73%).
Capital allocation and shareholder value: share price about INR46 vs IPO price INR111, buyback rejected in favour of growth capex; IPO funds unutilised INR36.85 crore as of June 2026.
key_quotes: So what we are seeing is that, last year we would have -- whatever revenues we had booked from November-December onwards that will get booked for the entire year during this financial year.
So whether there is going to be an expansion at the EBITDA margin at a percentage level is hard to say.
There will be no increase in debt. Debt levels will stay the same. There will be no increase in debt.
So I would expect at least an increase of about 1% to 2% in the EBITDA area over the next 2 years or so.

544496|2026-03.headline: Vikran FY26 revenue hit a record INR1,249 crore (vs INR916 crore) with EBITDA margin near 14%; FY27 guided at INR2,200 crore plus.
544496|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue from operations was INR647 crore, up from INR355 crore a year earlier, with EBITDA of INR92 crore (14.2% margin) and PAT of INR56 crore (vs INR38 crore). For FY26, revenue rose to INR1,249 crore, EBITDA was about INR175 crore (around 14%) and PAT was INR92 crore (vs about INR78 crore). Management attributed margin dilution to delayed Jal Jeevan Mission receivables (provisioned, mostly in Q4), and to early-stage solar EPC projects. The company closed its acquisition of NOPL Solar (969 MW PM-KUSUM project) at end-April 2026 and guided FY27 revenue of INR2,200 crore plus, with a 14-15% EBITDA margin target.

vs INR470 crore last year (per analyst)

financial_highlights.value: upgraded to IND A, stable outlook

segments.name: Power T&D
segments.commentary: Management sees FY27 power T&D at about 30% of revenue, focused on selective 765 kV GIS/AIS projects for clients such as Power Grid and NTPC. Scope includes substations, lines, underground cabling and smart metering.

segments.name: Solar EPC
segments.commentary: Solar is now the main growth pillar, with management expecting about 60% of FY27 revenue. Marquee wins include 100 MW AC (Ellume Energy), 400 MW AC / 580 MWp DC (NTPC Renewable) and 600 MW (NOPL Solar); 20 MW of NOPL is commissioned, with more due by end-May.

segments.name: Water infrastructure
segments.commentary: Water is about 10% of FY27 revenue from the existing order book, roughly INR600 crore; no new water bids for about 18 months. Jal Jeevan Mission receivables are about INR400 crore, and INR17-18 crore was received in FY27 to date.

segments.name: NOPL Solar (subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Acquired 100% at end-April 2026; project cost INR4,200 crore with sanctioned lender funding. Management cites revenue over INR500 crore over 25 years, 85-88% EBITDA margin, and about INR1 crore per month from the first 20 MW.

EBITDA margin guided at 14-15% for FY27, which management said it was confident of maintaining.
Possible additional INR1,000-1,400 crore solar EPC order from the Onix balance EPC scope, not yet in the INR5,700 crore order book; may be booked at arm's length price.
FY27 growth expected to be higher than FY26; FY28 revenue about INR3,000 crore plus; management declined to give FY29 figures.

Data centre EPC target of about INR100 crore order book in FY27, initially 50-100 MW.

Project funding of INR4,200 crore is sanctioned by a major lender, and the existing financing line rolls over to the new owner subject to a promoter evaluation; backup financing is in place.
Solar EPC: 500 MW EPC project in execution; company's total under-construction portfolio stated as about 1.5 GW (1 GW developer, 500 MW EPC).
Operational footprint: 22 states, 190 locations, about 1,200 staff, with about 222 at the Thane head office.
Management is cautiously evaluating Middle East and Africa opportunities, and says it is not pursuing a developer or investment model for data centres.
demand_pricing: Government push and private demand for solar; management sees better cash flow and margins in solar.
Management said it is selectively bidding; no new water orders for about 18 months.
Management said the company has no BESS in its current scope but has bid for some BESS projects.
Supply chain is largely dependent on China, but management says procurement was front-loaded in FY26 and the West Asia conflict has had limited impact so far.
Management says CFO-level margin for FY23-25 was 15-17%, and that projects are being chosen for similar margin range.

qa_highlights.question: Will EBITDA margin recover from 13-14% to historical 18-22%, and what is the status of the Onix project and its financing?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said FY23-25 EBITDA was 15-17%, with FY26 at about 14% due to JJM receivable provisions (reversed on collection). Management said the Onix SPV is now 100% owned; the lender is comfortable, and 4 projects are commissioned with 2 more due by end-May.

qa_highlights.question: What is execution in FY27 with and without NOPL, and what milestones have been achieved?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says INR2,200 crore plus is achievable with or without NOPL, and that a plan without NOPL 'does not make a lot of sense'. Milestones since the April takeover are limited to a few commissioned projects; land and evacuation issues are cleared.

qa_highlights.question: How much receivables exposure is there from water/JJM, and how much was provided in FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said about INR400 crore of water receivables are due from JJM. About INR20 crore of provision was taken in FY26, mostly in Q4; the CFO said there is no specific high-risk receivable.

qa_highlights.question: When will cash flow turn positive, and will there be equity dilution?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said there are no plans for further equity dilution and that operating cash flow is expected to turn positive from FY28; the order book has grown from about INR2,000 crore to over INR5,000 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What is the revenue mix for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Chairman said about 60% solar, 30% power T&D and about 10% water.

qa_highlights.question: Is the additional INR1,400 crore NOPL solar order included in the INR5,700 crore order book?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is not included because the order is not yet placed and documentation is pending; the CFO said about INR1,000 crore may be booked in coming days, executable over 12-15 months.

NOPL execution: about 85% land identified, 150-odd locations to complete by March 2027 deadline; the lender line roll-over is subject to a promoter evaluation.
Pending INR1,000-1,400 crore Onix balance EPC order (arm's length pricing) that would be additional to the INR5,700 crore order book.
Supply-chain and geopolitical risk from China sourcing and the West Asia conflict; management is hedging with large suppliers.
Data centre EPC entry, with a small INR100 crore target; no formal order yet.

544497|2026-06.headline: Anlon Q1 FY27 consolidated EBITDA margin fell to ~17% (PAT ₹8.28 cr) on raw-material spikes and Remember India consolidation; management targets 25-27% for FY27.
544497|2026-06.overview: Consolidated Q1 FY27 total income was ₹87.62 cr versus ₹33.31 cr in Q1 FY26, with EBITDA of ₹15.65 cr (vs ₹6.26 cr) and PAT of ₹8.28 cr (vs ₹3.55 cr). EBITDA margin moderated to about 17%, which management attributed to a sharp rise in solvent and petrochemical raw-material prices after the geopolitical conflict and to operating costs of the newly acquired Remember India Health links being consolidated. The company completed the 63.98% acquisition of Remember India on 8 May 2026, has acquired Apiqo Organics and Bizotic Lifesciences, and is moving into finished dosage formulations. Management reiterated FY27 revenue guidance of ₹350-400 cr and a ~30% three-year revenue CAGR, but gave limited quantitative detail on Remember India.

544497|2026-09.headline: Anlon Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 102.3% YoY to INR105.61 crore, with EBITDA margin recovering to 23.9%.
544497|2026-09.overview: Consolidated revenue for Q2 FY27 was INR105.61 crore, up 102.3% YoY, and H1 FY27 revenue of INR193.17 crore already exceeds full-year FY26 revenue. EBITDA margin recovered to 23.9% in Q2 from 17.8% in Q1, which management attributes mainly to passing raw material costs on to customers through price revisions. Management reiterated FY27 revenue guidance of INR380-400 crore and gave FY28 guidance of INR650-700 crore, excluding medical devices and CDMO upside. Operating cash outflow narrowed to INR7.94 crore in H1 FY27 from INR79.44 crore for all of FY26, and the company is targeting positive operating cash flow by end-FY27.

segments.commentary: Contributed 43.7% of H1 FY27 consolidated revenue; has opened an industrial and fine chemicals vertical as a new revenue stream outside pharma. Management cites a sustainable EBITDA margin of 20-23% and PAT margin of 11-13%.

segments.commentary: Contributed 11.7% of H1 FY27 consolidated revenue; provides ready-to-operate API capacity at a second manufacturing site. Share swap to take the company to 100% ownership was said to be completing within 8-10 days.

segments.commentary: Entered finished dosage formulations (tablets, capsules) with access to over 30 formulation dossiers; operations start from Q3 FY27. Management expects first revenue in Q4 FY27 and sees a tablet/capsule peak of INR80-90 crore.

segments.commentary: Both incorporated in the period. Anlon Biologics targets peptides, oligonucleotides and biosimilars, with first revenue in Q4 FY28; Anlon Medico targets surgical implants and devices, with first revenue from Q3 FY28 and INR70-80 crore expected within 3 years.

FY28 revenue guidance of INR650-700 crore (INR680-700 crore in a later answer), excluding medical devices and CDMO upside.
Sustainable EBITDA margin target of 25-28%; current run-rate is 23-24%. Management said FY27 full-year margin could reach 25-26%, and FY28 is 'very early to commit'.

Positive operating cash flow targeted by end-FY27. Working capital cycle nominal target of 170-180 days; receivable days are being cut to 90-100 from 130-140.
Dividend decision deferred; management will review cash availability and free cash flow around Q4 FY27 results.
Capital raise of up to INR250 crore being finalised by end-November, subject to AGM approval; INR65-70 crore term loan planned for capex.
capex_capacity: Group installed capacity is about 1,900-2,000 MTPA against 400 MTPA at the Anlon parent facility; consolidated utilisation is 65-67%, expected to stay flat for the next two quarters.

Rajkot greenfield expansion adds about 1,200 MTPA via 8 new clean lines, targeted for Q1 FY28 (construction on track; a public hearing in December could cause a 1-2 month delay). Expansion of 500 MTPA planned across the group; Apiqo's 500-600 MTPA expansion is also due by Q1 FY28.
Of the INR130 crore expansion capex, only INR15-20 crore has been spent so far; maximum spend expected by December as advances are paid to suppliers.
Anlon Medicos injectable facility expansion has started, with injectables expected by end-FY28.

Management claims cost is 10% or more below Chinese prices for its key molecules and that it has displaced Chinese suppliers in Europe, LATAM, Japan and Korea.

544501|2026-09.headline: Sugs Lloyd H1 FY27 revenue rose 73% to INR213.31 crore and PAT 69% to INR20.01 crore, with order book at INR1,067 crore.
544501|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue was INR134.91 crore, up 12% YoY and 72% QoQ, making H1 FY27 the strongest half in company history. H1 EBITDA was INR31 crore at a 14.5% margin, and PAT was INR20.01 crore, with EPS of INR8.62 against INR6.86. Q2 new orders totalled INR395 crore excluding GST, all from outside Bihar, which cut Bihar's share of the order book from about 82% to about 55%. Management kept the INR1,000 crore FY28 target and the 10% product revenue goal, while operating cash outflow and debt (about INR160 crore) remained the key watch items.

segments.name: Power T&D (incl. smart grid)
segments.commentary: About 80% of H1 FY27 revenue, driven by RDSS and distribution project execution. Flagship partner project (about INR542 crore pre-GST) is due for completion by March 2028, and the Odisha maintenance contract adds about INR60 crore a year for 3 years.

segments.name: Solar EPC
segments.commentary: Balance of H1 revenue. Amritsar solar plant scheduled for completion by December 2026. Management says EPC is becoming more competitive and it is shifting toward capex-plus-RESCO models through Sugs Renewables.

segments.name: Engineering products (FPI)
segments.commentary: Company says it holds more than half the domestic fault passage indicator market. Compact FPI completed testing and first unit to be supplied within the quarter. Target of about 10% of total revenue by FY28, covering all products together.

segments.name: Order book
segments.commentary: INR1,067 crore at 30 September 2026 (about 3.5x FY26 revenue), of which about INR929 crore is power T&D and the rest solar. About 9/10 is with government utilities, PSUs and centrally funded schemes.

guidance_outlook: FY28 revenue target of INR1,000 crore remains unchanged; management said it is on track.
FY27 revenue target of INR600 crore and 10% product revenue target for FY28 described as intact.
EBITDA margin expected to average about 15% for the full year, with quarterly variation within the 14-15% band.
Management expects to add about INR400-500 crore of orders this year and said it would get more than that; about INR900-1,000 crore expected from bids within 6-9 months.
Year-end FY27 debt expected at about INR230-240 crore (beginning FY28), rising to about INR300 crore by end of FY28 at a debt-to-equity ratio of about 1.2-1.3x.
Management expects working capital interest rates to fall as external credit ratings improve. Company expects to remain cash negative while growth stays around 70%.
capex_capacity: FPI manufacturing capacity utilisation is under 5-10%; management says FPI capacity is not a constraint.
Vacuum circuit breaker (VCB) billing expected in FY28; ring main unit (RMU) billing about 6 months after that. Management did not quantify volumes.
Backward integration under consideration for frequently bought items.

Bid pipeline: INR19,150 crore of tenders floated, INR6,600 crore selected for bidding, and INR1,260 crore at final evaluation (about INR800 crore power T&D, INR400 crore solar and storage, INR60 crore products).
BESS: about 20 MWh bid across EPC and RESCO models, funded by a mix of equity and debt.
Subsidiary Sugs Renewables to bid for and hold RESCO projects for recurring revenue.
demand_pricing: Bihar share of order book fell from about 82% (end-July) to about 55% now; company operates in 10-11 states, and new orders came from Punjab (RDSS, 15 months), Odisha (maintenance, 3 years) and Noida and Madhya Pradesh power utilities.
Strike-rate targets of 15-20% on qualified bids and 10-15% in new states.
Competition in FPI is mainly Siemens; VCB competitors include Siemens, ABB, Schneider; RMU has many players. Management cites customisation and new-model development as entry barriers.
Management said a transmission tender in Jammu and Kashmir where it was L1 was scrapped after a state policy change; it has since bid for Rajasthan and other transmission tenders.
Management expects growth in SCADA through project-specific joint ventures with software partners; technical collaboration talks are ongoing with completion targeted by H1 FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Margins fell to 14.1% in Q2 from 15.3% in Q1; what is the outlook for FY27 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said quarterly variation is due to the mix of high- and low-margin items in long-duration projects. It expects about 15% EBITDA margin for the full year.

qa_highlights.question: Debt was about INR160 crore versus a guided FY27 peak of about INR130 crore. What is the peak and the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said INR130 crore referred to fund-based debt only. Total debt will be kept at about 1.2-1.3x debt-to-equity, with year-end FY27 debt of about INR230-240 crore and about INR300 crore by end of FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Will operating cash flow turn positive by year-end?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is unlikely while growth stays around 70%, because growth consumes working capital. Cash positivity would need slower growth.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the INR190 crore receivables will be collected within 6 months?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the full INR190 crore is expected within 6 months. About INR200 crore was collected in H1, and about INR50 crore has been collected since quarter-end.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any plan for further equity dilution, and will unsecured promoter loans be used?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there are no plans for further equity dilution now. Promoters may extend unsecured loans if required, depending on the situation.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said there was no disqualification. In Haryana, a document (a revised bank certificate format) was submitted late, which led DHBVN to disqualify the bid.

Q4 FY26 revenue was about INR77 crore (up 6.8% on the stated basis) and Q4 PAT was INR5.5 crore, up 28% YoY. The SteriPort ISBM capacity expansion (6.6 crore to ~12 crore bottles per year) is not yet contributing and is guided to start by 20 June 2026. Price revision initiated about 20-25 days before the call with no customer resistance reported; for a 100 ml container the price increase is about 5.5-6% of selling price.

Management said power costs have fallen because of solar, and that polymer price pass-through typically lags, with price cuts on reversal expected to be partial (e.g., INR2 rise may reverse by INR0.75-1).

Indian IV fluid demand growing 8-10% YoY, ~INR185 crore market per management's estimate; two-port segment expected to grow 12-13%. SteriPort demand estimated at 20-25 crore bottles, rising to 75-80 crore bottles by 2030; management targets 20-25% share.

544502|2026-09.headline: Amanta Q2 FY27 revenue rose 17% YoY to INR83.1 crore with EBITDA margin of 21.6%; SteriPort Line 3 commissioned, taking capacity to about INR11.6 crore.

H1 FY27 revenue was INR151.9 crore (up 12%), EBITDA INR33 crore (up 8%) and PAT INR8.17 crore (up 12%). SteriPort Line 3 was commissioned in early September 2026, and management reiterated FY27 revenue of INR420-430 crore on an annualised run-rate basis. Polymer price volatility was absorbed in the quarter, with price increases of about 4-4.5% taken across products; the SVP expansion has slipped from Feb-Mar 2027 to a Q1 FY28 start.

rows.label: NPPA/NLEM distribution-margin reforms

544511|2026-03.headline: Karbonsteel crossed ₹300 crore revenue in FY26 with 10.86% EBITDA margin and ₹10.51 crore PAT, which management says normalises to ₹16.56 crore.
544511|2026-03.overview: FY26 revenue crossed ₹300 crore, but the company missed its ₹340 crore ideal level because of Khopoli exit, labour migration after the March LPG force majeure, and a ~₹40 crore shortfall from low-value labour jobs. Reported EBITDA margin was 10.86% and PAT ₹10.51 crore, including a ₹1.65 crore NCLT bad-debt write-off, ₹2.4 crore rent for the delayed Umargam expansion and Khopoli shifting costs. Order book was stated at about ₹350 crore as of May, up from near ₹200 crore. The Umargam expansion from 30,000 to 54,000 tonnes slipped from March to October 2026.

segments.name: Heavy and precision structural fabrication
segments.commentary: Core business; 70-80% of FY26 tonnage was complex custom work. Realisation about ₹100/kg for full fabrication versus ~₹30/kg for labour-only jobs; conversion margin ₹30-45/kg.

segments.name: PEB
segments.commentary: Revenue contribution fell to 0%; management says it will remain a small part as the company focuses on production rather than erection.

segments.name: Railways / bullet train
segments.commentary: Bullet train work (4,500 tonnes) was largely booked in the prior year; FY26 contribution nominal. Railway product development is at a very early stage.

guidance_outlook: Normalised EBITDA margin of 12-13% expected going forward; H2 FY26 normalised EBITDA cited at ~14%.
Production target ~40,000 tonnes annually at ~₹100/kg; FY26 utilisation guided at 80-90%.
PAT margin ~4-5% for FY26 and above 5% for FY27; aspiration of 7-8% later.
Finance costs guided at ~4% of turnover in FY26; FY27 targeted revenue ₹400 crore with order book of at least ₹500 crore.
Automation expected to add 15-20% efficiency; automation alone contributes ~1% EBITDA margin uplift by FY28.
Long-term aspiration of ₹800-1,000 crore revenue and 7,000-8,000 tonnes per month, requiring post-FY27 expansion funded by internal accruals and equity.
Labour expected to return by end-June 2026; ~₹150 crore order pipeline expected around September-October.
capex_capacity: Umargam expansion from 30,000 to 54,000 tonnes; completion revised to October (management cited 'October 2025' in places, which appears to be a transcription error given the call date of June 2026); initially targeted March.
₹21 crore work-in-progress on the expansion; another ₹10-15 crore capex planned next year, split between shed/building and automation.
Sheds 1 and 2 about 60% complete; a blasting machine under installation; automation planned in cutting, automatic beam welding and fit-up centre.
1 MW solar plant in two phases at ~₹3-3.5 crore, expected online October-November; expected to cut power bills by over 50%. Energy cost ~₹25-30 lakh per month.
Khopoli facility (2.5 acres, rented) exited, removing ~5,000-6,000 tonnes of capacity; team consolidated at Umargam (20+ acres).
demand_pricing: Order book grew from ~₹200 crore to ~₹350 crore as of May; management targets at least ₹500 crore of orders against a ₹400 crore revenue target.
90-95% of orders are repeat business; clients include ArcelorMittal, a major Maharashtra steel company, two large business houses and a power company.
MOU signed for 15,000 tonnes specifically for data centres.
Steel prices rose from ₹50-55/kg to ₹65-70/kg; price variation clauses pass through most steel cost, but conversion and transport fixed portions are being accepted gradually.
Management says PEB peers realise ₹115-120/kg but are EPC contractors; not comparable as Karbonsteel only manufactures.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the EBITDA margin rise only 1% by FY28 if one-offs disappear?
qa_highlights.answer: The 1% uplift is attributed to automation alone; other improvements are expected beyond that. Normalised margin expected at 12-13%.

qa_highlights.question: Expected production and utilisation after expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: About 40,000 tonnes annually at ~₹100/kg; FY26 utilisation 80-90%. Full 54,000-tonne capacity targeted for the following year.

qa_highlights.question: Solar capex and savings?
qa_highlights.answer: ₹3-3.5 crore for the solar plant, cutting bills by over 50%; eventually 100% solar power. Automation like laser cutting deferred until solar is in place due to power intensity.

qa_highlights.question: Will the labour issue be resolved?
qa_highlights.answer: Labour is returning; normalisation expected by end-June. April-May utilisation affected, Q1 utilisation about 80%.

qa_highlights.question: Why did H2 growth fall short of the 30% guided?
qa_highlights.answer: Khopoli exit cut 5,000-6,000 tonnes capacity; ~₹40 crore lower revenue from labour jobs; March LPG crisis delayed April-May completions.

qa_highlights.question: What is the ROE?
qa_highlights.answer: On ₹115 crore net worth and ~₹38 crore steady-state fixed assets, management expects ROE of 17-19%.

Labour availability: migration after the March LPG crisis; normalisation hoped for end-June.
Single LPG supplier force majeure exposed supply risk; management now says multiple gas sources are available.
Steel and input-cost volatility; fixed conversion and transport costs not fully passed through.
Large rental and depreciation costs until new capacity is commissioned; finance cost ~₹15 crore vs. stated ~4% of turnover guidance.
Margin targets (12-13% normalised EBITDA; 7-8% PAT aspiration) well above reported 10.86% and ~3.5% PAT.

544512|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue rose 106.5% YoY to INR725.6 crore and FY26 PAT rose 89% to INR115.5 crore, with working capital absorbing cash.
544512|2026-03.overview: Shringar reported Q4 FY26 revenue of INR725.6 crore (+106.5% YoY) with PAT of INR34 crore (+123.5%), and FY26 revenue of INR2,245.8 crore (+57.1%) and PAT of INR115.5 crore (+89%). Production capacity was raised from 2,500 kg to 4,000 kg in Q4, with FY26 utilisation at 87% on a blended 2,625 kg. The company entered bridal jewellery with Tanishq and Malabar Gold and Diamonds, and management reiterated about 30% value CAGR guidance for the next two to three years. Management acknowledged that working capital growth absorbed cash, leaving free cash flow negative, and said it expects to shift toward outright sales and organised clients within about two quarters.

segments.commentary: Job work revenue (labour fee) was INR28 crore in FY26 versus INR26 crore in FY25, per management.

FY27 mangalsutra sales expected to rise about 33-35% within the year.

demand_pricing: Client base of 1,333 customers across India and abroad; management plans to shift weight toward organised players such as Tata, Birla, Reliance, Malabar, Joyalukkas, Kalyan and PNG.
Malabar Gold and Diamonds accounted for 17% of revenue; Titan is a job-work client, so management said its value is not comparable.
Average inventory cost of gold about INR10,500 per gram on weighted-average basis; management cited gold prices up nearly 2x YoY (INR1,52,228 as of 15 April 2026).
Management said April and May 2026 were not particularly difficult, with corporate orders continuing without interruption.
Gold import duty raised from 6% to 15%; management said the increase is absorbed into domestic gold prices and has not caused distinct difficulties.
Management cited about 1 crore weddings in FY26 and weddings growing about 7-8% annually.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the working capital increase and the debt position?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said the debt-equity ratio is 0.27 and inventory churn is about five times; higher working capital was needed to support revenue growth.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the sharp rise in other expenses in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it mainly to notional hedging losses on MCX-hedged gold, plus about 10 exhibitions, machinery and setup costs for the new factory, and higher CSR spend.

qa_highlights.question: What is the job work versus outright sales split and margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Roughly 30% job work and 70% outright sales. Job work earned INR28 crore in FY26 as a labour fee. Management said converting job work to outright sales could lift revenue to INR70-80 crore on the same volume and triple profit on that volume.

qa_highlights.question: Why did working capital rise and was the cycle lengthening?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said outright sales require more capital, which is the trade-off for higher margin. It expects organised clients with fixed payment dates to ease cash-flow churn over time. It did not give debtor or inventory day figures.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 30% guidance value or volume growth, and does it include bridal?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 30% guidance is value growth and a minimum target. Bridal is not included in that guidance; it could push growth above 30% if bridal reaches parity with mangalsutra within three years.

qa_highlights.question: When will free cash flow turn positive?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it expects to convert a significant portion of operations to outright contracts within about two quarters, which should help move cash flow from negative to positive.

risks_watch: Negative free cash flow in Q4 FY26 driven by working capital; watch debtor and inventory days and whether cash flow turns positive in about two quarters.
Gold price volatility (near doubling YoY) and hedging losses; FY26 hedge ratio about 60%.
Shift from job work to outright sales raises capital needs and inventory risk, and depends on clients such as Tanishq converting contracts.
Q4 EBITDA margin fell 41 bps YoY despite higher gross margin, driven by hedging notional losses, exhibitions and CSR spend.
Bridal jewellery is at an early stage with a small contribution; the first lot was delivered in May 2026.
Management did not give a split of revenue by client beyond Malabar at 17%; client concentration remains unclear.

544512|2026-09.headline: Q2 FY27 revenue rose 54.8% YoY to INR 818.7 crore and PAT rose 73.2% to INR 39.5 crore, with PAT margin at 4.8%.

segments.name: Job work (gold-to-gold)
segments.commentary: Labour-only revenue with customer-supplied gold, which management said carries no inventory or gold price risk; Tanishq business is 100% job work. Management said job-work pricing is roughly 4.5% to 5% versus about 6% for outright.

segments.name: Bridal jewellery and mangalsutra
segments.commentary: Bridal began gradually in Q1 FY27 with 20 karigars, rising to 40; it reached about 10% of business by volume within six months. Management expects it to approach core-business levels in two to two-and-a-half years; mangalsutra category reportedly grows at 30% CAGR.

segments.name: Proposed wholly-owned subsidiary
segments.commentary: Board-approved for jewellery manufacturing, design, trading and distribution across gold, silver, diamond and semi-precious stones, aimed at B2C (online first) and lightweight products around INR 50,000; initial capital about INR 2 to 5 crore.

Subsidiary launch expected within two to three months of board approval.

demand_pricing: More than 90% of revenue comes from repeat orders, per management.
Corporate chain-store share about 51% of business, up from about 35% at IPO; customers include Titan/Tanishq, Malabar, Tata, Birla and Reliance (as named by management).
Management said sales volumes held up even as gold prices rose; with percentage-based making charges, higher gold prices lift revenue per unit.
Competition: unorganised jewellers said to be unable to keep pace with volume growth as corporates expand.

Core Services NTV accelerated for a fourth straight quarter to 29% growth (₹1,056 crore), and Services adjusted EBITDA margin improved to 6.9% of NTV. Consolidated loss was ₹(65) crore, almost entirely from InstaHelp, while the rest of the business delivered an adjusted EBITDA of ₹67 crore. Management retained its guidance of consolidated adjusted EBITDA breakeven by Q3 FY28 and ₹1,000 crore adjusted EBITDA by FY31, and framed InstaHelp as the main investment area.

segments.commentary: NTV ₹237 crore, up 76% YoY (58% ex-currency). UAE and Singapore both grew strongly; the Saudi Arabia JV is approaching profitability. UAE and Saudi JV are described as nearing or at profitability, and the company is not planning new international markets.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said the flywheel comes from densifying many micro-markets, which improves partner utilisation, lowers churn and supports trust. It cited UC Instant (30-60 minute service) as a new driver. It declined to give growth guidance, said the 29% was helped by a muted prior-year base from unseasonal rains and monsoon, and said the margin of 6.9% is in line with the 9-10% long-term target, which is not a trade-off against growth.

InstaHelp needs two years or more of investment, with capital allocation revisited at adjusted breakeven, hopefully within about 18 months.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said the goal is to reach the 9-10% range without rushing and without trading growth for margin. Priority one is growing fast, priority two is margin expansion. Once it reaches about 10%, it will decide whether to lift margins further or reinvest for faster growth.

qa_highlights.answer: The base case is INR 7,000-8,000 crore NTV and the bull case is INR 10,000-12,000 crore, with 3 orders per user per month. Management said the 3 major players have limited coverage to about 3.5-4 million households and that subsidised repeat orders dominate spend. It expects a low single-digit market share outcome and says it will not spend heavily on the category to drive share, while being opinionated about winning micro-markets.

Gross breakeven needs about INR 200 per hour, and an AOV of about INR 300 is needed for InstaHelp to break even. Management said breakeven could take a couple of years or up to 5 years, and it declined to give growth guidance beyond the 29%.

qa_highlights.question: Bank of America: how is AI being used and how much margin benefit is there?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 90-95% of the code is now written by AI, and that support, supply-side onboarding, quality audits and fraud detection are increasingly AI-led. Marketing and Finance/HR run AI end-to-end. It said the margin benefit has started to show but there is a long way to go.

Two-wheeler access for Beauty professionals is now a majority. It expects 3 transactions per month, not 30-40, for the 10-12 lakh household case. It expects private players to keep burning cash and believes it will be the eventual winner in the category.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said the user growth is largely from MAU, DAU and MTU growth and better conversion, and that marketing spend in Services was about INR 25 crore versus INR 24 crore a year ago. For Core, it said capacity is comfortable but is being scaled up, with all hands on deck, to match trainer and infrastructure growth. It said InstaHelp supply is also being expanded.

It said it is not building a durables company and will keep its focus on a small number of categories, mainly water purifiers and smart locks, with the aim of serving the top households in India.

544516|2026-03.headline: FY26 revenue rose 66% to Rs.319.6 Crores with PAT margin of 12.2%; FY27 guidance is Rs.500 Crores revenue at 12-13% PAT margin.
544516|2026-03.overview: FY26 revenue reached Rs.319.6 Crores (up 66% YoY), with H2 contributing Rs.229.1 Crores (up 114% YoY), and EBITDA of Rs.64.2 Crores at a 20.1% margin (EBITDA margin down from about 25% per analyst question). PAT was Rs.39.1 Crores (up 52%) at a 12.2% margin. Management said the Rs.1,000 Crores revenue milestone timeline may extend modestly because it declined to pursue low-margin re-tenders amid aluminium and stainless steel inflation. Management guided FY27 revenue of about Rs.500 Crores at 12-13% PAT margin, backed by an unexecuted order book of about Rs.469-487 Crores (figure varied in the call) and a Rs.1,200 Crores bid pipeline.

financial_highlights.change: +66% YoY vs Rs.192.4 Crores in FY25
+114% YoY vs Rs.107.3 Crores in H2 FY25
receivable days down 24 days; inventory days down 48 days

financial_highlights.metric: Net debt to equity at 31 Mar 2026

segments.name: Railways
segments.commentary: Largest growth driver; management says about 70% of the pipeline is railway, roughly Rs.900 Crores of the Rs.1,200 Crores bid pipeline, covering Atmanirbhar Bharat, Spark and Kavach coaches, Vande Bharat sleeper and Amrit Bharat turnkey contracts. Refurbishment is cited as a separate opportunity of about Rs.26,000 Crores sanctioned, with hoped-for orders of at least Rs.100 Crores this year.

segments.name: Metro
segments.commentary: About Rs.70 Crores of metro orders held, with another Rs.120 Crores expected within the Rs.1,200 Crores pipeline; Kolkata Metro turnkey contracts are named as a focus.

segments.name: Defence and aerospace
segments.commentary: Rs.29 Crores of current order book to execute this year, plus Rs.60-70 Crores expected from HAL tenders (mainly simulators, not AMCA airframe production). Proposed JV with Big Bang Boom Solutions to be incorporated before 15 June 2026; Airfloa committed about Rs.25 Crores, focused on autonomous drones and electronic warfare.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue target of approximately Rs.500 Crores with PAT margin of 12-13%; management said PAT would not fall below 12%.
Rs.1,000 Crores revenue milestone timeline may extend modestly; management also said it could be reached in FY28 or earlier if conditions allow.
Management said about 70-75% of the Rs.500 Crores FY27 target is covered by the existing order book, and 30-40% of the Rs.1,200 Crores pipeline is expected to execute in FY27.
R&D spend to rise to about 8-9% of sales this year from about 4% earlier; management later said R&D spend would be capitalised on the balance sheet.
Capex of Rs.30-40 Crores planned for FY27-28, including about Rs.30-35 Crores for a 14-acre facility with 50,000 to 1 lakh sq ft of initial shed space, expanding to 3-4 lakh sq ft.
Debt funding of about Rs.120 Crores at 8.25% from two banks: Rs.60 Crores sanctioned, the other Rs.60 Crores expected by end June 2026. No equity raise planned this year.
capex_capacity: Current capacity utilisation is about 90% of existing facility; two-shift operations in use since around December 2025.
New 14-acre facility planned: initial 50,000 to 1 lakh sq ft, later extending to 3-4 lakh sq ft; land already acquired and term loan discussions with bankers under way.

Machinery purchases, mostly from China, delayed because Chinese OEMs require an end-user certificate from the Government of India; management expected clarity in June 2026 and may switch to different machinery for lightweight rail interiors.
Plans to consolidate seven units into about two, reducing rent of roughly Rs.20-25 lakh per month.
Channel partner model in place to execute zonal railway contracts without building facilities in each region.
demand_pricing: Unexecuted order book about Rs.469-487 Crores (figure cited differently in different answers): Rs.415-420 Crores government and Rs.50-55 Crores non-government.
Bid pipeline about Rs.1,200 Crores with historical bid-win ratio of about 20-25%.

Raw material inflation: aluminium up more than 80% and stainless steel up 60-65% YoY; price variation clauses cover only about 50-60% of the increase, and accessories (30-35% of assembly cost) are not covered.
Competitors named: Kineco, Hindustan Fiberglass Works, DTL Ancillaries, Vibgyor, Universal Engineers; seating competitors Tata (with Fainsa), a Korean firm and firms from Mumbai and Bengaluru.

qa_highlights.question: How will working capital be funded and when will operating cash flow turn positive?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects about Rs.100-110 Crores of receivables collected by June end; receivable and working capital cycles targeted at 60-70 days from 90-95 days within 3-4 months. Debt of Rs.120 Crores is being raised.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the Rs.500 Crores FY27 target is covered by orders?
qa_highlights.answer: About 70-75% is covered by the existing order book, and 30-40% of the Rs.1,200 Crores pipeline is expected to execute in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Margin pressure and its causes in H2 FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: Aluminium and stainless steel inflation hit margins. Management said price variation covers only about 50-60% of losses, and it used advances, LCs and BGs to block vendor prices, limiting losses to 20-25% of the uncovered amount.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of added debt interest and R&D on the 12-13% PAT target?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said PAT would stay at or above 12%, citing higher-margin bids and that R&D spend would be deployed only when expected returns are met.

qa_highlights.question: Can FY28 revenue reach Rs.1,000 Crores and PAT Rs.150 Crores?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Rs.1,000 Crores could be reached even this year if all goes well and that FY28 could exceed Rs.1,000 Crores, without firm numbers.

qa_highlights.question: Does the Rs.500 Crores target hold given 90% utilisation and machinery delays?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said machinery delays would not affect FY27 turnover; two-shift operation and channel partners could add Rs.400-450 Crores from the Rs.320 Crores base.

risks_watch: Working capital: trade receivables of Rs.214 Crores at year-end; collection of about 70% expected by June, and cash conversion still negative.
Debt servicing: about Rs.120 Crores new debt at 8.25% adds interest cost of roughly Rs.10 Crores per year, per the analyst's calculation.
Raw material and commodity inflation, with price variation clauses covering only part of the increase.
Dependence on lumpy Indian Railways orders and back-loaded execution in H2.
Possible equity raise in FY28, which management did not rule out.
Defence revenue timing: management said defence products need 6-12 months of trials, and the Big Bang Boom JV is expected to be incorporated before 15 June 2026.
Inconsistent figures on order book (Rs.469 Crores vs Rs.486.9 Crores) and on EBITDA margin, which the analyst described as falling from 25% to 20%.
544516|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on FY27 execution and margins, but evasive on timing for the Rs.1,000 Crores milestone and on defence revenue, which management described as a long-cycle, first-time bid area. Several answers were repetitive or unclear, and management did not give firm numbers for the JV or the new facility.
key_quotes: Looking ahead, we are targeting a revenue of approximately Rs.500 Crores in FY 2027 while maintaining PAT margin in the range between 12% to 13%.
So I do not think that we can reduce our overall PAT level less than 12% for sure.
The bidding of Rs.1200 Crores is predominantly on the Indian railway sector.

rows.why: Management may switch machinery for lightweight rail interiors and the defence JV (autonomous drones and electronic warfare, Airfloa committed about Rs.25 Crores) is to be incorporated before 15 June 2026, but no product launch dates or revenue were given.

rows.label: Receivables collection and cycle reduction
rows.why: Management expects Rs.100-110 Crores of receivables collected by June end and a cycle cut from 90-95 days to 60-70 days, against Rs.214 Crores of receivables at 31 March 2026.

rows.label: Equity raise in FY28
rows.why: Management did not rule out an equity raise in FY28, though none is planned this year, and net debt to equity is 0.2 times after the Rs.120 Crores debt plan.

tone.note: Management was confident on FY27 execution (70-75% order cover) and the 12-13% PAT margin, but evasive on the Rs.1,000 Crores timeline and on defence revenue; analysts pressed on the EBITDA margin fall from about 25% to 20%, debt interest cost, and inconsistent order book figures.

544516|2026-09.headline: Airfloa H1 FY26 net profit rose 24% YoY to INR12.09 crore on INR90.98 crore total income; order book crossed INR455 crore.
544516|2026-09.overview: Management reported H1 FY26 total income of INR90.98 crore (up nearly 7% YoY), EBITDA of INR22.46 crore and net profit of INR12.09 crore (up 24% YoY), its first results call after the BSE SME listing in September 2025. Active order book was stated at over INR455 crore after a recent INR1,013 crore order win in a single week from ICF and MCF. Management guided to FY26 turnover of over INR300 crore and FY27 of at least INR550 crore, with defence (drones, anti-drone, laser systems via a JV with Big Bang Boom Solutions) as a stated growth driver. Capacity is being expanded through a 14-acre plant purchase, with a term loan under discussion.

financial_highlights.metric: Net profit margin (as referenced by analyst)

financial_highlights.change: crossed after recent wins; includes about INR65 crore defence

segments.name: Railways (govt and non-govt)
segments.commentary: Management put railway orders at about INR390-405 crore of the book, 75-80% from Indian Railways and 20% from non-government customers. Key programmes cited include Vande Bharat, LHB, Amrit Bharat and metro work.

segments.name: Defence and aerospace
segments.commentary: Defence order book about INR65 crore. Management expects INR100-120 crore of defence revenue in FY27 from a new INR200-250 crore order intake. Products cited: tether drone, loitering drone, anti-drone laser systems, radar, unmanned land systems, MBT hulls and aerospace simulators. Entered defence in 2020.

guidance_outlook: FY26 turnover guided at over INR300 crore; management said up to INR310 crore is committed, with 300-350 crore possible.
FY27 revenue guided at a minimum of INR550 crore, with INR500 crore+ cited on paper; management called 550 the bare minimum.
Q3 FY26 revenue indicated at INR70-75 crore and Q4 at about INR120 crore; Q4 typically 40-45% of annual turnover.
Management said defence could reach about 50% of revenue within two years, and that margins should improve as defence scales.
Management said the order book could reach about INR1,000 crore by March 2026 and that a further INR30 crore of orders was expected in the near term.
capex_capacity: Capacity utilisation about 85% on each of two shifts after moving from single shift in September 2025.
A 14-acre plant is being bought; a first facility of 50,000 sq ft is targeted by end-December 2026, scaling to about 1 lakh sq ft; land settlement expected by January 2026.
Planned new facility capex INR20-30 crore to start; management expects asset turnover of about 4x the investment.
Plan to set up a facility near MCF and RCF to cut transport costs; term loan talks with banks under way.
Defence capex of INR100-150 crore over 1-1.5 years; INR6-7 crore already invested in prototyping, with INR25-30 crore planned over the next 6-7 months.
Capex deviation: machine model changed with vendor PONC, saving about INR22 lakh.
demand_pricing: Management said it takes only contracts that meet its margin threshold; PAT margin of about 12% cited by an analyst, with management aiming to improve margins through defence mix.
Door systems (Vande Bharat focus) and vacuum toilet systems named as near-term products; orders expected to be announced in the following weeks.
Six products in development across railways (security, surveillance, fire suppression, doors, vacuum toilets); two have development orders.
Kavach-type integrated train security system to be exhibited next financial year; approval needs RDSO/Railway Board trials of 9-12 months.
Certifications cited: about 52 defence labs (CVRDE, ARDE, DRDO labs), STANAG certificate, and AI (aerospace) certification enabling supply to HAL and ADA.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the INR455 crore book is rail versus defence, and what is the execution timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Defence is about INR65 crore; the rest is rail, both government and non-government. INR200-250 crore is to execute within this year, running to December of next year.

qa_highlights.question: Are the 12% PAT margins sustainable, and is there scope for improvement?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it does not take contracts below its margin threshold and is trying to lift margins, helped by defence traction; no numerical margin target was given.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Big Bang Boom JV and how much is being invested?
qa_highlights.answer: A JV with Airfloa holding a majority stake, focused on high-power laser anti-drone systems (2,000-5,000 m range) and an autonomous drone programme. Details were deferred to a later presentation, citing compliance constraints.

qa_highlights.question: What capacity and capex are needed to deliver FY27 revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Current shift expansion gives about INR300 crore; the new facility (INR20-30 crore capex, funded by term loan) is expected to take revenue to INR500 crore+ from January 2027 onward.

qa_highlights.question: What is the defence capex need and funding plan?
qa_highlights.answer: INR100-150 crore over 1-1.5 years for drone and anti-drone systems, to be recycled and supplemented by a separate fundraise later. Around 25-30% is planned by March 2026.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the IPO proceeds are unutilised?
qa_highlights.answer: About 18% of IPO proceeds remain unutilised; the deviation relates to a machine model change with the same vendor.

risks_watch: Execution risk: FY26 target of INR300 crore+ needs about INR200 crore in H2 (about INR91 crore delivered in H1), with capacity at about 85% on double shift.
Capacity constraint until the new 50,000 sq ft facility (targeted end-December 2026); FY27 INR550 crore guidance depends on it.
Defence scale-up depends on tenders, trials and certifications; management said several products are awaiting trials, and the JV's contribution is not yet quantified.
Working capital and funding: term loan not yet sanctioned; another equity fundraise is planned in about 1.5 years.
Disclosure risk: management deferred several details (the six products, the Big Bang Boom JV, door-system empanelment) to later announcements.
Several figures varied across answers (for example, railway book INR390 vs 405 crore, and the FY27 defence figure), so the numbers need confirmation against filings.
